title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’ve been using the Legion Pro i7 (RTX + Intel i7 configuration) for a few weeks, playing a variety of modern AAA and multiplayer games — and overall, I’m impressed. Here’s the full breakdown from a gamer’s point of view:
What I really like

Performance: This thing is a powerhouse. It handles demanding titles (think open-world, high-settings) without breaking a sweat. When you crank up settings or use high refresh rates, the i7 + RTX combo keeps fps stable and smooth — no noticeable lag even in hectic firefights or big open-world scenes.

Display: The screen is . Crisp visuals, vibrant colors, and smooth frame delivery make everything look clean — from fast-paced shooters to cinematic story-games. As a gamer who cares about immersion, that matters a lot.

Versatility: It doesn’t feel like a gaming-only machine. I’ve done some lighter tasks, streaming, and even editing-type work (video/audio) and the system handles it like a champ. Perfect if you want one machine for both gaming and “real life.”

Build & convenience: Keyboard and overall build feel sturdy and premium. Ports, connectivity and cooling seem well-balanced — you can plug in accessories, external drives or headsets without fuss; fans don’t get unbearably loud unless under heavy load.

What you should know / What could be better

Battery life: Don’t expect long unplugged sessions. Like most powerful gaming laptops, the battery drains fast if you actually game on battery power. For anything heavy (games, rendering), you’ll want to be plugged in.

Portability vs performance tradeoff: It’s not a super-light laptop. If you move the machine around a lot (school, cafés, trips) you’ll feel the weight. It’s better suited as a “desktop replacement” rather than a daily-carry laptop.

Power draw and heat (if pushed hard): With high settings and long sessions, expect the fans to come alive and the machine to get warm. It’s manageable, but noticeable — plan accordingly if you game on your lap or in hot environments

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Only been using for one week, but the experience so far has been great. Here's a few things I care about:

Laptop Build (5/5). Keyboard is snappy and feels good to type or game on. Track pad is very precise and allows me to read, zoom-in, and traverse webpages very easily. Laptop has some good weight to it and won't move around on a slick surface. Screen has a robust pivot and will move exactly where you want it to and stay there. USBs are as advertised, but there is a physical switch to turn camera off which is really nice. All ports are on the left and right, and the power plug is not a circular power cord, rather a rectangular one which this laptop deserves. It's a good, solid connection, not going to slip out.

Heat Tolerance (5/5). So far, I have had no problem running games on ultra settings. Neither the power brick nor the laptop itself has gotten too hot, just warm. The heat is dissipated behind the screen, pointed away, which is a great location for it. Noise level for maintaining good temperature is great, better than my prior laptop.

Screen/Color Quality (5/5). The screen is beautiful and definitely bright enough. There is built-in color correction that is a game changer, and compared to previous laptops it is not even close. It's great to read or play games on, and there's lots of options.

Gaming Quality (4.5/5). When just playing a game alone, it does great. I have played games on Ultra quality and the FPS doesn't drop below 240 Hz, which is the max refresh rate of the screen. There are certainly more powerful systems out there, but this one is excellent for a laptop. I sometimes will have many Youtube videos open, a discord call, etc., and it still keeps this performance. However, the graphics cards struggles slightly when in the GPU optimized for gaming. Animated GIFs in discord will sometimes glitch out when using this GPU. Additionally, when closing out a game, there is a lag spike that can takes a few seconds, which is the system switching out GPUs. These are minor things, but expect some annoyances. Outside of these instances, it has been perfect.

Operating System and Software (3/5). The systems comes packaged with a bunch of bloatware, and Windows 11 shoves ads down your throat at every opportunity. However, I was able to uninstall all bloatware, and through a few hours of searching the internet, I was able to suppress all of Windows 11's ads. I was also able to remove Copilot, which is a must. I immediately went to install a new browser (Edge is still terrible), but the system seemed to keep on setting my default BACK to edge. It took 4 or 5 tries for it to stick. Clearly, MS doesn't want you making this change. The same is for the default search engine, which kept on going back to the default, when I wanted DuckDuckGO. I was also able to uninstall McAfee (also terrible) and put on Malwarebytes. It comes with a subscription, but you couldn't pay me to that software. Overall this is pretty standard procedure for any new Windows machine, but it stank a little more this time.

Battery Performance (2/5). When the system is on battery, don't expect to play games. For reference, Bloons TD6 is too much, and it switches between normal speed and chugging along like a device from 5 generations ago. It clearly is not able to take it, nor optimized for it. You can do other things like watch videos or whatever for maybe a few hours. I highly recommend keeping this thing plugged in 100% of the time.

Given that all the bloatware and Windows 11 annoyances were able to be fixed, and that battery performance isn't much of a factor for me, I still give this laptop a 5/5. It's a fantastic choice overall. It really feels like a medium performance desktop crammed into a laptop.

Windows S Mode and McAfee are glitchy performance killers and restrictive applications. Switching out of Win 11 S mode should be a straight forward process but it just does not work as it should, along with McAfee installed, whether you want it or not. McAfee acts like a worm virus, intrusively imbedding itself deep into system architecture instead of being a gate keeper like other anti-virus apps. Windows S Mode dose not allow you to install and run any app that is not Microsoft verified and found on the Microsoft Store. In S Mode, you cannot install and run any browser other than MS Edge or Bing. There is an app within the MS Store to switch out of S mode but it will not work because, I suspect, of the bloated software that launches when you first turn on and set up this laptop. So...I could not install Quicken, Google Chrome, Open Office and other apps not endorsed by Microsoft! I spent hours searching for how to turn it off.
To save you the time, here is the info:
Turning off S Mode is permanent. Once you turn it off, you can't turn it back on.
To turn off S Mode, go to Settings > System > Activation. Under "Switch to Windows 11 Pro," click Go to the Store, then click "Get."
If you don't have a Microsoft Account, the only way to get rid of S mode is to disable Secure Boot in the UEFI (BIOS).

I purchased this laptop in January, and by March, it was already showing major issues. The performance declined rapidly — it became unbearably slow, frequently crashed, and often struggled to open even basic programs or web pages. Using it has been incredibly frustrating.

Unfortunately, I didn’t dig deep enough into reviews before buying and was misled by overly positive ones. After running into these problems, I did more research and discovered that this model is widely known for poor performance and reliability.

I called HP and they told me that Amazon or 3rd party sellers modify the laptop from the original 4 GB RAM to 16 GB. This laptop is not compatible with 16 GB, and that's why this is a piece of garbage.

HP also informed me that there are many customers who are experiencing the same problem, but because the laptop was modified by a third party, they can’t honor the warranty or provide technical support for the device in its current configuration.

I strongly recommend avoiding this laptop. Take the time to research alternatives (and maybe invest a bit more) to get something reliable. This one simply isn’t worth the frustration.

DO NOT BUY THIS LAPTOP. I depend on customer reviews so I carefully researched laptops before ordering. I had this laptop for one week and noticed that the power cord box got very hot. Also, the bottom of the laptop would get unusually warm. One day I left the charger plugged in with the laptop closed. When I opened it, the power would not come on. I unplugged it, kept trying and it eventually came on once cool. I called HP for support and after telling them I had 16 GB RAM, they looked at the upgrades made by the seller and VOIDED MY WARRANTY! Here's the quote from the transcript: "The computer was originally manufactured with hardware that matched the requirement of this computer, however when I see your computer specifications now, it looks like it has been upgraded by seller beyond its holding capacity and unfortunately this has voided the manufacturing warranty on this computer and due to that we will not be able to provide any support from our end. There is a good chance that the problem that you are facing now could be possible because of these changes made." So now I have to wipe the computer and return it with the prepaid label they are sending. Amazon is refunding the extra protection policy I purchased. In addition, HP stated that I had 336 days left on my warranty even though I only had the computer for 7 days. Evidently, the seller must purchase them to upgrade and then resells them - creating the gap in the time expired from warranty duration. One more tip, HP agent said I could get a copy of the transcript after I close the chat... but don't close it yet, there's another button to push for transcript first before closing the chat. This has been a totally frustrating experience and the seller should not upgrade unless more RAM is purchased. BUYER BEWARE!
UPDATE: Returned laptop and got a notice about the refund and was glad until I saw the amount was over $130 LESS than what I paid. After contacting Amazon, they said the seller charged a restocking fee! I explained the entire situation and they reached out to the seller. The seller's reply: "In accordance with Amazon policies, we typically charge a restocking fee for used items or those damaged by customers. After reviewing your return reason, we have decided to trust your explanation and issue a full refund." The refund is labeled "Goodwill Refund". It is still about $8. short. I'm tired of fighting this battle. Where is the accountability for creating this problem? I have since purchased a new laptop through Microcenter and have purchased their Priority Plus plan which is worth its weight in gold. I can call up at anytime and they will remotely address any issues on my laptop.

text:
I wish I would have done more research before I bought a computer but alas, like all I do in life, I went at it fast, furious and hoping for the best. However, that was not what I got. Because I am in no way happy about this laptop.

While I love the manufacturer, HP, I did not like the software that came with this laptop- Microsoft. Because compared to Chrome, it goes slower and sometimes takes forever to open up, freezes.

I had a HP Chrome notebook before this purchase and when the Chrome notebook passed the two year mark it started to overheat underneath and stall. So, my baby would need a break and that was the time that I purchased this HP. During the first week with the new HP I found myself going back to my old baby, because the new one would freeze, stall- it wasn’t easy to operate.
I don't know whether it is the inside of this particular version of notebook/ laptop or the operating system but the only difference between the two is that one opens to Chrome and the other, Microsoft.

Even using Microsoft Word now, over the Google Docs was frustrating because Word has too much going on in their toolbar now for me to figure out. Twenty years ago, Word was simpler, easier and to figure out many things, you didn't go to the toolbar but the drop downs (which I loved). Now, when I look at the tool bar I can’t even figure out where cut and paste is. The only thing I like about Microsoft over Word is that Word gives me suggestions to correct mistakes in reviews, whereas Chrome never does. But, it all ends there and that is really nothing I absolutely need.

Really, I don't recommend this laptop at all. I don't know if I got a lemon- just one that didn't work right from the beginning or if they are all like this. But I am not happy with the purchase- Microsoft Word doesn't even input all my google mail, after I requested it. I missed so many emails- for like a week until I just started logging into my google email online. And that I can't go on to Google Play at all- I don't think. I have no idea what Microsoft offers app wise, but I don't want to find out.

However, I liked that this laptop might work with my beat pad but then I tried to download the software, which was for Microsoft and nothing went right. All I can say is that if you're getting a great deal on one and just need something to type on, for school, something simple, you can get this one. But if there is any other option that seems good, take it. Because the one thing that I needed to work, the beat pad software, has been too complicated to figure out, if I even can.

I would recommend others to look a little harder, do research, know what you want and make sure what laptop or notebook your purchase has. Do not be fast and furious with a bigger purchase like this- because you’ll only be furious with your own attitude over the whole thing. But at least I learned a lesson and know, in the future, what to do and look for.

Update 11/19- This is the second (or third) month in which I have had this laptop- and I have not been using it much because I found a used laptop, I liked better- and works better. So even though I barely have used this one, when I opened it today- I got an alet that it doesnt this battery made need replaced because it does not have enough storage capacity (within the battery). And as I type this review, it took me forever to get on the Internet and sometimes the words come out slow, sometimes faster- this computer, right in the beginning, is a nightmare to use and now- to have to replace a battery??

I have never gotten any kind of alert- even after years of hard use of a Chrome labtop. This feels like a complete waste of money and I am lowering my rating from two stars to one. I don't want anyone to get "duped" into spending two hundred dollars for something that performs terribly... And I doubt a new battery is inexpensive- how can at three months of barely using this- can I open it up and get a computer message that the battery has low storage space? It would have been nice if I was told this labtop had little storage- before I bought it. And, like I previously stated- I had barely used this after the first month when I aquired a used labtop that was better (because this one was frustrating). So much for bying new- I thought I would get a better product and I feel as if what I spent was now a complete waste!!

Windows S Mode and McAfee are glitchy performance killers and restrictive applications. Switching out of Win 11 S mode should be a straight forward process but it just does not work as it should, along with McAfee installed, whether you want it or not. McAfee acts like a worm virus, intrusively imbedding itself deep into system architecture instead of being a gate keeper like other anti-virus apps. Windows S Mode dose not allow you to install and run any app that is not Microsoft verified and found on the Microsoft Store. In S Mode, you cannot install and run any browser other than MS Edge or Bing. There is an app within the MS Store to switch out of S mode but it will not work because, I suspect, of the bloated software that launches when you first turn on and set up this laptop. Switching out of S Mode is permanent. All the advise and direction I found to get this switch to work had failed. Lots of frustrated people out there with the same issue. I finally got MS Support on the phone and they told me this is a very common problem with this product and the only way to resolve it was to reset the PC. A total reset, wiping the OS and all files you may have added. No big deal as this is a new PC and I did not transfer anything from my old PC. After the PC was reset, I was able to switch out of S mode so that I now have Win 11 Home instead of Win 11S Home. At the same time, a McAfee install popup was automatically prompted so I could select Do Not Install. This was all a bit of a pain but other than that, this laptop is not so bad. The display colors are not as vibrant as I hoped but with a resolution of only 1365 x 768, I should have expected that. However, the graphics display very well on a connected higher resolution monitor and it handles steaming video from Amazon Prime Video beautifully. I hope this information can help someone avoid the frustration of dealing with what was intentionally sold as a very restrictive operating environment. Getting rid of S Mode and McAfee gives you back unrestricted use of your laptop.

One more annoying detail is that, by default, this operating environment is set to save everything to the MS cloud. The default storage of Document, Downloads, Pictures, etcetera, are all MS cloud folders which is where every file is stored unless you go through a few more clicks to store the files on your local laptop drive. By default, initially you cannot even boot up this laptop without entering your MS PIN to log onto your laptop, and thereby logging into your MS account at the same time. I found this a bit presumptuous that MS thought this was a good idea. Perhaps good for their own marketing efforts though, as some bot scans your files for things you do in order to tailor marketing ad pushes to you personally, but I digress. If you do not want Big Brother holding on to all your personal, professional, private, or other data, then you need to go in to system settings and turn off the MS log in PIN. Doing so allows you to boot up your laptop to your local drive account only. You can always log in and log out of your MS account if and when you choose at any time. Of course, you can even turn off your own laptop log in password so it just simply turns on. without a password. Your choice, as it should be.

text:
I was searching for a Plex Media server upgrade to my aging and stuck-on-Windows-10 HP EliteBook, and my reseach brought me to this listing. This is the first time I've ever bought a PC refurbished, and also my first experience with SFF PCs like this one originally designed for business/commercial use (all my other PCs were consumer oriented). As with most refurbished products, you never really know what will happen and you just gotta trust that the company did their due diligence with it before selling it to you.

UNBOXING: Out of the box, the packaging is very generous and was basically more than enough to pad all the crucial components. It came in the super thick bubble wrap that made it impossible to rattle around in the box. The mouse and keyboard came in a separated box, and other accessories were in separate bags.

CONDITION: I don't know if I got lucky or maybe this company really does refurb items properly, but my unit was pretty much immaculate inside and out. No visible scratches or scuffs on the outside, and the inside was shockingly dust-free. The ports all looked perfect (usually they would get mangled or scuffed up from constant use), and the AC power adapter was equally as immaculate. Either way, I'm more than satisfied

BOOTING UP: Setting it up was was dead simple. Turning it on brings you to the "HP Secure Boot" screen and you load straight into the Windows 11 setup screen. It was definitely a good taste of the performance of this PC because it just blazed through the setup screens.

IN USE: The clean Windows 11 installation was definitely true, because there was basically ZERO bloatware pre-installed. After all the updates that it installed shortly after setup, getting everything up and ready for my Plex server use was incredibly fast and simple. The i5-8500T (which I specifically looked for in my research since this gen of CPU had the improved Intel Quick Sync), 16GB of RAM and the 256GB SSD are such a big step up.

Even after opening up various Chrome tabs, NAS software, and transcoding my media library fails to cause this system to slow down or run into any performance issue. The fan does spool up and the PC gets a bit warm, but unless you have this PC right near your face or you have it placed on your hands, you won't really notice it running.

ACCESSORIES: they were generous to include the mouse and keyboard, WIFI + BT dongle, and DisplayPort dongle in the package. While they all worked pretty well, I only ended up using the DisplayPort dongle and the WIFI + BT dongle ONLY for the BT. My own mouse and keyboard were better, and Ethernet will ALWAYS trump WIFI especially for Plex use.

The WIFI + BT is half-hit half-miss. The BT part works pretty well with no disconnects experienced, but the Realtek chip for WIFI using the archaic 802.11n standard; my Wifi speeds were limited to 140-160mpbs up/down For comparison, my gigabit Ethernet basically hit 980mpbs up/down. If you have an Ethernet connection available, I STRONGLY suggest you use it with this PC.

VERDICT: This PC and, by extension, this refurb company have definitely set the bar high because I am very happy with this PC. While long terms reliable is still up in the air, the fact that this SFF PC with an 8th gen CPU was basically in immaculate condition and runs like a $1000+ machine is impressive. I'll update my review if I run into any issues down the line, but for now, solid 10/10

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
It's really amazing what gets packed into a small, light package these days, often for not a lot of money. This laptop is a good example. The AMD Ryzen 7 processor is no slouch, providing quick response for multiple apps. The Radeon graphics look good on the 15.6-inch 1920x1080 (full HD) LCD, and when you connect it to an external monitor via HDMI it really looks good. Half a terabyte of NVMe M.2 storage means you have plenty of room for all of your stuff. The 3 USB 3.2 ports means you can connect to just about anything -- more external storage, printers and other devices -- at super fast speeds. If there is any limitation with this laptop, it's the 8GB of memory. Honestly, it's probably more than enough, but I would have liked the option to upgrade. It also includes Gigabit ethernet, but really for a laptop, WiFi makes more sense. Throughout the setup and "personalization" (which included downloading multip apps) I didn't see any need to connect it to ethernet, because the WiFi was plently fast enough. For the price, this is a nice little machine. It's thinner and lighter than my old HP laptop (which isn't that much older) so it will definitely replace that.

I have to be honest: I am not a fan of Windows. My standard desktop is Linux and I got this to use when I need to use Windows (because not everything I need runs on Windows.) That's not the subject of this review, but I have to say that HP's "extras" do not really add to the Windows experience (which *is* part of the review.) Between HP and Microsoft, I feel that there is too much intrusion into my workspace that I could do without. It seems like both of them want to make sure they get as much money out of me as they can, with Microsoft making it hard to use the computer without logging in to Microsoft (as opposed to logging in to Windows) and both of them wanting me to subscribe -- with a fee after a "free" trial -- to the extra software and services they put on this PC. All of that is avoidable, but requires some effort. If you don't mind getting MS Office on a "free trial" basis that you will ultimately have to pay for, and the assortment of software HP adds on (with the same deal, free trial, pay later) that's fine. But if you don't need that there should be an easier way to opt out and never get nagged about it again.

That all may seem a bit off-topic for a review about this particular laptop, but it's part of what I got when I got this laptop, so I feel like it should be part of the review. I appreciate that HP put together what really is a nice little laptop, but I feel that the experience of using it -- part of what I am reviewing -- needs to be part of the review. I haven't taken off any stars, and I'd still recommend this laptop to someone in the market, because HP isn't unique it cramming "bloatware" onto their system, and Microsoft's windows offerings are going to be the same regardless of the vendor providing the hardware.

So comparing apples to, erm, apples, this is a good laptop, you won't go wrong buying it, and it will do at least as much, with about the same amount of effort, as any other. Plus you get good built quality is a light package with good battery life and stellar performance right out of the box. If you need a laptop, this would be a good choice.

...media consumption device due to the screen angle. The screen must be at just the right angle to get the whole screen visible otherwise it darkens at the edges. Also, my previous laptop had a 1920x1080 screen. This screen is a definite downgrade in sharpness.

I don't use Windows anymore, so I immediately replaced the SSD with a new one and installed Linux Mint on it. It took a while, but I got Mint configured to where I'm happy with it.

The touchscreen works under Linux Mint, but I prefer it to be off, so it's turned off completely. Linux has a way of disabling (or re-enabling if desired) the touchscreen.

The touchpad is too sensitive. If you press it just a little too hard, while navigating the screen, the cursor wants to select everything that it contacts. It's a pain in the butt to get it out of that mode, so I use a USB mouse most of the time, instead, which is fine for work, but not so good if you want to use the device on your lap. Also, I find that a 17-inch laptop too large for my tastes while using it on my lap.

Processing power is great. The processor shows up having 12 cores. It's speedy enough to handle multiple virtual machines (VMs) running at the same time (4 running concurrently). With several VMs running at the same time, I've come nowhere close in peaking out the 64 GB of RAM.

There is no AI in this version of Linux Mint and I'm completely fine with that. In fact I relish not having any built-in spyware from Microsoft.

Power consumption is nowhere near what my previous laptop could do. The battery will only last about 2.5 to 3 hours depending on the workload even with "power saver" mode engaged. My LG laptop could go 4.5 to 5 hours under daily workloads. Speaking of power, there is no charging through the USB C port. That would've been another deal-breaker if I'd had known about it before purchasing this device.

Final words: Your Mileage May Vary (YMMV). It will be highly dependent on your needs. Is it worth the price tag? In my opinion, no. I wouldn't buy it again knowing what I know now, but it is what it is and I needed a replacement immediately, but didn't want to spend much more than a grand on it.

After using this HP 15.6" touchscreen laptop for several weeks, I’ve been consistently impressed by how well it handles everyday tasks. The standout feature is the combination of a modest CPU with a generous 32GB of RAM and a fast 1TB SSD, resulting in much smoother performance than expected from a Core i3 system.

The i3-1115G4’s strong single-core performance allows quick boot times, fast app launches, and responsive system navigation. The 32GB RAM is a major advantage, enabling seamless multitasking with numerous browser tabs, office applications, and streaming content open simultaneously.

The 1TB SSD offers excellent speed for file transfers and significantly improves overall responsiveness. With this much storage, it's easy to keep large photo libraries, documents, and multiple applications installed without worrying about space.

The touchscreen is responsive and intuitive, making browsing and media viewing more natural. While the display is HD rather than Full HD, the colors are pleasant, and brightness is adequate for indoor use.

The keyboard provides a soft, comfortable typing experience suitable for long sessions. The touchpad is accurate and reliable, with smooth gesture support.

Key strengths:

-Fast multitasking performance thanks to 32GB RAM
-Quick boot and file operations due to the 1TB SSD
-Responsive touchscreen enhances everyday use
-Low fan noise, suitable for meetings and quiet environments
-Great overall value for students, remote workers, and general home use

The built-in speakers are serviceable for video calls and casual media consumption but lack depth for music playback. Additionally, the HD display may feel less sharp for users accustomed to Full HD or higher.

Despite these minor limitations, the laptop’s performance, storage capacity, and usability far exceed expectations for its price range.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
I bought this laptop as a spec upgrade to my old 2021 HP laptop, and this one is better in every aspect!
I got this laptop for general use and for gaming. Yes, this laptop's processor is so powerful with the Ryzen AI 7 350 chipset. It outperforms the steam deck and Asus ROG Ally X. In fact, I'm selling my steam deck so I can stick to using this laptop instead. I never used my steam deck and I'm on my laptop every day. So, having a two-in-one device is much better. I decided not to get a gaming laptop because I wanted a longer lasting battery while web browsing and this laptop excels at that! It lasts significantly longer than my old laptop and the temps range from 32 - 45 C for general use. Using energy saver at all times also greatly extends the battery life further.

About the other review regarding the screen color quality, it certainly holds true. The colors are terrible on this laptop by default. It's a difference compared to my old HP laptop, looking like it has a yellow tint as if night light mode is enabled. However, this can be fixed using Window's color calibration tool. Go through the calibration program until you get to the part where you adjust the three RGB color balancing. I set blue to about 90%, green to 75%, and red to 65%. With these changes, the screen colors look normal without the yellow tint. The screen was my main worry and now I can enjoy the laptop fully.

The Pros:
- The ips display is perfect, you can view the screen from any angle without glare. This is not an OLED screen though so don't get it mixed up like me.
- The lit-up keyboard can be toggled any time whenever you need it. It auto dims when not typing.
- The touchscreen is useful for times when you're doing tedious tasks like clicking check boxes.
- The camera is nice for signing into the laptop without typing anything. Though sometimes it doesn't work so I use a pin code instead.
- The taller screen helps you see more on webpages and images at once without scrolling down.
- The battery while doing basic web browsing or reading lasts for over 7 hours which is much more than I've ever seen from a Windows laptop! Just be sure to enable energy saver. I barely have to charge it up and the temps stay low.
- The incredible processor having such high speeds and the RAM being at 7500 MT/s makes for a snappy experience. Just buy a laptop stand to help with cooling and you'll be golden.
- The AI key can be remapped to chatGPT instead.
- The chassis is made out of aluminum and feels cold to touch, good for thermals. It is also very thin.
- It has a built-in battery optimizer enabled by default that can learn your usage patterns and prevent you from always charging to 100%, which helps the battery last more years down the line. Though this confused me because the battery still shows 100% even though it doesn't reflect the lower amount that it really is.
- Running a medium ended 3D game got 54 C in temp, starting the TDP at 25 watts and went down to 15 watts automatically. This is very reasonable temps so far for playing a game.
- The max TDP is 28 watts which is useful for pushing higher end games. It automatically fluctuates between 2 watts to 28 watts as it needs for the tasks. It hovers around 2 - 4 watts TDP when web browsing.

The cons:
- You can only charge the laptop on the right side.
- The so-called fast charge is not that fast. I gain 35% in 30 minutes instead of 50% like the advertisement. But it's still reasonably fast while the battery lasts long between charges.
- The screen aspect ratio is 16:10, so 16:9 videos won't fill the screen and shows a black bar on top and bottom.
- There's no SD card slot for extra storage, but you can use a small-sized USB SD card adapter instead.
- The power button is next to the delete key. But at least it's harder to press in and it has to be pressed down for a bit to work.
- There are AI services that start up with the system and use up a chunk of memory. You cannot permanently disable them and have to remember to close them upon each reboot.
- The rubber grip on the back causes the laptop to slide around on certain surfaces.
- The USB ports are stiff to insert into, but this also helps keep peripherals plugged in sturdier.

Overall, I'm happy with this laptop and it surpasses my old HP laptop and my steam deck in so many ways and combines both of their uses into one device. I would recommend this laptop to pc enthusiasts and to anyone who wants an actual GOOD computer without paying $1000. These specs do not disappoint. This is a future laptop to use over the years until its end of life. No need to ever upgrade from here.

text:
9/10 Would Recommend
In Summary:
- Expensive computer, but for all the features you get it's definitely worth it, and you can easily buy a "like-new" one from a third-party and still receive a basically brand new laptop while saving hundreds of dollars.
-The ability to flip into a tablet, "tented" screen, and regular laptop creates so many options for use and programming; it's basically a great quality three-in-one laptop/tablet/TV.
- Works well for cloud gaming.
- Crisp, clear screen, that is big enough to be able to see even if you need glasses, but not too big.
- The only negatives I've experienced so far are that the keyboard is a little different and takes some getting used to, and that the speakers are on the keyboard which causes the sound to come from "behind" the device if using it in tablet or "tent" mode.
- I'm really happy with this purchase and would recommend it to anyone who is looking for a quality device with multiple uses.

Totally exceeds expectations!
I'm so glad I chose to buy a "like-new" one instead of buying one brand new; I've never done it before because it always made me nervous something would be wrong, but truly, it was like getting a brand new laptop for hundreds less than it would have been. The only difference is that there was no packaging; the laptop was just in a regular cardboard box within a box, but was secured and protected for shipping with a lot of bubble wrap. When I booted it up, it immediately prompted me to set up the computer for the first time; I don't think that this laptop was ever even used by anyone else before. If it was, I would have no way of knowing because it came in pristine condition and needed to be set up as if using it for the very first time.
The laptop itself is awesome; I love the way that it flips into a "tablet, " as well as how you can flip it ~270° to tent it so you can watch something on the screen without having the keyboard in the way. The battery life is unbelievably long; I've had it for almost 3 days now and have used it for hours, without turning it off when not using it and still haven't had to plug it in. I love gaming and have a Luna controller that I use to play video games through the cloud; it was a little confusing and difficult to connect the controller to the computer but once I did, it worked awesome and I've had a blast being able to play games on a much bigger screen than my tablet has. The screen itself is also beautiful; I wear glasses, and even without them on I can see it really well from a few feet away. It's a decent sized screen: it's big, but not too big. It's sharp and clear.
The only thing I don't like about it too much is the keyboard. It's a little awkward, like the buttons are almost slightly to the right of where my hands think they should be so that's taking a little getting used to. My one other small complaint is that when you flip it into "tent" mode, the speakers wind up behind the screen since they're on the keyboard part of the device. This makes it a little hard to hear and you can definitely tell the sound is coming from "behind" the screen rather than in front of it, which is what you would want if you were using it to watch TV or play a game. This is only a small inconvenience; if you turn up the volume a little bit you can hear it better, and you get used to the sound being behind the screen. If it really bothers you, I'm sure it would also be easily fixed by connecting a speaker through Bluetooth.
All-in-all, I love this computer and am really happy with my purchase. I spent months comparing laptops: their speed, screen-quality, features, and many more aspects - the most important of course being price. While this choice was a little more expensive than what I originally budgeted for, I was able to make it work by buying it "used" and it was totally worth the extra money. 9/10 would recommend.

They worked on the laptop for about 25 minutes, and while I can't tell exactly what was done, I do know it was a series of keystrokes and a flash drive. Geek Squad hands the laptop back to me and tells me it's a hardware issue and not worth the cost of repair. I take the laptop back home and get in a chat with technical support. They have me do what appears to be the same steps Geek Squad did. Then they tell me I need an empty flash drive to reset/reinstall the BIOS. Now I'm not really that tech savvy, but I know enough to tell the technician that all the steps that they have had me do I already had done by Geek Squad, their authorized repair center. Tech tells me that without doing that last step with the empty flash drive they cannot determine that it is truly a hardware issue (really??!) and that they won't be able to give me a repair/replacement if I don't take that last step.

Sorry, HP, but you cannot convince me that the cost of a replacement laptop is worth more than the bad taste in my mouth, and my withering review (not only on Amazon, but to anyone who asks) of your inability to honor your very limited warranty. I can't imagine why you wouldn't send a replacement of a low-end laptop just to keep positive goodwill towards your customers. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
What I needed:
I needed a computer for my electronics lab. It didn't need to be immensely powerful, but I wanted something that would be easy to expand as needed. This PC met my needs almost perfectly, and at a very economical price. I purchased this 6 months ago (almost to the day), so this is not an "out of the box" impression, but one based on months of experience. It has been powered on (or sleeping) continuously, so I can remote access it when needed.

My uses are primarily centered around my lab work: Electronic Design, PCB Layout, and 3D Rendering of PCBs, along with Design of small enclosures and modest software development. I also have several PC connected pieces of bench equipment: Digital Scope, Power Supplies, Function Generator, and whatever thing I'm creating. Most of these connect via USB, and one via RS-232.

This PC:
You can see in the pictures that the front panel has 4 USB ports - 2 are SuperSpeed. These have already proven valuable for quick attachments.

The rear panel is loaded up with 6 more USB ports (2 of which are SuperSpeed), and I've used most of them. If I had to, I could easily dig out an old PS2 Keyboard to free up another USB port - but with 4 empty ports on the front I'm ok for now.

As noted above, I needed RS-232, and this PC had one - which is a bonus. Of course, I could have plugged in a USB to RS-232 adapter. Beneath the back-panel RS-232 port (the gray plug in the picture) is a VGA connector, which I don't expect to use. To the left of those are a couple of Display Ports - one connected to my big screen (3440 x 1440). The specs say that each can support a 4K monitor, but my bench doesn't have space (and the screen resolution works for my eyeballs and needs).

The host processor in the unit I purchased is an i5-4590 quad core running at 3.3 GHz. The motherboard memory slots are full, loaded with 16 GB of RAM. The motherboard has 3 SATA ports, but they are fully occupied, connected to a 240 GB SSD hosting Win10 Pro, a 1GB spinning HDD, and a DVD drive. The graphics is served with an integrated Intel HD 4600. For further expansion, there are 4 PCIe slots: 2 x X1, 1 x X4 and 1 x X16.

Other Discoveries:
* The BIOS still had the name of the prior "owner" (a company), which is probably where many of these came from. It was simple to change, so now is hosts a name appropriate for my lab.
* This PC is not for gaming, so I didn't rate that since I've never run a game on it. With my single high-resolution monitor connected, spinning a 3D model of a modestly complex circuit board is fast - it more than meets my needs.
* And I had no need for Tech Support, so I didn't rate that either.

My Expansion:
* In the pictures you'll see one of the PCI slots is occupied - with the 4-channel SATA adapter that I added. The 3 on the motherboard were occupied but I needed one more for an external HD dock.
* I expect to add a Webcam soon.
* I also expect to add one more PCI card to it, to add USB-C connectors. My newest gear (Laptop, Phone, etc.) all have USB-C, so this will be necessary.

My Summary:
This was the right PC for my needs. It was also relatively inexpensive. It has been running close to non-stop since my unboxing. It "seems" quiet enough for most any location, but my lab isn't the best place to judge that.

It didn't have support for every interface I needed but was more than expandable enough to add to it. I do wish the overall unit was a bit smaller (for my lab space), and in years prior I had a large tower PC, but tired of crawling under the desk to swap cables around.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
It was delivered on time and was in like-new condition as advertised. It has a smaller footprint than a full-size desktop which I had concerns about before I got it. However, once I opened the access panel, I was impressed. It has a recessed latched pull handle that removes the whole access panel exposing everything and no screws to unscrew or lose. Inside, not a speck of dust, literally, like a new computer, you can't tell that it's renewed/upgraded.

Even though it's smaller everything is easy to see and get to so if you need or want to do anything inside it's awesome. You can see everything and get to it with ease. You don't have to be a contortionist or have tiny hands and fingers. The drives and optical reader (DVD) are contained within a rack that you just pivot upward to release and you have full easy access to them. Additional expansion slots to add what you like. If you should want to increase RAM from 16 to 32 GB there is nothing around them so removing and replacing them in the slots would be effortless. I was surprised how cool this computer runs even when using multiple high resource software at the same time with no lag.

As for the USB Keyboard and Mouse, USB WiFi Adapter. These are low cost and just so you have something. As low cost as keyboard and mouse are I really like them. If you use something else don't throw them out as others have said. Save them as an emergency back up or give them to someone. I have a Logitech wireless keyboard and mouse but still using the ones that came with this computer. USB WiFi Adapter isn't the best it's not real fast and not great for long-distance so I did buy a better one at the same time. There are a lot of cheap USB WiFi Adapters that stop working after 2-3 months but here is a low-cost $17 good one I use so can avoid the hassle.
Just search amazon for -
TP-Link AC600 USB WiFi Adapter for PC (Archer T2U Plus)- Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop with 2.4GHz, 5GHz High Gain Dual Band 5dBi Antenna, Supports Windows 10/8.1/8/7/XP, Mac OS 10.9-10.14
It increased my transfer speed from 300 Mbps or less and 3 bars signal strength to a transfer speed of 433 to 490 Mbps and 5 bars signal strength.

All you have to do is connect a monitor, the keyboard, mouse, and USB wifi adapter and power up. You do need to set up you user account like any new computer. This is Microsoft so it wants you to use a Microsoft account to have a better "online experience". But all you need to do is enter your login for a Microsoft email account or create one during set up. That step requires connecting to the internet and entering the password. Or you can create an offline user account like the old days. The rest of the setup questions are about your preferences and you're ready to go.

Windows 10 Pro works perfectly. My daughter got one of these a while ago and wouldn't stop praising it so I got one. She gave me a heads up about the USB WiFi Adapter solution too. I couldn't be happier with this purchase.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This laptop is an excellent supplement to my desktop windows PC. It's speedy, lightweight, and turns on in a blink. I appreciate the privacy settings and that I can disable all the (MANY) AI features as I'm not into that - if you are, you'll be pleased with the functionality. If you're not, it's easy to turn off.

Since the OS is chrome, signing into a google account makes setting up all of your access stupidly simple. The entire startup process - including downloading updates, which were estimated at an hour long - took less than 20 minutes including the time I spent finicking with the text display, background, etc., and then I was off to the races.

The screen is beautifully matte. No distracting glare or reflection means I don't have to stare into my own eyes while typing this. The speakers aren't anything to write home over and the sound gets garbled at the higher end of the volume range, but as I'll personally be using my headphones it's not a concern for me.

If this laptop will supplement your windows computer, I ~strongly~ recommend google remote desktop. You can link this laptop to any of your other devices and access them securely. No third party scaries with questionable security - just google! I was initially a little disappointed that I wouldn't be able to run any of my windows specific programs, but this solves that problem with the side benefit of not having to re-install everything. Just run the remote access on both machines et voila! You're in. The other PC does have to be on, but there is no noticeable lag and it runs amazingly.

A caveat - Google Meet is preinstalled, which is convenient, but it's the barest of bare bones. The video call was clear, with crisp sound and not a moment of lag even when switched between chrome's web access and the app, but I mean BARE bones. No background filters or removal, no blur, just plain unaltered video. Looking into it, it appears that the version available is not able to use these features. I was very surprised considering it's a native app, built for this OS and even my very dumb, very cheap android can handle it better. A word of caution if that's part of your intended use.

Everything else is similarly efficient. It works. The apps are numerous, fast, and easy to use, and I was pleasantly surprised at the speed and smooth playback even when I opened everything at once.

This laptop is quick, lightweight but solid, a good value, and an awesome supplement to my PC. It will be valuable for me to have to continue managing my business while I'm on the go, and would be a great option for simple entertainment needs.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
Simplicity and ease of use, that's what we like. Setup is as easy as it gets, especially if you're already an android user and have a Google account. This is the easiest device I've ever set up, hands down. It was up and fully running in about 20 minutes or less. Many thanks to HP for streamlining this process. The build quality is excellent, which is what I've come to expect from HP so no surprises there. I love that it runs the Chromebook OS rather than Windows. I'm very familiar with both but tired of Windows bloatware and this OS is refreshing to use. Apps are easy to browse and quick to download. The AI and privacy settings allow you to easily tailor them to your liking and I appreciate that. 
It has 4 gigs of RAM and 64gigs of storage so it's not a monster but it's no slouch either. It's not designed to be a gaming laptop so don't expect great results if you're running a meaty game. It is very good for tasking and streaming however. This laptop boots in a heartbeat, very fast. I'm using a Starlink connection and web surfing has been seamless and flawless. I've had zero problems running DIY vids and streaming movies. The speakers are sub-par so don't expect great sound. In less than a minute I was able to connect my JBL Flip via Bluetooth so no problem there. The screen is as crisp as it gets and has a beautiful matte finish. 
Battery life is decent and it recharges pretty fast. It can run a little warm but that's not a big surprise. Most laptops run warm in my opinion and it's not any hotter than others I've owned. It could benefit from more C-ports but not a deal breaker. It's an outstanding laptop for the price in my opinion.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This laptop is an excellent supplement to my desktop windows PC. It's speedy, lightweight, and turns on in a blink. I appreciate the privacy settings and that I can disable all the (MANY) AI features as I'm not into that - if you are, you'll be pleased with the functionality. If you're not, it's easy to turn off.

Since the OS is chrome, signing into a google account makes setting up all of your access stupidly simple. The entire startup process - including downloading updates, which were estimated at an hour long - took less than 20 minutes including the time I spent finicking with the text display, background, etc., and then I was off to the races.

The screen is beautifully matte. No distracting glare or reflection means I don't have to stare into my own eyes while typing this. The speakers aren't anything to write home over and the sound gets garbled at the higher end of the volume range, but as I'll personally be using my headphones it's not a concern for me.

If this laptop will supplement your windows computer, I ~strongly~ recommend google remote desktop. You can link this laptop to any of your other devices and access them securely. No third party scaries with questionable security - just google! I was initially a little disappointed that I wouldn't be able to run any of my windows specific programs, but this solves that problem with the side benefit of not having to re-install everything. Just run the remote access on both machines et voila! You're in. The other PC does have to be on, but there is no noticeable lag and it runs amazingly.

A caveat - Google Meet is preinstalled, which is convenient, but it's the barest of bare bones. The video call was clear, with crisp sound and not a moment of lag even when switched between chrome's web access and the app, but I mean BARE bones. No background filters or removal, no blur, just plain unaltered video. Looking into it, it appears that the version available is not able to use these features. I was very surprised considering it's a native app, built for this OS and even my very dumb, very cheap android can handle it better. A word of caution if that's part of your intended use.

Everything else is similarly efficient. It works. The apps are numerous, fast, and easy to use, and I was pleasantly surprised at the speed and smooth playback even when I opened everything at once.

This laptop is quick, lightweight but solid, a good value, and an awesome supplement to my PC. It will be valuable for me to have to continue managing my business while I'm on the go, and would be a great option for simple entertainment needs.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
Simplicity and ease of use, that's what we like. Setup is as easy as it gets, especially if you're already an android user and have a Google account. This is the easiest device I've ever set up, hands down. It was up and fully running in about 20 minutes or less. Many thanks to HP for streamlining this process. The build quality is excellent, which is what I've come to expect from HP so no surprises there. I love that it runs the Chromebook OS rather than Windows. I'm very familiar with both but tired of Windows bloatware and this OS is refreshing to use. Apps are easy to browse and quick to download. The AI and privacy settings allow you to easily tailor them to your liking and I appreciate that. 
It has 4 gigs of RAM and 64gigs of storage so it's not a monster but it's no slouch either. It's not designed to be a gaming laptop so don't expect great results if you're running a meaty game. It is very good for tasking and streaming however. This laptop boots in a heartbeat, very fast. I'm using a Starlink connection and web surfing has been seamless and flawless. I've had zero problems running DIY vids and streaming movies. The speakers are sub-par so don't expect great sound. In less than a minute I was able to connect my JBL Flip via Bluetooth so no problem there. The screen is as crisp as it gets and has a beautiful matte finish. 
Battery life is decent and it recharges pretty fast. It can run a little warm but that's not a big surprise. Most laptops run warm in my opinion and it's not any hotter than others I've owned. It could benefit from more C-ports but not a deal breaker. It's an outstanding laptop for the price in my opinion.

text:
I took the risk that you take when you buy these refurbished machines, and I got lucky-- absolutely no damage, and it functions perfectly as far as I can tell (I've had it for several weeks.)

If you are not accustomed to the Chrome OS, then you need to understand that the sorts of applications you can install on it are extremely limited. But on the other hand, this thing isn't powerful enough that you would want to be doing anything terribly complicated anyways.

This is not a machine for video editing, animation, graphic design, or music composition, etc.

This is an outstanding machine for doing anything you can do within a web browser (checking and writing emails, messing around on social media, general browsing and reading, etc.)

Aside from that, my main purpose for this machine is to read and study ebooks and PDFs... I used to like eReaders, but now I think I prefer reading off a luminous screen.

But I am irritated that there aren't many Android apps for reading ebooks and PDFs that work exactly right on a Chromebook... you're limited to installing anything you could install on your phone.

If you're a nerd, you can find workarounds (which allow you to install Linux apps,) but I don't think it's worth the hassle.

Aside from all that software related stuff--the build quality of this machine is outstanding. The exterior is a very high quality hard plastic that feels like it's really going to take a beating... I can see how it's meant for students.

Of course the screen is very small, but that makes the whole thing overall very small-- I almost forgot I had it in my backpack the other day. I see why they call it ultra portable-- I can't wait to bring it with me on a long flight.

Some people might dislike the fact that the bezel all around the screen is very wide, but I know from experience, that is a *good* thing. It gives you something to grab on to, which you need with a machine like this, as you're going to be shifting it around all the time. I cracked the bezel on my last (insanely expensive) laptop, because it was just too thin/narrow-- just squeezing it between my thumb and forefinger was enough to crack it. That's not going to happen with this.

It takes a wall-to-brick-to-USB-C type adapter; it's funny they gave me a Lenovo one, but it works fine.

I'll end with something that really irritated me, though it's a problem of whoever did the packing and shipping at Amazon's distribution centre--this computer came in its own plain thin box with a tiny bit of bubble wrap, but then that small box was placed inside a MASSIVE box with no packing material around it at all-- allowing it to just bounce around freely inside. Amazon really has to do something about the people who pick and pack and deliver items in my neck of the woods (I've complained countless times, but the people I end up interacting with via email are just as useless)....anyhow, I can't remove any stars for that. This computer is rugged enough that it tolerated their incompetent packing.

text:
I have not used a Windows based ARM laptop yet and to be honest I was a bit skeptical as I had heard that Windows on ARM has not been great in the past. I did however hear that they had come a very long way so was curious to check it out for myself. I am pleasantly surprised at how seamless it has been so far, if I didn't know it was ARM I probably would not have picked up on it, at least not for a while. The laptop itself is actually quite nice and has lots to offer for a reasonable price but there are a few things holding me back from giving it a five stat review (not deal breakers but worth talking about).

So my first and biggest gripe with it is the bloatware, I have not experience this much of it on a laptop before. I understand these partnerships between Acer and these other companies help keep costs down but it felts invasive to me. Just to name a few, the laptop came preinstalled with McAfee, NordVPN, WebAdvisor by McAfee, Dropbox Promotions, a couple web links made to look like apps, the worst one being a pinned bookings.com logo to the task bar, and a ridiculous amount of Acer software. I am personally really not a fan of this kind of stuff as it adds things to my computer that may slow it down or take up space without me potentially knowing about it. I ended up making a Windows 11 ARM image and doing a fresh install after I linked this Windows 11 key to my account.

A few other things I noticed that are not my favourite, the lack of a finger print reader, USB-C ports only on the left side, and a relatively big power cord considering it is only 65 Watts. The laptop has Windows Hello which works really well and is a great feature. It also includes a physical slider to block the camera, again a really nice feature. However, I need to keep this slider open if I want the ability to quickly sign into my computer, a fingerprint reader would be a nice alternative for logging in. The computer has two USB-C ports which are also used to power the laptop, I am glad they are on the left side so they don't get in the way when I use a mouse but I do wish it had a port on each side to better accommodate any type of setup. For the power cord I was really hoping for a more modern looking brick that plugs directly into the wall with the USB-C cord going directly to the laptop, however its more the traditional style with the detachable (and thick) power cable going into the power supply then from the power supply into the laptop. But, it is USB-C for power and was able to use my own 65W power brick and cable without issues.

Outside of these, honestly pretty minor, issues, the laptop is actually pretty great. At 16" it is a fairly large laptop but is quite thin and not super heavy for the size. The screen has a 16:10 resolution and can run at 120Hz leaving the overall experience feel more smooth. The slightly larger aspect ratio is great as it gives that much more vertical space to work with. The screen is also a touch screen, has nice colours, and is bright. I actually really enjoy typing on the keyboard, the keys feel nice and responsive. The layout is a little different than I am use to so its taking a little time to adjust but nothing too crazy. It has a small num pad on the side, nice to have it but its size also requires some getting use to. The track pad is decent but I do find my finger has a hard time gliding across it sometimes, especially when trying to drag something. But it is large, has a click feedback when pressed, and works with the known gestures. The speakers, to me, feel pretty lacklustre, they are functional but not super loud and essentially no base. The camera falls in the same boat for me, the image quality is not great but it is functional and I am happy it has one.

Overall I think this is actually a pretty nice laptop at a reasonable price. I was worried the ARM processor would cause more issues but so far it has not stopped me from doing anything I normally do. I was even able to install Steam and boot up some "not so demanding" games and it simply just worked without any compatibility issues. The bloatware was annoying but a fresh install solved the problem. The other minor issues I pointed out are definitely not deal breakers and only worth mentioning. And as a bonus it included three months to game pass, not sure that will always be the case but was happy to get it!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If this PC matches your needs, it is an excellent buy.
Comments:
It has two expansion slots, one short, one full. Both PCIe. (The current picture shows four expansion slots. This is an error, it has two.)
It has room for two SATA SSDs (it comes with one, 1TB SSD.). I read somewhere that the max size is 2 TB, so the max internal storage would be 4 TB. If you add a second drive, you'll need a SATA data cable and a SATA power splitter (1 to 2) and a mounting bracket (The bay is for a 3.5" drive, most SATA drives are 2.5".)

The literature says it comes with five USB-3 and four USB-2 ports. All 9 ports are colored black. Normally USB-3 is colored blue. Based on the exposed pins inside of the ports, the four in front are USB-2, and the 5 in back are USB-3.1 (AFAICT.) USB 3.1 gen 1 supports transfer speeds of up to 5 Gbps. USB 3.1 gen 2 supports transfer speeds of up to 10 Gbps. As I read the spec I think it has gen 1 (5 Gbps.)

It comes with two display ports. If your monitor only has HDMI inputs, you will need an adapter. It also has VGA output.

I got the 32 GB memory version -- it is very fast. I would recommend also getting the insurance for any renewed item.

If you need more storage, use a USB drive. If you want it fast, use USB 3.2 gen 2x2 (20 Gbps.) You can also get a larger capacity drive (~20TB). For Gen 3.2 2x2 you'll need to use the short expansion slot for a USB 3.2 gen 2x2 card. Use the Small Form Factor (SFF) size. Usually a SFF USB card supports 2 drives.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This HP 24mh monitor has a clear, crisp display and is the perfect size for desktop use (not too big, not too small). It accepts both HDMI and DisplayPort inputs (and even VGA for old school PCs). While Windows will select 60Hz refresh rate by default, you can go into Windows' display settings and select 75Hz refresh rate for this monitor. The 75Hz refresh rate really does help smooth out motion. You should also go into the monitor's "Image" menu setting and set Response Time to Level 3 which provides the best VSYNC performance. One of the best features that places this monitor above and beyond its price range is the 90-degree rotating screen, height adjustment, and swiveling base. The stand is rock-solid without any wobble. The speakers are just fine once you discover the menu control I explain below:

HOW TO FIX LOW VOLUME SOUND: The built-in speakers are better than some reviewers indicate. I believe most people don't discover that the monitor menu has its own volume control that's set to 50% volume by factory default. If you just connect this monitor to the PC you'll automatically get sound through the HP speakers via HDMI or DisplayPort (you only have to use the separate audio cable when using the VGA input). But no matter how high you turn up your PC volume control, you'll only get 50% volume from the monitor's speakers which is why people complain about low volume. To fix this, all you need to do is go to the "Management" tab of the monitor menu, select "Audio", and then turn up the volume control from 50 (default) to 100 and you'll find the monitor speakers are plenty loud. After that, you'll only have to use your PC volume control as normal.

This is a great quality monitor with features beyond its price range. Fantastic value, HP!

ADDITIONAL NOTE: HP sells an identical monitor to the HP 24mh under the model P24h. The only difference is that the P24h has a black plastic logo strip along the bottom instead of silver like the 24mh. Everything else is identical (specs, speakers, height adjustable stand, etc.) plus the P24h comes with both an HDMI cable and a DisplayPort cable.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Let's start with the pros!
-The size is good, I think it looks pretty, it's clear, has decently good speakers, can be turnt sideways, and is decent for gaming. I bought this primarily as a budget gaming monitor and to use it while I'm streaming games on Twitch.
-Not too expensive
-Nice looking stand

Cons
-Whenever I play any dark game like Skyrim, or see a dark loading screen from a game, I unfortunately see yellow bleeding on the sides. It's been there since Day 1. I most likely will exchange it for a new one if I can find a solution for my second issue. I really needed a monitor for streaming, so I don't have time to go days without a monitor again. This monitor does have a warranty, so I'll have to contact HP at some point if it really starts to bug me while playing games like Skyrim.
-I cannot connect my Nintendo Wii. I've tried contacting HP support but no one knows the answer so far and I get an error every time I plug in my Wii saying that I need to "change the mode" when there is no option to change the mode. I was really looking forward to streaming switch and Wii games but I haven't found a solution for the Wii games yet although Switch games are fine... if I don't, I may have to get a BENQ or some other type of gaming monitor that is more compatible with different gaming systems.
**EDIT: I had to change my Wii settings from 480i to 480p and it works now! & Now I have two monitors and put them on a VESA dual mount!

Besides that, it's great! The height adjustment is AMAZING, I LOVE that it has speakers, and it has the ports that I need! Another HDMI would be nice, but it's okay. Main problems were just the bleeding and not being able to connect my Wii. If I find a solution for my Wii I'll update this review!

text:
Ich habe einen kleinen Laptop für unterwegs gesucht auf dem ich die normalen Bürosachen oder mal ein Onlinemeeting machen kann. Zusätzlich sollte Windows10 installiert haben, weil ich die Zusatzkosten nicht zahlen wollte.
Weitere Wunschkriterien waren 10 Zoll und eine gute Akkuleistung. Aber auch der Preis sollte nicht so hoch sein, weil ich ihn nicht sehr häufig einsetzen werde. Gleichzeitig sollte er nicht zu billig sein, weil ich mit den "Billiggeräten" bisher noch nie gute Erfahrung gemacht habe.

Die Verarbeitung ist gut und dem Preis entsprechend. Alles komplett aus Kunststoff - aber vollkommen ok.
Das Gewicht ist angenehm leicht.

Die Einrichtung ging super flott und der Laptop war schnell im WLAN.
Hier gab es keinerlei Probleme.

Ich habe gleich einmal ein Virenprogramm durchlaufen zu lassen um zu überprüfen ob schädliche Software installiert ist. Hier war alles in Ordnung. Auch die im Internet angegeben Daten stimmen mit meiner Konfiguration überein.

Der WLAN-Empfang ist etwas schwächer als bei meinem MacBook aber in einem guten Rahmen.
Das Display ist gut - nicht sehr gut aber für den Preis überraschend gut. Ich habe noch etwas an den Kontrasten gedreht (was ich hätte nicht müssen) und jetzt sind die Farben wirklich schön und satt.

Die Akkulaufzeit ist erstaunlich hoch schwankt aber natürlich je nach Anwendungsbereich.
Beim Speicher empfehle ich gleich eine SD-Karte mit zu bestellen. Hier würde ich einem Markenhersteller und eine schnelle Ausführung empfehlen (es gibt so viel Schrott auf dem Markt und eine falsche SD-Karte bremst das gesamte System).
Ohne zusätzliche SD-Karte ist der Computer fast nicht benutzbar und kommt viel zu häufig ins stocken. Mit SD-Karte ist ein angenehm schnelles Arbeiten möglich. Ich habe mich für eine SanDisk Ultra 200 GB, 120 MB/s, Klasse 10, U1 entschieden. Die sind für unter 20€ zu haben und sind ein guter Kompromiss aus Preis und Leitung.

Die Beiliegende Maus und die Kopfhörer sollte man ganz schnell und ganz tief in der Schublade verstecken. Ich habe keine Ahnung was der Hersteller sich dabei gedacht hat. Die Kopfhörer sind wirklich grottig. Die Maus ist ja noch ganz ok - aber etwas hakelig und komplett überflüssig.

Ich bin sehr zufrieden mit dem Laptop - man sollte sich aber bewusst machen was man mit dem Gerät machen möchte. Normales Dokumente erstellen ist kein Problem. Auch mal ein Foto bearbeiten geht ... oder was streamen oder Videos ansehen. Auch Videokonferenzen sind möglich ... aber wer regelmäßig mit Photoshop arbeitet, Videos schneidet oder generell mit großen Dateien arbeite sollte sich nach einem anderen Gerät umsehen ...

Ich bin mit dem Preis- Leistungsverhältnis sehr zufrieden - ich habe kein MacBook erwartet und auch kein andere Wundermaschine ... sondern einen grundsoliden und arbeitsfähigen Laptop ... und den habe ich auch bekommen.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If this PC matches your needs, it is an excellent buy.
Comments:
It has two expansion slots, one short, one full. Both PCIe. (The current picture shows four expansion slots. This is an error, it has two.)
It has room for two SATA SSDs (it comes with one, 1TB SSD.). I read somewhere that the max size is 2 TB, so the max internal storage would be 4 TB. If you add a second drive, you'll need a SATA data cable and a SATA power splitter (1 to 2) and a mounting bracket (The bay is for a 3.5" drive, most SATA drives are 2.5".)

The literature says it comes with five USB-3 and four USB-2 ports. All 9 ports are colored black. Normally USB-3 is colored blue. Based on the exposed pins inside of the ports, the four in front are USB-2, and the 5 in back are USB-3.1 (AFAICT.) USB 3.1 gen 1 supports transfer speeds of up to 5 Gbps. USB 3.1 gen 2 supports transfer speeds of up to 10 Gbps. As I read the spec I think it has gen 1 (5 Gbps.)

It comes with two display ports. If your monitor only has HDMI inputs, you will need an adapter. It also has VGA output.

I got the 32 GB memory version -- it is very fast. I would recommend also getting the insurance for any renewed item.

If you need more storage, use a USB drive. If you want it fast, use USB 3.2 gen 2x2 (20 Gbps.) You can also get a larger capacity drive (~20TB). For Gen 3.2 2x2 you'll need to use the short expansion slot for a USB 3.2 gen 2x2 card. Use the Small Form Factor (SFF) size. Usually a SFF USB card supports 2 drives.

I always use refurbished desktop computers with my TV to watch YouTube or streaming services like Disney + or Prime Video. So I ordered this computer knowing it was used to replace an old Windows 10 computer that could not make the transition to Windows 11. It arrived much sooner than anticipated. There are only two minor negative points I would mention, even though I don't think they deserve to have a star removed. First is that the case is a little big compared to what modern computers tend to (this one is way bigger than my previous computer, even though this one doesn't have a DVD reader), so if you plan on adding this to your entertainment unit or have limited desk space, you might want to plan for that. Second is that mine came with one loose Wi-Fi antenna in the back, thanks to a screw nut that is too thin. I managed to open the case and tightened up enough so the antenna won't fall over anymore, but that is something you might want to be aware of if you purchase this particular computer.

Other than these two minor imperfections, I am very satisfied with this computer and how it performs.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'm very pleased with my purchase decision. I am a semi-retired accountant, working from home as a Fractional Controller. I have preferred Chromebooks for many years. When searching for a new Chromebook a year ago, I settled on this HP mainly because of the expanded memory. It contains 8GB memory capacity, which is double the amount of less-expensive Chromebooks being sold on Amazon. It also has a 10-key number pad to the right of the keyboard, which is important to an accountant.

After one year of heavy usage, I am very pleased with this Chromebook. Even when running the memory-intensive QuickBooks Online Advanced edition, the Chromebook performs remarkably. It is lightweight, has a larger screen, and the battery lasts several hours--even under the intense workload of QuickBooks Online. When under an intense workload (working with QuickBooks, driving a secondary portable monitor, recharging the headset, and running an intensive secondary application (usually Google Sheets), the battery lasts for at least 3 hours. After a morning working on the patio, or when the RV is using StarLink, I'll be ready for a lunch-break after 3 hours, and the battery recharges quickly so I'm ready to pound keys again after an hour and a half.

This laptop has been dropped, has stayed in the hot automobile, and has been heavily used 8-10 hours per day, and is still functioning like new (although the case does have some scratches and assorted battle scars). Chromebooks are impervious to viruses affecting the expensive laptops (Microsoft and, sometimes, even Apple). The only thing I truly miss is the ability to add a SIM-card (or E-SIM, preferably), and maybe the fact that this chromebook offers only two Type-C connections, one Type-A connection, plus a standard mini-headphone jack, as well as an SD card slot. I have never used the SD card slot, nor the 1/8" headphone jack, but the other connections operate well. I charge with the Type-C on the left side of the keyboard; the one on the right side is hit-and-miss--sometimes it will charge the laptop, other times not so much. The auxiliary monitor goes into the Type-C on the right side of the keyboard, and my bluetooth headset uses the Type-A on the right side of the keyboard to maintain its charge when docked. (The headset is bluetooth, so could connect to its own charger, but it's much easier to plug it into the laptop to charge.)

I find no issues with lagging from the laptop side of the equation. Of course, the WIFI connection will sometimes (rarely) lag, and the QuickBooks application itself will sometimes lag, but I have come to believe these lags are not originating with the laptop itself. The screen is bright, the sound is good. When I'm not wearing my headset and receive a call on Google Voice, I can use the internal microphone and speakers, which provide excellent quality--although the headset's microphone dampens background noise much better than does the laptop's internal microphone.

I would recommend this particular Chromebook, with its upgraded memory capacity, to anyone using exclusively web-based software and needing a work-horse of a laptop computer. After a year of pounding the keys on this HP laptop, I would purchase again, with no hesitation.

text:
It's alright for a gaming laptop and functions as it's supposed to, which I can't same for some of it's competitors (Alienware). However I do have a huge gripe that knocks off two stars. Most of the hardware on this is pretty good, especially for the price. But the USB ports are extremely outdated. The highest they go to USB-C 3.0, which is 5Gb of transfer speed. USB-C 3.1 and 3.2 have 10 Gb of speed and most external hardware you're going to find assumes you have that.
How this issue specifically affected me: The laptop has a small amount of storage (understandable for the price, I chose to not get the 1TB on purpose.) and I was going to supplement that with an external SSD. I bought everything for it (roughly $150 total) and got to gaming. My game would consistently start lagging out after roughly 30 minutes, and then full on crash after about an hour. So I tested the transfer speeds of my new SSD, they came out to 400 Mb/s, atrocious. I was supposed to be getting up to 6000 Mb/s. So I got a replacement SSD thinking that was the issue, nope. I almost replaced the enclosure and cables as I was desperately trying to find the issue. Finally through research, found out that the USB ports on this laptop were HARD bottle necking my speeds, to the point that I couldn't run a fairly non-intensive game.
To be clear, ALL other hardware on this laptop was more than capable of running it, and when the game is on my C drive it runs perfectly. But I will NEVER be able to run games or transfer large files from external sources because they cheaped out on the USB ports.

I've been using this computer for a while now, it works very well, but there are times when it stutters, the FPS drops to 0, which usually takes less than 1 second, but it's still very annoying. The screen's 165Hz refresh rate is spectacular, but I did an online test and I'm almost certain it has ghosting, which is also quite annoying. Also it's a bit slow when performing various tasks, such as opening the browser or simply changing categories on Steam.

I'm going to add more RAM since the 8GB it has doesn't seem enough to me; I even think that might be the root of the problem I mentioned. So, I'll try to upgrade to 32GB of RAM.

But despite all of the above, it's still a very good computer. I like that it comes with the Nitro Sense application and also with Intel's graphics software, since it allows for some customization. The camera looks good and works smoothly in good lighting, but the computer doesn't have anything to cover the camera.

You have 3 fan options: silent, balanced, and performance. Expect a lot of noise from the fan in performance mode. Also, another bad thing is that when I connected my headphones with a built-in microphone, the computer only recognized it as audio output, not as both audio input and output, so I had a lot of problems with that. I even had to restart my PC in safe mode to reset everything because I had no sound anymore, so be careful with that, If you experience the same issue, simply open the Realtek Audio Console application, then go to advanced device settings and program it as an input and output.

So I think it's a very good computer. You have to do a couple of things beforehand to be ready to use it for gaming or anything like that, but I don't think I'll be changing it for a long time. Just add more RAM and you'll probably be good to go. I'll update this review when I add more RAM to let you know if there are any changes to the stuttering.

So my final thoughts on this laptop are that I wish it were more of a turn-on, ready-to-use thing, but I guess you can't expect that at this price. Despite that, I give it 5 stars
