title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
TL;DR: The Acer Nitro is a solid budget-friendly gaming laptop that balanced school and gaming well. Loud fans, weak battery gaming, and fragile screen were drawbacks, but it handled demanding games at high settings and was great for a student lifestyle who fancies gaming in free time.

I used my Acer Nitro V 15 daily for both school and gaming, and for the price, it really impressed me with how versatile it was. Definitely felt like a purchase worth it.

As a full time college student taking online classes, this laptop was more than enough for productivity. Typing was seamless for the many essays and assignments I had to crank out, and it handled regular browsing with multiple tabs without breaking a sweat. I don’t do heavy creative work like video editing, but for what I did use it for, it never let me down.

Gaming was where it really surprised me. Titles like Red Dead Redemption 2 and The Last of Us Part II ran great at high settings, delivering smooth, immersive gameplay that felt way beyond what I expected at this price point. Paired with an external 2K 144Hz monitor at times and it kept up without any issues.

Portability was another big win. While it isn’t the lightest laptop out there, carrying it in a case made it easy to take from work to the library or just toss in my backpack. Honestly, I barely noticed the weight after a while.

Of course, there are trade-offs. The fan noise is one to note. On auto, it can get loud under load, and on max, it’ll easily fill a quiet room. That said, cooling does its job, and with headphones it wasn’t a dealbreaker. The other thing: gaming unplugged was basically a no-go. Performance dropped heavily on battery, which surprised me at first, but since I always had access to an outlet, it didn’t really affect my routine. On light use like schoolwork or browsing, I’d get about 2–3 hours on battery.

The display itself was fine, standard but enjoyable. Unfortunately, mine cracked after about a year from what felt like light pressure, which was disappointing and ultimately why I’m moving on to a new laptop.

On the bright side, upgrading was a breeze. I swapped in 32GB of RAM and added a 2TB SSD, which gave me more headroom for multitasking and plenty of storage for my game library. That definitely added to the experience.

Overall: The Acer Nitro V 15 delivered a great balance of school and gaming performance in a portable package. It’s not flawless, the fans get loud, battery gaming is basically impossible, and the screen durability left me wanting more, but for the time I used it, it played the games I wanted at high settings and fit perfectly into my student lifestyle. For the price, it’s a solid entry into gaming laptops.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'm very pleased with my purchase decision. I am a semi-retired accountant, working from home as a Fractional Controller. I have preferred Chromebooks for many years. When searching for a new Chromebook a year ago, I settled on this HP mainly because of the expanded memory. It contains 8GB memory capacity, which is double the amount of less-expensive Chromebooks being sold on Amazon. It also has a 10-key number pad to the right of the keyboard, which is important to an accountant.

After one year of heavy usage, I am very pleased with this Chromebook. Even when running the memory-intensive QuickBooks Online Advanced edition, the Chromebook performs remarkably. It is lightweight, has a larger screen, and the battery lasts several hours--even under the intense workload of QuickBooks Online. When under an intense workload (working with QuickBooks, driving a secondary portable monitor, recharging the headset, and running an intensive secondary application (usually Google Sheets), the battery lasts for at least 3 hours. After a morning working on the patio, or when the RV is using StarLink, I'll be ready for a lunch-break after 3 hours, and the battery recharges quickly so I'm ready to pound keys again after an hour and a half.

This laptop has been dropped, has stayed in the hot automobile, and has been heavily used 8-10 hours per day, and is still functioning like new (although the case does have some scratches and assorted battle scars). Chromebooks are impervious to viruses affecting the expensive laptops (Microsoft and, sometimes, even Apple). The only thing I truly miss is the ability to add a SIM-card (or E-SIM, preferably), and maybe the fact that this chromebook offers only two Type-C connections, one Type-A connection, plus a standard mini-headphone jack, as well as an SD card slot. I have never used the SD card slot, nor the 1/8" headphone jack, but the other connections operate well. I charge with the Type-C on the left side of the keyboard; the one on the right side is hit-and-miss--sometimes it will charge the laptop, other times not so much. The auxiliary monitor goes into the Type-C on the right side of the keyboard, and my bluetooth headset uses the Type-A on the right side of the keyboard to maintain its charge when docked. (The headset is bluetooth, so could connect to its own charger, but it's much easier to plug it into the laptop to charge.)

I find no issues with lagging from the laptop side of the equation. Of course, the WIFI connection will sometimes (rarely) lag, and the QuickBooks application itself will sometimes lag, but I have come to believe these lags are not originating with the laptop itself. The screen is bright, the sound is good. When I'm not wearing my headset and receive a call on Google Voice, I can use the internal microphone and speakers, which provide excellent quality--although the headset's microphone dampens background noise much better than does the laptop's internal microphone.

I would recommend this particular Chromebook, with its upgraded memory capacity, to anyone using exclusively web-based software and needing a work-horse of a laptop computer. After a year of pounding the keys on this HP laptop, I would purchase again, with no hesitation.

text:
Edit: It charges insanely fast! It takes around 30 mins for it to go from dying to 93% and stays charged for over 5 hours.
-------------
I like the sound quality. Screen is nice and will be good for when I draw on Krita, stream something, or game. The keyboard is great. Not sure how the touch pad is because I only use a wired mouse. It arrived only 2 days after I bought it. I believe this is a great laptop, especially for the price.

This is the first time I've bought a laptop with a USB-c charger instead of the traditional laptop charger. At first I was appalled by the change, but then I realized it's more convenient because you can use any usb-c. I assume it won't charge as fast if it's only via usb-c/without the block but what matters is it *will* charge. Be careful plugging things into it's ports because it's a weirdly snug fit.

I definitely recommend getting a compatible SSD to add. This laptop on it's own has pretty much no storage space. I have Samsung Evo Plus 970 nvme 1tb storage. It is very slow on Windows 11 and updates are long. I got rid of Windows and installed Linux Mint and it works so much better, unsurprisingly.

The delivery box didn't have a Handle With Care/Fragile label and that should change. The retail packaging it came in was snug and sleek. No damage to the packaging- super fresh. Definitely be prepared with scissors and a dash of patience because it is a bit of a challenge to actually open the packaging. It's airtight! Not a complaint, just a fact.

My recommendations:

1.) It's extremely slow on Windows. I recommend installing Linux if you know/can learn how or can have someone else do it. Linux Mint is the most lightweight and beginner friendly Linux distro. This laptop should use something lightweight like Mint.

2.) Get a compatible SSD card because you will need more space for doing anything at all. Again, I use Samsung Evo Plus 970 nvme with 1TB storage. It isn't expensive, at least not expensive when I bought it.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: Several months ago when the keys on my laptop mouse pad started to go out, I was really irritated because I have gotten so used to using the mouse pad that I was worried that I wouldn't be able to work as efficiently using a wireless mouse. I knew that it would only be a few days before the keys got to the point that I wouldn't be able to use them and started looking on Amazon for a wireless mouse that I might possibly be able to stand using on a daily basis. I spotted the AmazonBasics Wireless Mouse and thought that it wouldn't be that great because it was way cheaper than most of the other wireless ones that I could find. I went ahead and placed my order because I needed something and thought that if it didn't work that well, I wouldn't be out of that much money. When it arrived, I was happy to see that it was a tad bit smaller than other ones that I have used with desktops in the past since I have small hands. I opened the package, popped in some batteries, plugged the nano receiver into my USB slot, and it was working instantly. I thought that it would take some time to install ( I did not read much on it when I purchased it honestly, I just needed one quick!), but was SO happy to see that it needed nothing to be installed. I have been using this wireless mouse for about a year and half now and I have recommended it to SO many people who were looking for one. I work at home on my laptop 7 days a week and anywhere between 12 - 18 hours a day. I only have to change the batteries about once every two months (sometimes it will go a little longer and sometimes a little bit less - not sure on why though). This mouse has worked flawlessly since the day of purchase and I was SO wrong to think that because it was cheaper than the others that it wouldn't work as well. There has never been a time where it disconnected from the computer or that there was any issue using it. A few times when it has needed the batteries changed and I wait a few days, there is a tiny lag - but that is all my fault. The AmazonBasics Wireless Mouse has a little red indicator light that lets you know when the batteries are getting low and need to be changed. I like that feature so that I'm always aware of when they need to be changed. Since I travel a lot, this mouse is great because it doesn't take up a lot of space in the laptop bag. I also never have to worry about losing the nano receiver because once you remove the little door to the battery area, there is actually a space that the nano receiver clicks into making it perfect for travel. If you are in the market for a great wireless mouse, I would recommend the AmazonBasics Wireless Mouse because it has been through over a year of my all day, everyday use and still works just like the day that I purchased it!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My system came pretty well cleaned. It had something oily on part of the top, but that wiped off, though some had gotten into the dust screen so that had to be removed to clean. There were no scratches on the system, and everything seems in good working order.

As most other reviews have mentioned, mine came with the Ryzen pro 5 2400g, which is a 65W part, vs. the 2400ge which is 35W TDP but lower clocked. The top is covered in mesh for better airflow, probably because the 2400g does get hot in this little machine. Running a stress test, I was able to get it up to 93C but the cooling system, in a room at 68F, was able to keep it there so it never throttled (which it should do if it gets to 95C) and maintained just under 3.6ghz on all 4 cores (the base clock). Stressing a single core, it will go up to 3.9ghz, so it could be that others who were having issues with performance might have some problem with their system.

It came with 8GB of SK hynix DDR4 2666mhz RAM and a 256GB (older) Samsung PCI-E SSD. I got the SATA drive cage as well, which does have a fan for both its drive and the PCI-E drive that sits under the fan. I actually had a 16GB DDR4 3200mhz RAM set not being used, so I put that in and the system sees it as 2933mhz, which is the maximum RAM frequency supported for this CPU without overclocking, which this system does not do. So, I'd recommend at least picking up a second stick to get the benefits of dual channel which is supported, but if you buy all new RAM, I'd recommend picking up the faster stuff as well as it'll handle it.

My system came with the HDMI module so it has 1 HDMI and 2 display ports. Accessories were a very generic USB wired keyboard, a very generic USB wired mouse, a mini USB wireless dongle and a mini USB bluetooth dongle. You can put a PCI-E wireless/bluetooth module in this system, so that might be a better option. Keep in mind that this system has antenna for the PCI-E wireless/bluetooth module, but does not come with the module, and you will most likely (I had to, someone else mentioned this as well) have to remove the motherboard to get to the antenna wires, as they seem to have been tucked underneath. To remove the motherboard, you have 4 screws plus the 3 that hold the heatsink onto the CPU. The problem here is that you shouldn't remove the heatsink without cleaning and reapplying thermal paste, so you basically will have to rebuild the system to install the wireless module properly.

The power adapter this comes with has been mentioned at least once before. Mine was not a HP OEM power brick, but a generic one. It had the right barrel connector, but it's a 90W 19V 4.7A adapter. It appears the OEM adapter should be a 19.5V 4.62A, but finding the OEM 90W adapter is tough unless you want to spend a lot. My system does immediately power on when plugged in as others have mentioned, but you can turn it off and it will stay off, and seems to run ok on the generic adapter.

One thing I think someone else mentioned, but the first generation Zen processors (Ryzen 1000 and 2000 series) are not on the Windows 11 supported CPU list, and you will be blocked from upgrading to Windows 11 on this machine. It does have TPM 2.0, so it's just the CPU that is blocking you. Microsoft does have instructions for getting around this, by entering a registry entry to tell the installer to allow unsupported CPUs, but Windows updates still will not let you upgrade directly. You'll need to download the installer/updater from Microsoft then run that. It does appear that upgrading from the installer works, though people were originally saying you would have to install fresh. Anyway, doing this, you have to agree that you are fine with possible issues and lack of driver support, so do it at your own risk I guess.

I've been wanting to upgrade my Lenovo intel i7 ThinkCentre Mini PC to a newer Ryzen Mini for a while and this Refurb deal from StallionTek looked too good to be true . When it arrived I noticed right away that one of the back USB ports was clearly broken with the pins touching each other . I nearly sent it back right there , but they were out of stock and I couldn't set up a replacement so I decided that if there no other problems that I'd keep it .
I separated the pins in the bad USB and put some electrical tape in it to keep it from shorting out and powered the PC on . It fired right up and wanted to update Windows so I went ahead and updated everything and checked the system specs to find that it was the same as most people reportedly received . A Ryzen 2400g , 256gb NVME SSD , 1x 8gb memory stick , an HDMI in the optional port , and has the HDD caddy for a SATA HDD as well which is great because I wanted to add a second HDD for storage . It does not have a wireless card in it , but it does have the antennas and an empty M.2 for one . The PC is fast and seems to be a happy little PC .
I wanted to install a wireless card and put some Thermal Grizzly thermal paste on the processor so I had to completely disassemble the PC to get the antennae wires out from under the motherboard and got a good look at everything in the process . This thing is really clean inside , no dust at all . It already had brand new thermal paste on the APU which is really good to see . So as far as the refurb I would give it an 8 out of 10 , the bad USB port is the only thing that I can complain about , it really shouldn't have shipped like that . So close to perfect . With a few more upgrades it'll be a little beast . I have 32gb of DDR4 coming and will add a 2TB NVME in place of the 256gb and will end up adding a storage HDD sometime in the future as well . I assume that I just had bad luck with the USB port so I will recommend this product , it's great .
**Edit - Installed the m.2 wireless and it works really well (Intel model# 9260NGW)
Installed 2x 16gb (32gb total) G.Skill Ripjaws 2666 memory with no problems
Installed 2TB Kingston NVME SSD and cloned the HDD to it with no problems

This mini is certainly a step up from my old one , love it .

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
First some background:
I am not a Dell lover, more of a Dell Hater. I don't like how they used specialized components in their computers. This one is no different, use this as is, it can't really be upgraded. Power supply is a dell custom one, and it's tiny. Having said that, this one has turned out to be a really nice computer.
Cosmetic:
This computer visually has no issues, no scratches and the inside had zero dust in it.
Components:
The components are about 3 to 5 years old according to the counters on the hard drives. One of the drives is an M.2 Samsung drive made specifically for Dell, it contains the OS (I call these gumsticks because of their shape). The second drive is a 2.5 inch 1TB drive. It's empty. This computer allows for toolless installation of hard drives, which is great. I replaced the 2.5 1TB drive with a 3.5 8TB drive with zero issue. There is only one SATA power and data cable spot on the motherboard, so it can't fit more than 1 hard drive along with the gumstick. It comes with a keyboard and mouse. I didn't use them, so I can't comment. It also has bluetooth I guess. I use a hardwired ethernet connection so i can't speak to any wireless connections.
Initialization:
During initialization I logged into my Microsoft account and everything worked flawlessly. I didn't have to enter an activation code like the STG Skytech Global paperwork said I would have to. I later went on my Microsoft account and verified this computer was registered with Windows 11 pro. I don't know anything about STG, but this computer was well cleaned and setup, so good for them. I left the computer on and occasionally cycled power over a full day to get all the windows 11 updates before I tried to do anything to the computer. I would recommend this to everyone. Let windows get fully updated before continuing. I'm not at Windows version 25H2. No issues. No display glitches that some people have indicated. Again, I would recommend not altering the computer for a day, until windows has updated to 25H2. I keep doing the 'check for updates' in windows to make this go faster.
Performance:
This computer takes about 15 seconds to boot. Very fast. Draws about 30 watts even when performing a disk transfer of 3TBs. I have no idea how they get the power so low. I haven't played games on it, nor would I suggest it. I'm using this as a backup system for my main computer. There is no external video card.
Conclusion:
I really am impressed with this computer. It's very small, uses almost no power, and allows me to connect via my local network to my main computer for backing up files. And it has windows 11 pro installed.

text: I am using this for a basic email and web surfer machine. It is very fast..... looks and runs like a brand new machine. Came with a new keyboard and mouse (not refurb) but the most basic cheap KB and mouse. The machine specs out exactly as advertised. Even came with CD/DVD player/ burner. The case is small form factor, so do not get it with the expectation of getting and doing a lot of upgrades. There is a PCI Express. There were NO unpleasant or unexpected surprises. Runs super quiet.... really not bad at all. Here is the deal as to why its so cheap for the most part. The copy of windows is an OEM version issued and licensed exclusively to Dell. You do not get a copy of Windows on disc with this machine, you get a hard drive with an image file on it ( the main drive has a partition on it) which is where the copy is located. You can do full factory restore from that partition and set the machine up like it was the day you got it and it will activate and be a legitimate copy/machine.... BUT it only works on the machine it shipped out with (or one just like it) Microsoft has almost reached the end of life with Win 10.... set for about Oct 2025. I ran the test to see if the machine would take win 11 upgrade and it says NO...however a Google search results many people saying they have run it just fine. The primary reason it fails is the processor. It is not in the recommended list of processors that Microsoft recommends for Windows 11. It passed on every thing else. And like I said there have been many folks who have said they have installed it (win 11) and it is running just fine with this very processor. In conclusion at this price it is almost basically a disposable cup...wait I mean PC, LOL.... you could just buy a new one every couple of years. Or you can do as I am going to and get the latest copy of Linux / Ubuntu Wilma and run that. (free for personal use) You can burn a copy that will boot and run from a USB drive if you want to try before installing (I have no affiliation with Linux or make any thing off this suggestion, its just something I personally like) Ok to end this, I have worked on/built computers for the last 30 + years and have quite a large knowledge base and I just can not find any reason to complain about this PC/purchase.

I only rank it as 4 stars because should something happen within the warrantee period, it will be a hassle to deal with HP, regardless of what anyone claims. But, the machine itself is flawless and I'm very happy with its performance thus far.

text: Shifty swap-outs. I got this laptop and a 4 year Asurion protection plan through Amazon, but later learned it really comes from a 3rd party seller, PConline US (440 Terry Ave N, WA 98109 is the address listed in my bill). I used the laptop for two weeks. All that time, the fan would try to come on and then turn off after two seconds, over and over again. The laptop got very hot. When I called HP, they said that 3rd party vendors swap out parts to "beef up" machines. For example, this laptop was advertised on Amazon as 64 GB RAM and 2 TB memory. HP said that model is only suppposed to have 4 GB RAM and 512 GB STORAGE MEMORY. HP says that this is a known issue, and that when sellers like this make these upgrades the new parts are not 100% compatible with other parts--like the fan. This business practice then VOIDS the manufacturer's warranty--which neither Amazon nor PConline mentioned. Luckily, I can still send this back to Amazon, which promises a refund. I think PConline should be more up front that their systems, though advertised as "new", are not new from the manufacturer. They are Frankenstein laptops refitted with additional parts and are therefore warranty-void.

text:
UPDATE 2/25/26:

This is still a great deal for the money. It has worked flawlessly. I'm adding a star because of the seller's behavior. RenewByte-Quality Recertified helped me quickly, efficiently and without hassling me about the problem I encountered and the solution.

I needed to implement NFS services on this system. I intentionally bought something running Pro because I anticipated this being a need. I went to activate the feature, and it wasn't there. I dug around and found that Win 11 Home had actually been installed. To me, this was a no brainer, easy think to fix knowing how the refurb market works, and it's an easy mistake to make, so shouldn't be any sweat. It took me longer working with Amazon to get a solid answer as to who specifically sold this to me through the Amazon refurb store than it did for RenewByte to solve my problem. All you need in this case is the right Product key and you can upgrade Home to Pro in-place (in case you didn't know that).

RenewByte was ON IT. As soon as I figured out it was them (and not the three other places Amazon pointed me at) they listened to the problem, understood the problem as I articulated it, and got me the right product key, which, of course, worked. My wife's system now has Win 11 Pro, not Home and all it took was a reboot to complete the process once I put the key in.

They could have, and I indeed have had other refurb groups run me around the mulberry bush to do a return because that's somehow "easier" for them when the only problem is something small like a card failed that I could replace on my own. RenewByte didn't do that. They took care of me with the least amount of friction possible.

THANK YOU, RenewByte, I will be looking to you for my future needs in this class of machine without looking at others, based on your customer service.

************************

This is a great deal for a productivity system. The unit is fast, and if you've got your MS account tied to your Windows machine, it really is an easy process to migrate systems, even from Win 10. As someone who has a heightened sense of security and data privacy I'm not a huge fan of that, but it does work super smooth.

For conducting online meetings with Teams or Zoom, MS Office work with large Word docs or Excel spreadsheets, it just cranks. The network is fast, it has plenty of USB ports and is not loud. I don't use the WiFi but it works and is decently fast. One thing I like about these Dell SFF systems is they are still expandable. There are 2 PCIe slots available, a bank of memory slots open, and I slapped a second SATA SSD for some working scratch space into the unit with zero issues.

I would imagine based on how well it performs that it could be used as a kids gaming machine. It would run Minecraft without breaking a sweat for sure, but for serious gamers you'd want something with more video capability.

I have used another one of these (though a 5070) as a linux jump server, and it works really well for that as well. It's tough to beat the price for what this system provides.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
PC sold mainly as advertised. It appeared mostly cleaned (save for some very light dust minus one star) , sealed and without odd smelling, came with some papers describing it was checked. The packaging was fairly well thought of and secured with foam corners.

The PC came with a large mouse pad, a mouse, and a keyboard. These, while serviceable aren't great to use for long term as the mouse does not have a switch nor does the keyboard. The mouse tends to turn off after 2 minutes constantly needing to be clicked on to function after it turns off. They required 1 AA and 1 AAA batteries which they did not come with. They also have their own separate dongles. In my recommendation, replace when possible with better peripherals.

As for the PC itself, it came with Windows 11 Pro as advertised. No bloatware of Dell which was nice to see just the vanilla, clean install of Windows 11. The machine is quick and responsive as expected of a machine with a 1TB NVMe drive, 32GB of DDR4 2666mhz of RAM, and a 9th gen i7 9700 with a blower style cooler. A nice addition was the power supply which is rated for an 80 Plus Platinum certification which is excellent use of power efficiency for a long term, long power on operations. the AX210 Wifi/Bluetooth module was taped to the front panel of the machine with the antenna loosely hung over the blower cooler. This was fairly sloppily put together even if it still remains functional. Though to note, the drive is of some no-name brand which is a PCIe 3.0 spec. I eventually plan to replace it with a more reputable brand but seems to be reliable for now.

There are some scuffs on the machine but they are minor. There was a white powdery substance but it was easy to brush and blow away with some cleaning tools. The back panel of the machine also had a flimsy bend to it, but the metal itself seems a bit flexible in that area and was able to be pushed back without any visible damage.

In the meanwhile of just owning the machine for a day, it will be purposed as an inexpensive game/media server. The price of 32gb of DDR4 ram and a fairly powerful 9th gen i7, this can't be beat for value and similar custom builds will easily go over the cost of a $450 machine.

Everything considered even if several generations old, I would recommend this machine if the package included everything as mentioned prior. One should expect that this isn't going to play much more than light games or be a strong desktop for office use or a game server without a proper gaming GPU. Options in a SFF are limited and these discrete GPU are likely not worth the price and extra power strain on the system. You would be better getting a regular sized case for gaming purposes.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is my first Chromebook, and overall I’m quite pleased with the purchase. I’m mainly going to be using it for basic internet browsing and writing, so when I was shopping for the right model I was favoring cost, weight and battery life over other features like screen size and processing power. I ultimately felt this was the best balance of weight and battery life for the price. I definitely wasn’t wrong about the battery life. I’m amazed. This thing lasts and lasts. It’s not the fastest computer but it suffices for my use case.

Two things that bother me.

This first is the lack of an illuminated keyboard. I knew it lacked one going into it, so I can’t complain that much. I just didn’t realize how much I’ve come to rely on it on my other laptops. I’m often using the computer in dark environments, where it’s difficult to see the keys. Again, I knew this wasn’t an included feature, so this isn’t really a complaint as much as something to give extra consideration to before purchasing. With that being said, even with the lack of the illuminated keyboard, I don’t regret the purchase, and would buy again.

Which takes me to the second point. There is an issue with some of the video playback. In extra bright scenes in videos on YouTube and elsewhere, there is some discoloration in the highlights. Meaning, that in certain areas of the video, particularly that are white, there is some blue artifacts/pixelation happening. I have confirmed that this is an issue with this model and have seen it replicated in floor models at Best Buy and heard other people complain about this. I’m frustrated that HP has allowed this to continue to be a problem without offering a fix. As I said, most of my use cases involve writing; so video watching isn’t high up on my list of priorities. If it was, this would be a much bigger problem for me.

Overall, I’m pleased with the purchase given the price, and recommend it for anybody who is looking for an inexpensive, long battery life Chromebook option.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
These small, inexpensive Windows laptops are disappearing. It looks like 95% of the market in this segment has been taken over by by Chromebooks. If you find Chromebooks even more obnoxious than Windows machines, read on.

I don't want to travel around with a $600 laptop, so this cheaper, lightweight machine is perfect for traveling, and possibly getting stolen or lost.

It was no trouble to disable "S" mode. Instructions are readily available on the internet. I disabled it on the first try.

Some things I like: There are LED lights for both "power" and "caps lock." Though the keyboard is not lighted, the "enter" key is painted fluorescent green around the rim, which makes it easy to see in dim light. The response from the 128GB SSD is pretty snappy, and better than I expected. The screen is matte, which is good -- not glossy. The power supply is small, about the size of a standard cell phone charging block.

It took about 30 minutes to get Windows 11 going the first time.

On the first charge, I ran the laptop for about 3 hours straight, always doing something, and used about 35% of the charge. This looks more than adequate for the tasks I do.

There was approximately 80GB of free space on the 128GB SSD, since Windows takes up a good chunk of it. That's still plenty, since you are unlikely to install any giant games.

About the only downside I see is that it gets a little warmer than my previous laptop when doing a lot of work. Not hot - just warm. When it's idling or under low usage, it's nearly at room temperature. But the N4500 processor is about 3X faster, so this is not a factor to drop the score. The processor in this 2024 model is also significantly better than the one in the 2023 model.

No problems encountered thus far. I am very pleased with this machine.

UPDATE: After three days, I ran into a problem -- but it has to do with the dreadful Windows 11, not the ASUS laptop itself. The Windows version that came installed was two years out of date (V22H2). When I attempted to update, the update downloaded, but then failed to install, giving a message that Windows had reached the end of its service life. Attempting the update again gave no relief. In short, this is a problem with TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. This was solved by referencing the excellent article by Konstantinos Tsoukalas. Just do an internet search for "Windows has reached the end of service but not updating."

Another "problem" was that W11 was using 3.1GB of the 4GB on the machine when the machine was just sitting there idling. The CPU load was running at 20%. I used the REVO uninstaller to get rid of three-fourths of the Windows apps, and all of the ASUS bloatware (which was fairly minimal). This brought the idling memory usage down to 1.7GB and the CPU load down to 10%. Quite significant.

Still very happy with the laptop, itself!

text:
An Amazing Device, Lightweight yet durable But Not Your Average Laptop: Understanding the Chromebook Duet
​The Lenovo Chromebook Duet Gen 9 is a great device a truly excellent piece of kit, I must say. When I was told it was somewhat different from a traditional laptop, I didn't quite grasp the full extent of the difference, but having now purchased it, I've come to a firm conclusion about what those differences are.
​While it is superb, there are a few things to note for anyone used to a standard laptop keyboard:
​No Caps Lock: There isn't a dedicated Caps Lock key like on a regular keyboard.
​Touchpad 'Right-Click': You won't find a conventional right-click button. To perform this function using the touchpad, you need to double-tap with both fingers instead.
​Missing Delete Key: There is no dedicated Delete button on the keyboard, meaning familiar shortcuts must be performed in a different manner.
​Because of these differences, you'll need to learn or become much more familiar with keyboard shortcuts to manoeuvre around different pages and sites. This is a bit of a learning curve, which can be quite fun if you're keen on shortcuts, though perhaps less so if you're not!
​Versatility and Value: Why the Duet Stands Out
​Setting up the Duet was simply magic, operating almost like the click of a button—fast and effortless. This ease of use ties perfectly into the Google ecosystem. With Google being the main operating system, backing up anything from an old device, or moving data from this Duet to a future device, is reassuringly simple and seamless. This process already looks far easier than with my old tablet keyboard kind of laptop.
​The device itself is fantastic because it works great as both a laptop and a tablet. In fact, it has successfully replaced my old tablet keyboard kind of laptop, which I was very attached to! The Duet is very similar in shape and feel to that device, but it is arguably a better device and was certainly cheaper than the newest upgrade to that kind of laptop.
​If your primary usage is watching YouTube, connecting to your Bluetooth speaker for music and videos, Google searching, and playing light games from the Google Play Store, this is the perfect option for you. It's also great for drawing or writing out notes by hand because it can effortlessly turn those handwritten notes into text documents. If you love Google as a browser engine and enjoy the look and feel of how the Google ecosystem works, this device is a fantastic fit.
​In terms of value, this is your best, cheapest bet for similar functionality. If you are not looking to spend thousands or even a thousand on a new laptop or a more formidable tablet keyboard kind of laptop, this is a great upgrade that offers the same core functionality without the hefty price tag.
​A quick note on gaming: Some games you find in the Google Play Store are designed specifically for the standard phone format, so they may not look terribly great on the larger screen here. On a much brighter note, it does come with a built-in camera privacy cover, which is awfully convenient and means you don't have to bother buying an additional accessory!
​The Stylus Situation
​If, like me, you purchased a stylus pen separately as an addition to this device, be warned about the magnet. While it's lovely to have the function of the pen sticking to the back of the Chromebook so you don't misplace it when it's stationary, the magnet itself is simply not very strong. If you pick up your Chromebook with the pen attached, it will come tumbling off. Expecting it to stay put like a fridge magnet while you're either walking around or even just picking it up for a quick second is definitely not the case. If you intend to carry the stylus around, you will certainly need to invest in a case with a dedicated pen holder.
​A Word of Warning on Accessories
​Do be warned that the accessories for this particular device are very specifically fitted. If you're like me and assume that accessories for a similar-sized device might fit, be cautious! A mere few millimetres' difference will absolutely make all the difference. You are much better off purchasing accessories that specifically state they are for the Lenovo Duet Chromebook Gen 9 rather than something in a similar category, otherwise, you'll likely find yourself returning and exchanging things.

As far as the type cover goes, it's quite serviceable though I find myself not a fan of the touchpad. The cover magnetically attaches just like with a Microsoft Surface or iPad and functions reliably. I have also found that flipping the cover back it magnetically attaches to the back of the tablet which is absolutely awesome. Alternatively you can separate it from the tablet completely.

The kickstand is actually a magnetic back plate which holds quite securely but can also be separated for those times you don't want it.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is my first Chromebook, and overall I’m quite pleased with the purchase. I’m mainly going to be using it for basic internet browsing and writing, so when I was shopping for the right model I was favoring cost, weight and battery life over other features like screen size and processing power. I ultimately felt this was the best balance of weight and battery life for the price. I definitely wasn’t wrong about the battery life. I’m amazed. This thing lasts and lasts. It’s not the fastest computer but it suffices for my use case.

Two things that bother me.

This first is the lack of an illuminated keyboard. I knew it lacked one going into it, so I can’t complain that much. I just didn’t realize how much I’ve come to rely on it on my other laptops. I’m often using the computer in dark environments, where it’s difficult to see the keys. Again, I knew this wasn’t an included feature, so this isn’t really a complaint as much as something to give extra consideration to before purchasing. With that being said, even with the lack of the illuminated keyboard, I don’t regret the purchase, and would buy again.

Which takes me to the second point. There is an issue with some of the video playback. In extra bright scenes in videos on YouTube and elsewhere, there is some discoloration in the highlights. Meaning, that in certain areas of the video, particularly that are white, there is some blue artifacts/pixelation happening. I have confirmed that this is an issue with this model and have seen it replicated in floor models at Best Buy and heard other people complain about this. I’m frustrated that HP has allowed this to continue to be a problem without offering a fix. As I said, most of my use cases involve writing; so video watching isn’t high up on my list of priorities. If it was, this would be a much bigger problem for me.

Overall, I’m pleased with the purchase given the price, and recommend it for anybody who is looking for an inexpensive, long battery life Chromebook option.

text:
To start off, I just want to say this as it is crucial to the review. I have only had this computer for a day.
My rating is based on the (description vs product.)

So with that said, I shall begin to go over what I have come to notice and what I really think as an opinion.
When I initially bought this computer, there had been a few options available with 3 different price points.
After the purchase was made, I noticed a description change. It's original description stated it was 12G Ram.

The now current modification of the title and description now shows 8gb Ram.
Also the 3 options are no longer present. I feel in a way ripped off by that fact.
However, upon receiving the product I had noted there was also another discrepancy involving the description.

There is a sticker on this inside of the laptop, posted left side corner below the keyboard.
This sticker labels the computer with a Radeon Graphics Card installed. Only the base form Amd Radeon TM no other indicator of anything else, besides the description. The description specifies a Intel hd 400 which is short for intel hd 4000, just a typo. This appears to be completely wrong.

I do not mind the graphics card installed, however, it is a base form of Radeon, and it is slightly worse than intel hd 4000. Not by a huge margin, but I feel it is not appropriate to list it as something else when it most certainly is not. This is especially the case with the CPU processor itself being able to handle a better Gpu in general. I feel this laptop would function much better with a Vega 6 instead. Even the intel 4000 would be slightly better.

With all that said, I offer this a 2.5 star if I could, however I will stick with a 3 only because its overall design is quite good and it is very sleek. The screen is not the best, as this is a 2008 model laptop with an older screen and an older graphics card, the only thing new in this, would be the Processor itself, being made in 2022.

(Edit)---- I have done some test and resolved alot of the issues previously described, the description still remains a problem, however, I have tested this computer out and found it is actually better that originally stated. I would offer it a 3.5/4 stars possibly. The only issue that remains still is the lack of screen quality. It is rather difficult to see honestly, turning the brightness all the way up is really the only alternative to fix this issue.

Anyways, I have discovered with a few game test using the loggings offered by AMD, this computer actually has a Radeon Vega 7 Processor integrated right into the Processor. This is actually a very good computer on the inside for the most part. That has raised its functionality up by 200% and honestly, if this computer had a better screen, it could be sold for about $450 and be pretty decent of a computer. You could use this for games or just general work for either a job or for contracting. (Office stuff)
The specs of this computer for the price, totally worth it.

text:
Dear HP, why has your printer quality dropped so much?

I have Only owned HP printers for as long as i can remember, mostly having good success with them. The best printer i ever had was my first, a Deskjet from the 90's. While the color wasn't the premium level they have today (so they say), i used that thing like mad for more than 6 years.
After that one, each NEW printer lasted less than the one before that. My last one was the HP ENVY 6055e (purchased in 2023). It lasted me 1 year and the #1 reason i got rid of it was same issue i'm having today with the Smart Tank.
Before the 6055e was an Envy Photo 7858 (purchased in 2021); I really liked how well everything looked when printed, but i struggled to get it to print after a year. In the end i was hand feeding it every time to make it work. My brother has that printer and still hand feeds each sheet.

The Smart Tank 5101 I purchased on April 14, 2025 (currently doing the review 7 months later).
I got this for 2 reasons: 1) to fix the paper load issue, and 2)I was hoping to print my own designed sublimations to press on to shirts.
Well, not even a year yet and by far, this is the worst HP Printer i have ever owned. I waited this long to do the review as i really wanted it to work out and at nearly $200, i had my fingers crossed.
30 minutes now trying to print TWO LABELS and the printer finally fed the label sheet, but then it spit it out with nothing on it. I'm back to trying to get this to print
The gravity feed on the Smart Tank i thought would make things better, but if anything it's worse. No matter how many pages i stick in, 1, 20 or 40, it doesn't matter as majority of the time i can't get anything to print. Paper, labels, card stock, doesn't matter thick or thin, i find myself having to fight 20+ minutes to print ONE page.

I've tried talking to HP reps and they explain how to do the cleaning maintenance, something i've done with these for 25+ years and to load more paper into the feed. I don't have any more that i could even load this thing with; this is just insanity.

On this Smart Tank, i thought maybe it's like the others and i need to clean off the wheels. Uh, there's no easy way to clean the rollers as there are no panels on the bottom or back that come off. As a matter of fact, if you have a jam, the only way to get in is thru the front panel (and no the scanner bed does not lift open); best have some long pliers or tweezers to reach in there, especially if you have big hands
They do have a display for errors and print info, but it's just symbols, no words and is on the top, in the middle of the printer. If i want to attempt to read it, i have no choice but to stand up to look directly down at it; you can't read it from any other angle. The old printers had it on the front face and had words.
I can't get these labels to print. Even removed the label sheet, still nothing.
Those 1-star reviews for this printer are increasing and now i know why.

Holy Wait Time Batman, it finally loaded and started printing; 45 minutes to print one sheet.
It's a good thing i didn't have a hammer in this room, as the ungentle persuasion was a thought for a while. The page i got to print, was not my 2 labels i needed. I just said to heck with it and printed a full sheet on glossy photo paper and it printed. I tried for a second page, just as a test and NOPE, back to the same issues as before. I give up.
This was the first printer in a long time that i got Brand New, not a refurbished model and did not up for the extended warranty, which in the end is gonna cost me dearly.

I have 2 HP OMEN PCs and like them both, they have worked great and are chuck full of name brand components.
As for the Smart Tank if anyone else gets this, i hope you don't have the same issues because it is so frustrating.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
😡 A Nightmare in a Box: The HP Smart Tank 5101 is a Total Fail
Purchasing the HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Ink Tank as a gift turned out to be an absolute disaster. It's not just a bad printer; it's a useless paperweight that has caused nothing but frustration, especially since it was a gift sent out of the country and is now impossible to return.
Key Failure Points: A Litany of Errors
This machine failed at the most basic tasks, making its "Wireless All-in-One" designation an outright lie:
• Driver Installation Hell: The drivers would not upload properly, no matter how many times I tried to download the official software or troubleshoot. The setup process was essentially dead on arrival.
• Zero Wireless Connectivity: It will not connect to WiFi. The "Wireless" feature is non-existent. Without a successful connection or working drivers, it's impossible to even begin using the print functions.
• Spooling Issues Before First Use: The print queue, or spooling, seems to be fundamentally flawed or permanently confused. Even when attempting simple test pages (or maybe just because the drivers failed), the system threw up errors suggesting a spooling issue. How a brand-new machine can have spooler problems when it's never successfully printed is beyond comprehension.
The Final Insult: A Costly, Unreturnable Brick
This printer was purchased and sent out of the country as a gift, received in December 2024. Because it never worked from the moment it was unboxed and we are now too far away for a return, this "gift" has become an expensive piece of junk. It's utterly unacceptable that a major brand like HP sells a product this defective. Do not buy this printer. Save your money, time, and sanity.
I gave it 1 star because that was only low option!

text:
I have had this computer exactly one month today (2/18/24). It has performed well and has all the features that PCOnline said it would have. This is the second computer I have purchased from PCOnline and I have been pleased with their upgraded computer products and great shipping!
I purchased the 1TB SSD/16Gb Ram model with an Intel i5 processor. This processor is quite fast and will meet the needs of most of the customers buying the computer. You could "jump up" to the i7 processor but the difference in cost is really not worth it unless you are doing a great deal of heavy duty gamming or video work/processing/watching.
The computer is fine. Remember, it is NOT a 2024 model and it has been modified by the seller. The seller has done a great job in upgrading the item, however. It appears they are using all Intel and HP parts for their upgrades. Also, you can actually call the seller if you have questions. I will purchase another computer from PCOnline in the near future.
The computer is very good. Windows 11 is a pain in the ass! The computer is easy to set up but you must take your time when using the Windows 11 Home software. Many things you will need to use in set up are BURIED deep inside many of the settings menus. Just take your time, chill out and you will be fine.
If you are familiar with all of the settings menus in Windows 10 you will be wayyyyyyyyyyy ahead of the game.
Be sure to go INSIDE the computer menus and record the serial number and all of the other identifying information regarding the computer. You may need this in the future. Remember, the SELLER has MODIFIED the computer, NOT the manufacturer. The seller did a great job, but you never know what could happen in the future (you will probably not want to mail you computer to some distant site for repair if needed). HP will probably not want to do warranty repairs on your new computer because it has been modified.
So, to make a long story short; this computer is quite nice, works well and was modified correctly. The seller PCOnline is a reputable vendor (has been for me, twice) and all seems to be working well after one month of use. I will update later if there are any problems.
Go ahead and purchase it!
P.S. The first computer I bought from PCOnline was fairly advanced laptop that cost $1,200.00 +. That purchase was made about 11/2 years ago and the computer is still working well. It too was an HP.

text:
I love this computer, very happy with the large amount of RAM and fast SSD. It meets all of my portable needs. It's super fast boot (even with "fast boot" turned off for the reasons below), large SSD, lots of RAM and beautiful touchscreen make this a fantastic computer for most people.

The only thing of note is that HP ships this thing with "fast boot" turned on, which means when you perform a "shutdown" of the computer, it is actually hibernating and still using the battery. If you are using it untethered from the power brick, the battery will be close to empty if you leave it in this state overnight. Uncheck the "fast boot" option is Settings and you can preserve your battery when you shut down the computer.

Super happy with the purchase.

text:
This computer does a great job on most everything you would want it to do. I have the 1TB, 32 GB model and it runs very well and is very fast with the Intel i5 processor. In my opinion, for the difference in money, the i5 will suit most everyone's needs unless you are doing video editing and/or other advanced processes.
Remember, this IS an HP computer. It IS NOT a factory HP computer in that it has been modified by PCOnline. What this means is that HP will not honor the factory warranty on it if you send it in for repairs. HP WILL help you with telephone support and questions you may have. BE SURE TO GO THROUGH THE BIOS AND GET THE REAL SERIAL NUMBER!!!!!! If you do not have the real serial number HP will not help you! The number you receive from PCOnline is not the factory serial number, it is their serial number.
These computers fall under the Essentials model line. This is the basic model that HP sells. The next up are Pavillion and the Envy lines on most of their laptops. Don't worry--the "guts" of ALL of the computers are HP and proprietary in nature. The only real difference is that Essential computers have plastic bodies and not quite as fancy keyboards. However, most consumers will NEVER miss these options.
This computer with 32 GB RAM and 1 TB SSD storage is very fast and does a great job! This is the THIRD computer I have purchased from PCOnline and I have been very happy with their service and products.
You indeed will find that Windows 11 IS glitchy and a "pain in the ass". Once you get your computer set up it is not too bad. But, the "learning curve" for Windows 11 for an average person will certainly be a couple of months, at least. Just take your time and reference the internet as you learn how to use your new computer.
Also, download and install REVOUNINSTALLER and go to the YouTube video series "Ask Leo" regarding RevoUninstaller--that source will tell you a great deal about the software, how to use it and how important it can be.
Good luck!

It’s an elegant design that takes a wholistic approach to be as fast as it can be with the components it has and as cool as it can be while saving on power. It looks like it has 2 4gb ram chips so it can take advantage of the dual channel bump in speed. The display is actually 1920 x 1080 so that was a pleasant surprise. If you can get past your ocd about ram like I did and use it like a productivity laptop to do actual work it should be fine. I’ve barely turned it on but so far it has been pleasantly smooth. Hablando de su construcción. Cumple en líneas generales y pienso que por este lado está ok. Su peso está bastante bueno y que sea una netbook la hace superportátil. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: My stepdad-- who is not at all tech savvy -- needed a basic computer for checking his e-mail. He had been using an old laptop his sister had given him, growing more frustrated with its poor performance and overall lack of versatility, so I suggested he upgrade to something better. He did not need, nor was he interested, in a state of the art, hi-tech computer with all the bells/whistles, so I checked out the refurbished computers here on Amazon. This was my first time ordering a renewed PC and I took a leap of faith-- given my outstanding, years-long experiences buying from Amazon as well as the 90-day $$ back guarantee -- and ordered this HP ProDesk. Took it over to his house yesterday and set it up for him--WAHWAHWEEEWAH, I was blown away by how nice it was, especially for the price. It looked brand new. I had ordered a separate 27" monitor (will review that as well). Unboxing everything and setting it up took probably 15-20 minutes and consisted of mostly plugging in cables and cords. Although I still gave it 5 stars, it wasn't all peachy, however, so please be aware of the following: 1. The power cord is really short-- I think it was 24"? (I wish I had measured it), and we had to move his desk a significant distance to be closer to the wall outlet -- okay, an extension cord would have helped but stepdad just didn't have one on hand. 2. There was no HDMI port to connect the monitor to the computer -- we tried every port on the PC, to no avail. We figured out that the only way to connect monitor to PC was through a VGA cord-- not included with either the monitor or the PC. This necessitated a run to Best Buy where thankfully they had such a cord (you guys are the best!), $14.99 and yes, it worked perfectly. When that monitor screen lit up and displayed the Windows logo we both let out a whoop of joy, that's how good it looked. I went ahead and set up the starting questions for him and we connected the PC with the ethernet cable to his router (or was it the modem? not sure, but it worked) and he was in business. Absolutely fabulous, despite the 2 snafus we encountered with the short power cord and the lack of HDMI port on PC. Totally worth it, and I'm even considering chucking my old PC here at home -- which I purchased new, cost over $1000-- and "upgrading" to a computer exactly like this one. On an amusing side note-- the box that the computer came in is the perfect size for an adult cat to sleep in. As soon as I took the PC out and into the home office, within 5 minutes, Fluffy was in that box sound asleep, on top of the packing materials. Highly recommend this product! Even if you don't have a cat! :)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have been building/buying computers for forty years, starting with an Altair back in the day. My previous purchase in 2006 was a 64-bit Compaq/HP unit running XP, which I modified to a dual-boot XP/Win 7 machine. Though slow, it worked OK and I didn't give up on it until the BIOS failed recently, and it can't run Win 10. This guy is 4-12 times as fast (see Passmark CPU), with USB 3.0, four 6 GPS SATA ports and, last but not least, a virgin Win 10 (with its COA sticker on the side) which will be needed as Win 7 goes unsupported next year. An encouraging side note: Win 10 backs off a bit from the smartphone-like Win 8 interface -- though that's still lurking when you hit Start -- resembling Win 7 more than Win 8 did. You would pay over half the price of this machine just to purchase Win 10 alone.

Mine came with a 500 GB HDD and a SATA DVD reader, which I need to load my legacy software and photo discs. Two of the four RAM slots are stuffed to make 8 GB of memory. I'm not a gamer, but the Intel i5-4590 is quite competent; with more RAM, a video card in an open slot and an SSD in the empty drive bay, it should do fine. A new puter like this would run over twice as much. This one? Hard to tell that it's not new, it's that clean. And quiet. Since it was a business machine, it lacks two small but important touches: a WiFi connection and an XD card reader, which are cheap. I have two USB WiFi dongles already, and what with four USBs on the front (two are USB 3.0) and six on the back, there's plenty of ports. The HDMI outputs use HP's proprietary connector, so you'll need a special cable/adapter if they are used. There is also a VGA video OUT (won't see those much longer), which I use for my display as I'm already using its HDMI IN for DirecTV. (1920x1080 is the highest resolution supported by the integrated Intel graphics.)

In short: If you need an inexpensive, powerful and flexible Win 10 desktop to replace your old one, this is it.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The HP Color LaserJet Pro MFP 3301sdw is a dependable all-in-one color laser printer built with small offices in mind. It combines printing, scanning, and copying into a compact machine that feels sturdy and professional right out of the box.
Print quality is where this printer really stands out. Black text is sharp and clean, and color graphics come out vibrant without looking oversaturated. It handles reports, marketing materials, and everyday office documents with consistent results. Automatic duplex (two-sided) printing is fast and smooth, which helps cut down on paper use.
Setup is straightforward, especially over Wi-Fi. Once connected, it works well with computers and mobile devices, making it easy for multiple people to share. The automatic document feeder (ADF) is a big time-saver for scanning or copying multi-page documents.
Performance is solid for a small workgroup. It prints quickly enough to keep up with regular office tasks without feeling sluggish. For most small businesses or home offices, it offers more than enough speed and capacity.
That said, there are a few trade-offs. The starter toner cartridges don’t last long, and replacement toner can be expensive, which is typical for color laser printers. Some users may also experience occasional wireless hiccups, though these are usually manageable with basic troubleshooting.

Bottom Line
If you need a reliable, professional-quality color laser printer for a small office or busy home workspace, the HP Color LaserJet Pro MFP 3301sdw is a strong choice. It delivers excellent print quality, useful productivity features, and dependable performance — just be prepared for ongoing toner costs.

I’ve been using laser printers since they first became available, both black-and-white and color. For the first time since Apple stopped making laser printers—a long time ago, I’ll grant you—I’ve found a printer at this price point that delivers print quality worthy of much larger machines.

I tested it on both text and images, and it could almost be described as a *graphics-grade laser printer*: the colors are highly accurate, and the print quality is remarkably sharp.

Among the positives is the initial setup, which features a very nice color display and a simple, step-by-step guided installation process.

macOS users will find the HP Easy Scan app in the App Store, which allows you to import documents directly to your Mac. That’s also where you’ll find the app used to manage the printer itself (HP Print & Support).

The only real downside is the price of the toner cartridges, which is frankly excessive for this type of printer. That said, it may be the trade-off for achieving such high print quality—because with laser printers, the technology matters, but so does the fineness of the toner powder.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The reality is, if you use this printer for homeschooling (or you just print things fairly often), you're going to need a rich husband (or a rich wife, I don't discriminate 😉).

I didn't try to print entire books or anything, just a few pages every day or so for normal homework assignments. I also tried printing out a couple pictures, but nothing major. It took 3 months for the printer to say that all 4 cartridges were "beyond low".

Buying the real HP cartridges costs ~$400 for all 4. Those cartridges are good for about 1200 pages.

Or...go buy an EcoTank 4950 and get 7500+ pages and it costs less than $100 to replace all 4 colors of ink. It literally costs less to buy a nice EcoTank printer than it does to replace the toner in this HP printer. 😔🤦‍♂️

But, since it took 3 months, we're past the return window. I'm out almost $600 on a printer that I can't afford to use. HP, if you're reading this, please let me return this!

Aside from the toner, the printer works great. My only complaint was that it was really hard to scan one page in a book because the LCD screen doesn't fold out of the way. So, where the book would normally just hang out of the scanner while you scanned one page, there wasn't really room for that. Definitely a design flaw.

P.S. If you're thinking "I'll just go buy off-brand toner and save a ton of money; no big deal", then think again! HP has specifically put chips in their OEM cartridges to prevent this, and you'll have to disable all firmware updates, wait for the latest "fake" cartridges to come out, then buy that (with firmware updates off forever) to use an off-brand. It's a pain, and the quality of the off-brand cartridges isn't great anyway. You end up with weirdness in your prints pretty frequently.

All in all, this isn't a printer for the average or even above average family. It's clearly aimed at milking businesses for toner fees over time. Just buy an EcoTank. You have been warned.

text:
Decided on a new computer to replace an old Dell Laptop that I was using as a workstation in my study. I write a lot, surf the web, and use PowerPoint and Publisher, as well as Word and Scrivener.
The old unit had gotten real slow and was not Windows 11 compliant.

There were two rather serious issues when I opened the package. 1) the included power cord was not the correct one for this computer - which uses the squared-off corners cord found on most desktop computers. The one provided has rounded corners. Not a huge problem for me as I had an old cord that I was able to use.

2) More of a headache for me was that the computer shown on the Amazon webpage had a VGA video plug as well as two of the more modern Display ports that look like HDMI ports, except one end is squared-off. This feature was what lead me to pick this computer over similar models. Instead, I found that the computer has a third Display port in place of the VGA port. I had to purchase a new cord to connect to my monitor (which in my case is an old Sony 40-inch plasma TV). About $10 bulks, but delayed setting-up the computer by a day.

Other than that, the specs are as advertised, and I got it up and running very well. Don't have much nice to say about Windows 11, but that's not the vender's fault! This is an excellent, fast machine, with lots of storage. I can recommend it regardless of the issues I encountered.

Others may not have been able to do the things I did and would have had to be involved in returns and reshipping to get back in operation. The 4 star rating is not for the quality of the system but for the QC.

So now the computer just opens in the morning after "sleeping" overnight. This computer screen is also much narrower than my last HP All-in-One computer. The screen isn't as tall. After using it for a month, I still don't like such a narrow screen. I really just don't like this computer. It works to let me do what I need to do to function ~ email, social media, on-line shopping, etc. But, I don't really like it for the reasons above. My last computer went down after 5 1/2 years, and I had to have a replacement quickly. This one looked good with features and price here on Amazon. So I ordered it. May order a different computer with a larger screen and Dolby stereo speakers .. and just use this one as a back-up. Perhaps the Windows 11 system is what made sign in so difficult ~ I won't know unless I try setting up another new computer with Windows 11. Always thought Windows 10 was super easy, and loved it. This computer will work for basics, but I would not really recommend it.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I live in a more remote location where most bargain places (recyclers, etc) won't ship at all, or want crazy $$ to ship. So this review is partially based on my limited choices... but I like this machine enough that I'd probably buy it anyway. This is perfect for the general office use I need it for.

First of all, the one I have up on my workbench now is exactly as the ad says. CPU, RAM, SSD are all correct, and test OK. Also, the machine is a lot newer than I expected. This one has a "born on" date of May 16, 2021. Based on the CPU, I was thinking it'd be a bit older.

The inside looks very very clean. Almost immaculate. The ad does not specify an optical media drive but the chassis can accommodate a slim (laptop size) drive, if you want to add one.

The shipping box was a simple affair with very strong inflated padding inside. I suggest they use a bit more tape, but the box arrived ok. Inside, there was the PC, plus power cable, USB adapters for WiFi and BT, Keyboard and Mouse, and an adapter for DP to HDMI. Really a thoughtful combination. Just make sure to look through the entire box, as these items are loose. [A small baggy for these, taped to the machine would be good idea]

Before trying to power on, I opened the case to make sure RAM wasn't jostled loose during transit or the CPU cooler hadn't come off somehow. All was fine. On powering up, my machine sputtered a bit (on/off itself a couple times) and complained about a loss of date/time. This is normal for when the CMOS battery is too low/dead. I switched it out for a good battery and all works well. (This may be frustrating for some buyers, but if you leave the machine plugged in, it won't need the battery anyway until there's a power outage)

I'm ordering 2 more and will probably order more later on too. It's a 5-star product. Maybe a wee tiny bit expensive for big metro areas, but a great deal for me where I am.

EDIT: I've now ordered quite a few of these, and the price is better than ever. Some had SSD (SATA) and some NVMe. One had an optical drive. There's a relatively recent BIOS update too. I believe this vendor is merely following the correct MS **requirements** for selling refurbished machines which generally requires putting the original OS version back in it's initial state for a new user, and must include a kyb/mouse.

I bought this I purchased this Dell Inspiron laptop in June 2024, and by October 2025 the hinge completely failed during normal, careful use.
The hinge did not loosen gradually. The plastic casing around the hinge cracked and separated, exposing internal components. This is not wear and tear or accidental damage. It is a structural design issue where the hinge is mounted into thin plastic instead of reinforced metal.
I am a careful user. The laptop was opened and closed normally and was never dropped or abused. Once the hinge failed, the laptop became unsafe to open and close without risking screen or cable damage.
After researching, I discovered this is a common problem with this model, and replacement requires disassembling the laptop and replacing major parts. This should not happen to a laptop that is barely over a year old.
For the price point, I expected basic durability. I would not recommend this model unless you are prepared for potential hinge repairs

However, I’m writing this review to share something important that buyers should know. When I checked the warranty on March 4, I found that there were less than six months remaining—even though I had just bought the device. After contacting Dell, I learned that the warranty started when the third-party seller originally purchased the laptop, not when I did. So, even though this was a new, unopened product, the warranty had already been ticking down for months.

This detail wasn’t clearly mentioned on the Amazon product page. I had no idea buying from a third-party seller on Amazon could mean getting a product with an almost expired warranty. In my opinion, this should be more transparent. It’s something I definitely wish I had known ahead of time.

Other notes: the battery life is on the shorter side, and the fans are constantly running—so it’s not the quietest laptop out there. But in terms of speed and features, it’s a solid machine. The touchscreen is smooth and responsive, and everything else feels like good quality. As a computer science major it has definately satasfied my needs so far, and this is 6 months after purchasing it

Bottom line: Great laptop, but double-check the warranty details. This isn't something most buyers expect to have to think about, but unfortunately, it matters.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Good laptop overall, but a few cons. Here's my short review.

First off, I never booted this laptop up in Windows. I installed Ubuntu 25.10 on it and EVERYTHING works out of the box. Bluetooth, Webcam, WiFi, Fingerprint Reader, etc.

The good is that at this price point most laptops have 16GB of RAM but this one has 32GB which is why I picked it. But more on that later.

Build quality is great. No it's not a Mac but this is the second new Dell I've got in about a year and as long as you avoid the cheapest ones it's amazing how far Dell has come recently.

For daily usage include office, school, web development, etc. the Ryzen CPU and integrated GPU are great. Is it a gaming laptop? No. But that's not why you would buy this computer.

In terms of AI work... yeah I'll stick to using cloud services or my NVIDIA-based workstation for that. There's nothing AI about these Ryzen AI processors except for their name.

WiFi performance is decent. About 700Mbps vs about 800Mbps on my MacBook Air M4. Your performance may vary, just including this for comparison purposes.

But... as for the RAM thing I mentioned earlier. I actually bought this laptop for its RAM. I assumed given that it advertised 32GB of RAM it would come with two 16GB sticks. I had two 8GB sticks in another computer and I was going to swap them so that the other computer had the 32GB and this one had 16GB as for what I'm using this for I don't need 32GB (but if I buy 32GB of DDR5 at retail for the other computer it's almost half the price of this entire laptop).

Well, although it was nice that this Dell was easy to open (bottom panel comes off in under two minutes with just a few philips screws), I was VERY disappointed to find that Dell used a single 32GB stick vs two 16GB sticks in this computer. The reason this matters is that even with DDR5, although it matters less than it used to, dual channel delivers better performance, especially if you're actually utilizing the integrated graphics heavily. Now, this could vary based on the batch... in the real world, the performance difference can be anything from 10% to 40% depending on what you are doing!! if you're lucky, yours will ship with 2x 16GB vs the 1x 32GB mine shipped with. But it's something to consider.
