title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
UPDATE 2/25/26:

This is still a great deal for the money. It has worked flawlessly. I'm adding a star because of the seller's behavior. RenewByte-Quality Recertified helped me quickly, efficiently and without hassling me about the problem I encountered and the solution.

I needed to implement NFS services on this system. I intentionally bought something running Pro because I anticipated this being a need. I went to activate the feature, and it wasn't there. I dug around and found that Win 11 Home had actually been installed. To me, this was a no brainer, easy think to fix knowing how the refurb market works, and it's an easy mistake to make, so shouldn't be any sweat. It took me longer working with Amazon to get a solid answer as to who specifically sold this to me through the Amazon refurb store than it did for RenewByte to solve my problem. All you need in this case is the right Product key and you can upgrade Home to Pro in-place (in case you didn't know that).

RenewByte was ON IT. As soon as I figured out it was them (and not the three other places Amazon pointed me at) they listened to the problem, understood the problem as I articulated it, and got me the right product key, which, of course, worked. My wife's system now has Win 11 Pro, not Home and all it took was a reboot to complete the process once I put the key in.

They could have, and I indeed have had other refurb groups run me around the mulberry bush to do a return because that's somehow "easier" for them when the only problem is something small like a card failed that I could replace on my own. RenewByte didn't do that. They took care of me with the least amount of friction possible.

THANK YOU, RenewByte, I will be looking to you for my future needs in this class of machine without looking at others, based on your customer service.

************************

This is a great deal for a productivity system. The unit is fast, and if you've got your MS account tied to your Windows machine, it really is an easy process to migrate systems, even from Win 10. As someone who has a heightened sense of security and data privacy I'm not a huge fan of that, but it does work super smooth.

For conducting online meetings with Teams or Zoom, MS Office work with large Word docs or Excel spreadsheets, it just cranks. The network is fast, it has plenty of USB ports and is not loud. I don't use the WiFi but it works and is decently fast. One thing I like about these Dell SFF systems is they are still expandable. There are 2 PCIe slots available, a bank of memory slots open, and I slapped a second SATA SSD for some working scratch space into the unit with zero issues.

I would imagine based on how well it performs that it could be used as a kids gaming machine. It would run Minecraft without breaking a sweat for sure, but for serious gamers you'd want something with more video capability.

I have used another one of these (though a 5070) as a linux jump server, and it works really well for that as well. It's tough to beat the price for what this system provides.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
PC sold mainly as advertised. It appeared mostly cleaned (save for some very light dust minus one star) , sealed and without odd smelling, came with some papers describing it was checked. The packaging was fairly well thought of and secured with foam corners.

The PC came with a large mouse pad, a mouse, and a keyboard. These, while serviceable aren't great to use for long term as the mouse does not have a switch nor does the keyboard. The mouse tends to turn off after 2 minutes constantly needing to be clicked on to function after it turns off. They required 1 AA and 1 AAA batteries which they did not come with. They also have their own separate dongles. In my recommendation, replace when possible with better peripherals.

As for the PC itself, it came with Windows 11 Pro as advertised. No bloatware of Dell which was nice to see just the vanilla, clean install of Windows 11. The machine is quick and responsive as expected of a machine with a 1TB NVMe drive, 32GB of DDR4 2666mhz of RAM, and a 9th gen i7 9700 with a blower style cooler. A nice addition was the power supply which is rated for an 80 Plus Platinum certification which is excellent use of power efficiency for a long term, long power on operations. the AX210 Wifi/Bluetooth module was taped to the front panel of the machine with the antenna loosely hung over the blower cooler. This was fairly sloppily put together even if it still remains functional. Though to note, the drive is of some no-name brand which is a PCIe 3.0 spec. I eventually plan to replace it with a more reputable brand but seems to be reliable for now.

There are some scuffs on the machine but they are minor. There was a white powdery substance but it was easy to brush and blow away with some cleaning tools. The back panel of the machine also had a flimsy bend to it, but the metal itself seems a bit flexible in that area and was able to be pushed back without any visible damage.

In the meanwhile of just owning the machine for a day, it will be purposed as an inexpensive game/media server. The price of 32gb of DDR4 ram and a fairly powerful 9th gen i7, this can't be beat for value and similar custom builds will easily go over the cost of a $450 machine.

Everything considered even if several generations old, I would recommend this machine if the package included everything as mentioned prior. One should expect that this isn't going to play much more than light games or be a strong desktop for office use or a game server without a proper gaming GPU. Options in a SFF are limited and these discrete GPU are likely not worth the price and extra power strain on the system. You would be better getting a regular sized case for gaming purposes.

I was actually delighted that the size was the mini size instead of the larger computer as it fits my entertainment system needs. Plays streaming video flawlessly and performs like a much larger computer. Very good price. I recommend this purchase if you are looking for a great little but powerful computer.

An update. While these computers are a very good value, I didn't check my units to ensure the advertising was accurate and the hardware adverised was actually installed. One of the two I bought came with a 2.5" SSD instead of the M2 SSD. I did not notice this until after the 90 day return period had expired. I bought an M2 SSD, installed the image and found out why they made the swap. I tried installing an image of the 2.5" drive to the M2 drive but it would not boot but I don't know why. I ended up installing a fresh copy of W11 which worked fine. It took an addition $100 to correct these issues. Wish I had noticed this in time to resolve. A non-standard power supply was provied, one designed for the older versions of laptops which is very large, and the computer complained about the non standard unit. I had to buy a new power supply from Dell to resolve this issue.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Not what I wanted. I made the mistake. I ordered this computer under the new Dell's renaming plan. I wanted the renamed Latitude, not the renamed Inspiron which this computer is, and the seller CLEARLY titled it as such. The Latitude has more ports than the Inspiron. Again, MY BAD. Why... Why me. After looking and looking and then making this mistake...GRRRR. Anyways, what a fantastic computer!! I purchased my previous computer around ~2008, so yes, I am impressed with the newest and latest. I chose the upgraded components such as the Ultra 9, 32GB the high-end LPDDR5X (I'm talking about a max of 8,533Mbps, OMG), 2TB SSD... Logi M650L mouse. This combo is so fast, I mean so fast, I can't even keep up. Just a blink of an eye and my photography program(s) run, and the task is finished.
The backlit keyboard keeps turning off and turns back on with a touch of any key. I'll have to find the way to disable this in that I want to see the keyboard when I initially place my fingers. After that, it can turn off as I know where the symbols are.
Very easy and actually very quick setup. I chose to use a thumb drive to bring my programs and data over. Recognized my printer very quickly. My home webpage already saved my 'favorites', so no problems there.
Speaker is sufficient in that I do not have to turn it up to 100, just to barely hear it. Usually, 50-55 suffices with this computer. I can actually hear the stereo separation. Even with the audio/video players equalizer, it still plays music flat. Absolutely no bass. Yes, I know this isn't a home 5,000w speaker system, but this is 2025. I would expect a laptop to sound like a mini stereo system with, I don't know, BASS... or at least better than the cheapest cellphone. Come-on.
USB ports... As stated before, I wanted the Latitude with more ports. This one has only one USB. My mouse takes that one. That's it. No more ports. Hmm, 2025 says at least 2 ports standard?? It has 2 USB-C ports. One is occupied for power, although I believe it can be used if running off of battery.
This computer gets slightly; I mean very, very, VERY slightly warm on the bottom of the left side. Hardly even noticeable unless you are actually looking for it. The fan is also very quiet. I do not notice it unless I'm looking for the noise, slightly turning my head or it speeds up Still very quiet. Other than that, I can't hear it with the awesome, no bass music playing.
Screen is crystal clear and is advertised as "Low Blue Light (Hardware Solution)". Yeah, don't ask me. It seems to work.
I love this computer...BUT, as stated previously, I wanted the Latitude. Meh, I'll have to use my USB adapter.
Only one con I see. When turning on the computer, everything loads up fast to include connecting to the internet. However, the computer is slow to allow the home webpage to connect to the internet. I don't know why. I click the internet icon and shows it, in of itself, will not connect for a good minute, although the computer itself indicates it is connected to the Wi-Fi network. Could be my non-McAfee internet security checking things out first or could be this newest and latest Wi-Fi7 but who knows. Just a minor inconvenience.
Lesson learned. Take your time and know which model you are purchasing.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a semi-budget laptop with quite a few premium features. I bought it Feb 2026 for $718 making it even more of a value then the current price which I see is over $900. I've been using it for a week so I don't know how it will hold up over time but so far I'm very impressed.

PROS

- PROCESSOR: The Intel Core Ultra 7 256V seems really fast and responsive.

- NPU: It has an integrated NPU (Neural Processing Unit) rated around 47 TOPS to accelerate AI tasks. This seems great for this price-range laptop. I didn't even expect it to come with any NPU at all.

- DISPLAY: 2.5K resolution looks really nice and seems to be 100% sRGB which shows the full color gamut. It's also anti-glare which is really nice given how many amazing OLED and glossy laptops have unfortunate amounts of glare.

- GRAPHICS: Intel Arc Graphics which are better for gaming & content creation than Intel Integrated Graphics

- STORAGE: 1 TB storage is pretty good in this price range.

- SPEAKERS: Waves MaxxAudio Output + Dolby Atmos Cores and Stereo Speakers. The sound seems fantastic for a laptop but I was coming from an Acer Aspire which had pretty awful audio.

- LID OPENING: Can open and close the lid with one hand

CONS

- PORTS: Only 1 USB-A port. I really hate this. 2 USB-A ports seem to be the standard lately. I'm going to need to start carrying around a USB hub just because of this.

- KEYBOARD PLACEMENT: The keyboard is paused back further than I'm used to. I think it's because this model prioritizes a bigger trackpad over keyboard ergonomics. That's great if you use a trackpad a lot but I always use a mouse with a laptop so I rarely touch the trackpad. Hopefully I'll get used to the new placement.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this for my girlfriend as her first computer 4 days ago (12-01-25) and today (12-05-25) the power supply literally blew up. It made a super loud pop sound and immediately shut off without warning. Upon opening it up, a white chalky looking thing came out which is typically from a capacitor. I thought at first it may have been the motherboard, but apon looking, it was fine. I took the power supply out of the pc and visually inspected it and seen nothing wrong.

I jumped the power and ground on the power supply, nothing happened. No fan or anything. So I checked with a multimeter and got 0 volts from any wire. The grounds were fine since they had 0hms.

I am a bit tech savvy so I will not be returning or sending in for warranty. I have since ordered a replacement power supply. I did not feel like packaging up everything for someone 35 dollar upgrade. It came with a 225 watt power supply and ordered a 255.

If you dont know what you're doing with computers, I suggest you get a brand new computer. Not a refurbished one. I took a chance knowing something may happened due to the seemingly never ending stream of similar instances in the reviews.

It does have rgb which is okay, it ran pretty smoothly and did run the sims on medium low graphics, the wifi adapter is pretty okay, it was doing 100+ mbps and 50+ upload. However, none of that makes it worth even 2 stars considering we've had it for 4 days.

Thanks for reading.

Updating my review: I did this, and it seems to have stopped the flashing off screen - Refresh the graphics driver: Press Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B at the same time. Your screen will flash, and this refreshes the graphics driver, which can resolve the issue. Hopefully this resolves all issues.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Alright so to begin, the only reason I won't give this bundle as of right now, 5 stars is due to a few technical errors and concerns.

I will say however that the computer bundle itself is quite nice overall. The monitor is basic but fits the needs of most. When viewing it at different angles I am also proud to say the picture clarity doesn't change. It will be viewable the same at any angle you look at it or tilt it.

The speakers have a great sound quality however the ones I received are not as depicted in the photo which is not an issue but I would like that addressed.

Now I have said a lot of good things I will even go so far to say the keyboard isn't bad. It functions and does what I want it to do. I even have it set to turn the computer on from sleep mode. However, that's where a few issues also reside.

Now I have been nice and offered 4 stars as the computer itself is lovely. But the technical issues and concern are incoming, which for some would be an automatic 3 star rating.

So first things first. Power supply. All the main issues I have are about the power supply. Upon plugging everything in and booting up this computer for the first time I did run into a issue where it didn't want to activate. It gave me an error code being a flashing yellow light on the power button. This was due to having it completely hooked up with every USB attached and display attached along with the Ajax plugged in. After removing everything and unplugging the unit, I was able to boot it up. Then it gave me no problems. I do think it might be an issue later on though ( crossing my fingers )

Onto the technical issues pertaining to power supply that are more so about the systems components and settings.

I am able to make it so the keyboard shuts off it's light displays meanwhile allowing it to wake the computer from sleep. I unfortunately am unable to do the same with mouse and the speakers also I have an issue with making their lights deactivate up on entering sleep mode

I have attempted BI0S settings to manually deactivate the ports. I have gone into advanced power settings to change the plan and USB activations. I have gone into the devices themselves and tweaked the sleep and wake modes along with updating the drivers. Nothing seems to make their lights shut off which is kinda annoying...

Now with those concerns highlighted, once again I will say this is still not a bad setup. The computer works and everything works fine. Just a few hiccups. The speakers sound lovely even though they are cheap and not the same in the picture. The mouse works and it's DPI can be changed via it's internal settings in the computer, but it doesn't have the button on it itself, nor does it have back and forward buttons like the pictures advertised, but it works. The keyboard is just fine with noncompliant from me and it is the one in the picture. The monitor is basic but isn't bad and it surprisingly does hook up via HDMi which I'm happy about, it also is the correct one. The computer looks pristine, it's systems have been checked and performance tallied and it is a functional workable machine that I hope last a long time, as long as the power supply does not act up.

Overall pretty decent.

text:
But, be ready for what you're getting. You'll receive an OLDER, ahead-of-its-time system that was probably built and sold to schools or colleges and used very little by the time it rotated back out and was replaced. Those older systems then go to a refurbisher who cleans them up, checks them out, and resells them.

That means they're in reliably-good shape when you get them, but be careful to read VERY CAREFULLY. Many of the systems you see being advertised for pennies-on-the-dollar are cheap because they aren't capable of running Windows 11 and future OS that requires TPM 2.0 (or higher). They'll be fine until about 2025, but after that, it's up to the manufacturer as to whether they will support Windows 10 or another OS on the unit.

But enough. My Optiplex 5060 arrived in a plain box that was well-suited for shipping. But, honestly, the Optiplex was the ONLY THING IN THE BOX. No power cord, no keyboard, no mouse, no driver CDs, NOTHING. So, these little units may not be for everyone.

That being said, within 3 hours of receiving the Optiplex, I had connected it up to existing keyboard, mouse, and power and was in the process of transferring all the files and apps from my old Windows 10 computer (thank you Lap-Link Mover Pro!).

After getting the Windows 11 up and running, I added a second 1 TB SDD (you'll need a SATA power splitter and an additional SATA data cable to connect to the vacant second channel SATA adapter connector on the main board to add a second SATA drive.) The main board also supports the micro-format and large-format M.2 SDD drives if you crave yet another TB or so of storage.

Don't expect much of the WiFi either. You may want to reserve the limited PCIe slots to add a Wifi-Bluetooth combo card, because the USB-based WiFi dongle I got with my system was an 802.11n which cut my WiFi speeds by 66% over my retired system running 802.11ac.

Overall, I'd give this little diamond 5 stars if it weren't for the corners cut on things like power cords and WiFi. But, as it sits, this little system was worth every penny paid and more.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I recently purchased the Dell OptiPlex 3070 SFF Small Form Factor Desktop with an Intel Core i7-9700 processor, and I’m beyond pleased with the performance and quality. Here’s a breakdown of my experience:

Performance:
The Intel Core i7-9700 8-core processor, with speeds up to 4.70GHz, delivers impressive power. I use the desktop for a variety of tasks including office work, web browsing, and light photo/video editing. It handles multitasking effortlessly, and I haven’t experienced any lag even when running several programs simultaneously. The 32GB DDR4 RAM ensures smooth operation, and I can easily switch between tabs and apps without a hitch.

Storage & Speed:
The 1TB SSD is a significant upgrade compared to traditional hard drives. It boots up quickly, and file transfers are fast and responsive. The large storage capacity is perfect for storing all my files, media, and documents without worrying about running out of space. The SSD has made a huge difference in both the overall speed of the desktop and in the responsiveness of apps and games.

Design & Build:
Being a Small Form Factor (SFF) design, this desktop is compact and fits easily on my desk. The build quality feels solid and premium. It doesn’t take up much space, but still manages to offer great performance. The front panel is neat, and the overall aesthetic of the desktop is clean and professional, making it suitable for both home and office use.

Graphics & Display:
While this model comes with Intel UHD Graphics 630, I mostly use it for work and light gaming, so it’s more than enough for my needs. It’s not a gaming powerhouse, but it handles everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming, and office work with ease. If you’re a heavy gamer or do graphic-intensive work, you might need a dedicated GPU, but for most general users, the integrated graphics are perfectly fine.

Connectivity & Features:
The Dell OptiPlex 3070 comes with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and all the essential ports you need, including USB 3.0 and HDMI for easy connectivity. The presence of DVD burner is a nice touch, as it allows me to easily read and burn discs when needed, something that’s becoming rare in newer models but still useful for certain tasks. The Windows 10 Pro version comes pre-installed, and it has been stable and easy to use.

Condition (Renewed):
This unit is renewed, but it arrived in excellent condition. There are no visible signs of wear, and the desktop works just as expected for a brand-new machine. The refurbishment process seems to have been done well, and I didn’t encounter any issues upon boot-up or while using the machine.

Overall Verdict:
The Dell OptiPlex 3070 SFF Desktop is a fantastic option for anyone looking for a powerful, compact desktop. It provides excellent performance with the Intel i7 processor, 32GB RAM, and 1TB SSD at a reasonable price, especially considering that it's a renewed unit. I highly recommend this desktop for home or office use—it’s a solid choice for anyone who needs a reliable, fast machine.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Great deal on a nice performing PC. Had I not known it was refurbished I would have thought it was a new unit. All worked just as it should. I upgraded it right away to Win11 (free), after first installing all Win10 updates. It is a lengthy process of downloading, but after initiating it I just left the machine alone for a couple hours.
The thing to look for in a refurb is not only the name of the processor, but the generation. Mine is an i7-9700k. That is a 9th generation. Many sellers are advertising i7 desktops for less, but they are earlier generations. Thus slower performance and some will not be compatible with Win11. Also it came with 32gb ram, and a terabyte solid state drive. Included are a flimsy keyboard and mouse. Both good enough for setup, but this was for my wife, so I merely swapped in her wireless keyboard/mouse from her previous machine. To make it easy on myself, I copied all her documents and photos from her original machine onto a USB external drive, and expect that is where she will store all specific files in the future on this machine. This way we use the SSD as a "swap drive"containing only the OS, and the slower external for storage. Theoretically, next time we upgrade, I won't have to copy any files. Just plug and play. Delivery was fast.

In my view, the market for used/reconditioned computers is people that upgrade piecemeal and have parts.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
I got the Dell Inspiron 5645 for Amazon Prime Day in July 2024. Since then this has been a good computer. The price was around $815, which included a protection plan, and I'd say it was worth the price. Most notably, it's more than 5 times faster than my previous fastest computer, which is really great. I put Linux on it and it has run well, though in the last month or two it's been a little glitchy. As of today it's been able to run all my Steam games, as well as a virtual machine for Windows 10.

 I have only two real complaints about it: the computer has only 2 USB A ports and only one slot for a disk drive.

 My previous computer was a Dell Inspiron 3505 I got in 2021. It had 3 USB A ports and two slots for disk drives, and only cost about $300.

 I got the 5645 on Prime Day, but I had found out it was Prime Day only about 4 or 5 hours before it ended. I had a number of things to research in that time, so I didn't really look into the 5645 as thoroughly as I'd have liked. But once I got it and discovered it only had the 2 USB's and 1 storage slot I decided I should probably send it back and get a better machine. But after a week or two of researching it didn't really seem like there was a better laptop available around that price. Apparently the laptop industry has largely decided to only put 1 storage slot and 2 USB A's in their laptops, which I consider very awful.

So I ended up keeping it.

 The lack of a second storage slot and 3rd USB A made it extremely difficult for me to install Linux (which I did largely to avoid Windows Recall). It was the first time I'd installed Linux, but these hardware limitations made it far more difficult than it should have been.

 Overall I do recommend this machine. Just know that in some regards laptop hardware quality seems lesser than it used to be.

text:
I have been a loyal Dell customer for over two decades. But after my most recent experience, I can say this with certainty. Dell is no longer the company it once was.

I purchased a high-performance Dell Inspiron computer through Amazon.ca in good faith, expecting the level of quality and after-sales support I had come to trust. What I received instead was a slap in the face wrapped in corporate excuses and systematic failure.

From the moment I activated the device, I was hit with a falsely backdated warranty that started weeks before I even received the product. Dell’s excuse was they shipped it to Amazon earlier. That is not just unfair, it is deceptive. No warning. No disclosure. Just a sneaky and silent reduction of my warranty coverage.

Then came the operating system. Windows 11 Home. On a professional-grade computer with commercial specs. No Remote Desktop, no BitLocker, no administrative tools. All the things a power user actually needs. Dell refused to upgrade or compensate. Their response was it shipped with what it was configured for. No logic. No flexibility. No care.

Then came the tech support experience. I was told with full confidence, it was not possible to connect two external monitors to my system. That was false. I later proved them wrong using a third-party StarTech adapter that worked perfectly. The Dell technician failed to know. Failed to research. Failed to assist. Case number 202706220, technician named Prashan. He insisted there was no way. And yet I found a way.

When I raised all these issues and requested fair correction, I was met with scripted apologies, pre-canned excuses and ultimately complete rejection. Warranty? No change. SupportAssist upgrade? Not happening. Windows 11 Pro upgrade? Declined. Instead they tried to sell me extra warranty and support packages, offering nothing for free to resolve their own mistakes.

This is not customer service. This is customer dismissal. And it is unforgivable. Dell today is not what it was. Their support is a wall of indifference, their policies are inflexible and their commitment to quality has eroded completely. The brand has become unrecognisable.

If you are considering a Dell product, be prepared. Be ready to be misled, ignored and blamed for their own oversights. There are far better choices out there. This is not a one-off mishap. It is systemic rot. I will never purchase another Dell product again. Not one dollar more. And I hope this review reaches someone before they go through the same mess.

Dell, you have lost a customer for life.

**Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro Computer, Intel Quad Core i5-6500T**

**Compact and Powerful—An Excellent Choice for a Home Office Setup**

I recently upgraded my home office with the Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro Computer, and it has been an outstanding addition to my workspace. This compact yet powerful machine handles all of my daily tasks with ease, making it perfect for anyone needing a reliable and efficient computer for work or personal use.

**What I Liked:**
- **Compact Design**: The first thing that stands out about the Dell OptiPlex 7050 is its incredibly compact size. It takes up minimal space on my desk, which is a big plus in a home office where space can be limited. Despite its small footprint, it doesn’t compromise on performance, making it a great option for those who need to maximize their workspace.
- **Strong Performance**: Powered by an Intel Quad Core i5-6500T processor with speeds up to 3.1GHz, this micro computer delivers excellent performance for everyday tasks. Whether I’m multitasking with multiple applications, browsing the web, or handling office work, the system runs smoothly and efficiently. The 16GB of DDR4 RAM ensures that everything runs quickly and without lag, even when working with demanding software.
- **Fast SSD Storage**: The 256GB SSD provides fast boot times and quick access to files and programs. I noticed a significant improvement in overall system responsiveness compared to my previous setup. The SSD is also more reliable and durable than traditional hard drives, adding to the longevity of the computer.
- **Windows 10 Pro**: The inclusion of Windows 10 Pro 64-bit is a great feature, offering enhanced security and administrative features that are ideal for a professional environment. The multi-language support (English/Spanish/French) adds flexibility, especially if you work in a multilingual setting or need to switch between languages.
- **Easy Setup and Connectivity**: Setting up the Dell OptiPlex 7050 was quick and straightforward. It comes with all the necessary ports, including USB 3.0, HDMI, DisplayPort, and Ethernet, making it easy to connect to peripherals like monitors, printers, and external storage devices. The built-in Wi-Fi also ensures that I stay connected without needing extra adapters.
- **Renewed, But Like New**: I was initially hesitant about purchasing a renewed product, but the OptiPlex 7050 exceeded my expectations. The computer arrived in excellent condition, with no visible wear or signs of previous use. It functions just like a brand-new machine, offering great value for a fraction of the cost.

**What I Didn’t Like:**
- **Limited Internal Storage**: While the 256GB SSD is fast and reliable, it might be on the smaller side for those who need to store a large amount of data or run multiple large programs. However, this can easily be mitigated by using external storage or cloud solutions. For most home office tasks, though, the storage capacity should be sufficient.
- **No Dedicated Graphics**: The computer uses integrated Intel HD Graphics, which are fine for general office work, web browsing, and video streaming. However, if you need to perform graphics-intensive tasks like video editing or gaming, this system might not be the best choice. That said, for typical office use, the integrated graphics perform adequately.
- **Basic Accessories**: The computer doesn’t come with a keyboard, mouse, or monitor, so you’ll need to have or purchase those separately. While this isn’t unusual for a desktop setup, it’s something to keep in mind if you’re starting from scratch. However, this also allows you to choose accessories that best fit your needs and preferences.

**Bottom Line:**
The Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro Computer is a compact, powerful, and reliable option for any home office setup. Its strong performance, fast SSD storage, and efficient multitasking capabilities make it an excellent choice for professionals who need a dependable computer for daily tasks. While the internal storage and graphics capabilities might be limiting for some specialized uses, the overall value and functionality of this renewed system are hard to beat. If you’re looking for a space-saving, high-performing computer that handles typical office work with ease, the Dell OptiPlex 7050 is a fantastic choice. I’ve been very satisfied with its performance in my home office, and it has made my workday much more efficient and enjoyable!

The OptiPlex 7050 Micro turns out to be a surprisingly capable little lab box, especially when you throw Linux on it and let it breathe. The i7-6700T may be older, but paired with 32GB of RAM, it handles Docker stacks, lightweight VMs, home-lab services, and general experimentation without breaking a sweat. For a machine roughly the size of a sandwich, it’s shockingly stable under continuous workloads—something you notice when it’s been running for days without a hiccup or thermal complaint.

In practice, it makes an excellent “utility node” for the kind of mixed tasks labs tend to accumulate: small containers, automation tools, monitoring agents, or a handful of personal services. And yes—it even runs a Minecraft server just fine. The kids don’t care that the CPU launched during the Obama administration; they care that it doesn’t lag when someone decides to dump 12 stacks of TNT. The SSD and RAM make the whole setup feel modern, and Linux has no trouble with the hardware, meaning you spend your time deploying things—not troubleshooting drivers.

Limitations are predictable and manageable: no GPU means anything graphics-heavy is off the table, and CPU-bound workloads will eventually remind you this isn’t a workstation-class chip. But for a quiet, low-power lab machine that sits on a shelf and just handles whatever odd job you give it, the 7050 Micro punches well above its weight. It’s one of those “why didn’t we repurpose these sooner?” machines—cheap to source, easy to maintain, and perfect for homelab and testing environments.

Pros
• Handles Linux, Docker, and small services extremely well
• 32GB RAM = plenty of headroom for containers and light VMs
• Quiet, low power, and stable under long uptimes
• Great for kid-friendly game servers (Minecraft, Valheim Lite, etc.)
• Inexpensive and plentiful on the refurb market

Cons
• Skylake CPU will bottleneck heavy multi-container or CI workloads
• No dedicated GPU limits certain lab scenarios
• Limited storage expansion (one M.2 slot)
• Not suitable for large databases or high-throughput services

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
A decent little PC with plenty of opportunities for upgrading. I should note - I am running Linux Mint on this machine, not Windows 10 or 11. I feel like I get better performance with a Linux distro than I do Windows. I dropped in 32 GB of DDR4 memory into the machine after purchasing it. I also swapped drive out for an SSD 1TB drive. There are two expansion slots on the motherboard. I purchased a form factor GPU, the AMD Radeon RX 550 4GB, to give me some gaming options. Its not perfect - obviously not going to run the newest games at the highest quality, but I was pleasantly surprised at the large variety of games I can run under proton on Steam. BG3 did open and run at 30 FPS at low to medium settings. Not perfect, but anything older than that should run great. Skyrim, Fallout, City Skylines, Palworld, etc. all run smoothly with no issues. For the last expansion slot, I purchased an NVME to PCI card to attach an extra SSD 1TB Drive, giving me some extra storage.

The issues I did have... there is a dead USB port on the back of the machine. Its the one right next to the Ethernet Port. Not a huge deal if that was the only thing broken, just a little frustrating. Was dead under Windows 10 and Linux Mint after I replaced the OS, so I don't think it was a driver issue. There are not many SATA ports on the main board. I think there is only one (I might need to go back and look), so if you want to expand, you will need to get a Sata expansion card or a NVME to PCI card like I did.

All and all, I've been using this as a daily driver now for about half a year. Wanted to put it through its paces before leaving a review. If you are on a budget and don't mind doing a little bit of upgrading, this is a nice little PC. It runs extremely well under Linux and I can see this thing lasting a while with enough care.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros:
* Fast, cool, and quiet. After hours of gaming with Stalker 2, Cyberpunk 2077, and BG3, max temp hit by the CPU was only 79 degrees C, and that only for a very brief time. My old ASUS Tuf would be at least ten degrees hotter after such a test. Also of note, at the end of that test, the fans do not sound like Blackhawk helicopters under military power, an annoying characteristic that both my older Asus and older HP Omen had. Test was done "vanilla" with no external cooler fans, repasting, etc.
* Nicely configured hardware. The 5060, Ryzen 7, and WD SSD drive all work well together.
* WD SSE drive, very high quality, reads at 6300 mbps.
* Second SSE slot is open.
* Caser very easy to open, well organized.
* Good build quality. The Acer feels very solid and can be opened with one hand. The unit has no "flex".
* Good gaming performance. Cyberpunk 2077 at 2K / high detail can hit 65 fps with ray tracing on and can reach well over 100 FPS with ray tracing off.
* Reasonable price and good component value. Costs $100 more than similarly configured laptops selling with 4050 GPUs, 16 GB RAM, and 512 GB HDs, machines much worse in all ways.

Neutral:
* FHD screen, fast but dim. Typical of midrange laptops. I suggest using an external monitor anyway, but if you plan on playing all the time off the laptop, you may want a better screen option, which will likely cost a lot more.
* Port selection is adequate. 3 3.2 USB As, 1 USB 4.0 C, 1 HDMI, SD card reader, headphone jack. Decent, but a Thunderbolt port and / or additional C port would be welcome.

Cons:
* Front of lid seems to be easily smudged and seems a fingerprint magnet.
* Usual annoying bloatware that needs deletion, including world's worst AV software (McFluffy).
* Need to set up / sign into MS to launch the operating system. Owners should have the option to bypass this annoying step.
* Documentation is close to non-existent, both in terms of what's in the box and what's online.
* 32GB RAM comes as two 16 GB chips, so upgrading to 64 GB means having to buy two new chips instead of one. Every PC maker seems to do this, which does not make it any less annoying. Give me one 32 GB chip, charge me $20 more.

Note: Make sure to purchase directly from Amazon. Third party sellers often void mfgr warranties by adding components themselves and some will ship returned machines as new. Amazon is the only PC seller I'd buy from on their site.

Bottom Line: Well balanced, well made, and reasonably priced for high value components.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
One strange issue I ran into is when I went to add a 2nd SSD drive - it wasn't recognized by the BIOS nor Windows. After doing some searching online, the fix was to swap the slots, switching the original SSD to the 2nd M.2 slot and the new to the 1st. You can then change the boot load order in BIOS.

Build quality seems solid. The lid opens/closes without bouncing around due to stable hinges and the weight of the base which helps hold the laptop in place.

A bit daunting at first to disassemble when upgrading/replacing battery, but it's not difficult. Be sure to have a quality set of assorted precision screwdrivers.

The black chassis gets smudgy easily even with clean hands.

Keyboard has nice tactile feel. Nice layout - not cramped or oddly arranged. The backlight is especially helpful.

I'm not a huge fan of RGB, but the colors on this really pop. It looks very nice! Custom-configurable in software, too.

The Lenovo pre-installed software is very helpful in checking for and installing driver updates, BIOS firmware, etc. It's not overly intrusive or gimmicky. McAfee software was not desired but it was simple to uninstall.

Weight is not as bad as expected. I've owned prior gaming laptops, which were much clunkier. This fits nicely in a standard 16" laptop carry case and doesn't feel like a workout to transport.

Performance is solid. I leave mine on 'balanced' and opt not to push the wattages/temps. It handles like a champ.

Have only used it for about a month now and will update this if issues arise.

Recommended.

text:
I bought this monitor to get more viewing space and the curved screen. But, it took me sometime to figure out how to get it to work properly because I am using a docking station that only support USB-C upstream at 5Gbps/100W and 2K HDMI, 4K HDMI.
This monitor has 5M pixel (3440x1440) that is equivalent to 2.5K. If your docking station only supports 2K HDMI, the image will be blurry. Once, I switch to 4K HDMI port on the docking station, the blurry image is gone. Please make sure the HDMI cable is also 4K, too. The one come with the monitor is good. After that, the image is perfect but it flicks (screen black out 2s, come back, and disappear agin) every few seconds, especially when I use Web browser. This basically make it useless. I google the problem, updated my graphic card driver, and it is still the same. I suspected upstream speed of my docking station is too slow. I search internet and it shows 5Gbps is enough for 2.5K. When I connect with my laptop Thunderbold 4 port (40 Gbps), the flicking is gone. It only happens when I connect with my laptop's USB-C 3.2/DisplayPort/PD (10 Gbps/100W) combo port. At this point, I am pretty sure it is caused by the docking station 5Gbps upstream speed. Therefore, I bought another docking station that support USB-C upstream 10Gbps/100W with 2x HDMI 4K. All problems are gone when it connects with the new docking station. By the way, the USB-C cable come with the monitor only support 5Gbps/100W so that I have to use my own USB-C cable. To sum up, it needs USB-C 3.2 DisplayPort/PD combo port (10 Gbps/100W) connection including the USB-C cable and a 4K HDMI port and cable. Overall, this is a good monitor.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Been using this monitor for a while and the screen quality and response time of the VA pixels are much better than you’d think for a monitor at this price. The 100hz refresh rate actually looks like 100hz, and on a VA panel, this is impressive. It handles all my open windows well too as I hoped for, so that’s great. I do love how an ultrawide monitor adds a TON of emersion when playing games and watching content. First thing I did when I powered on the monitor on my PC was load up the second season of The Rings of Power, which felt somewhat small on my 16:9 32” 4k monitor that I have, but only because it is recorded as an ultra-wide, so when on this monitor it filled it corner to corner, giving me a FULL-screen ultra-wide 34”. Watching ultra wide content on this thing makes it feel actually a bigger image than on a standard 16:9 43” display to be honest, or at least the same. And when playing video games, the extra FOV is pretty nice for the emersion. The monitor does show the regular drawbacks of a VA panel though, especially with penning over darker colors on a bright background, or visa-versa, you do still get the smear-y look, but as a VA panel that it is, the monitor really makes up for it with the 100hz refresh rate and a good response time (with FreeSync support — dunno about G-Sync though I haven’t tried) to mitigate this.
The colors are nothing to write home about, and the display lacks HDR, however, they are 10-bit and is seamlessly recognized by windows. So, that’s strange, it must be an 8-bit+FRC then, regardless, if you set the gamma, color, contrast/brightness settings right, it really does look like an HDR panel minus the brightness levels of course. But, in regular use, it does get very very bright still on the desk, I haven’t ever used it past 50-60% brightness, normally having it at around 30% or so with no issues seeing anything.
The stand it comes with is a bit cumbersome (albeit not as bad as a lot of other monitor stands), so I would recommend putting it on a monitor arm though.
Don’t bother getting a monitor with a higher refresh rate. 100hz at 1440p ultrawide (4k length x 1440p width), you are effectively pushing nearly the same amount of pixels as a 4k monitor, and you won’t ever get, let’s be real here, more than 100fps in almost all your games at 4k (I am using an AMD RX 6800XT), so the 100hz is more than sufficient for this. You’d benefit from a higher refresh rate for just general tasks around windows, but for games and content it is plenty.
Oh, and when viewing 16:9 content or other aspect ratios, it’s still pretty good, it’ll just have the same resolution as a non-wide screen 27” monitor with black bars on the sides. But that brings me to my last couple points, the monitor recognizing different resolutions is automatic and scales very nicely, which I haven’t had good luck with with other monitors in this price range. For example, plugging in my nintendo switch, and the display automatically scales for 1080p, which is pretty convenient (just make sure you turn off FreeSync for that…yeah that’s really dumb). Then you also have the PiP mode, which is great if you want a couple different sources you want to reference at the same time on the same screen. Would’ve been nice though to be able to set the sources side by side or something and have it properly adjust the aspect ratio…the PiP is a bit janky to be frank, albeit still works well, just keep that in mind.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Beautiful image (I believe it's a Samsung panel) but the Dell firmware and drivers are extremely buggy, are not user friendly, have some very annoying issues with Windows 11 "Power & Sleep" settings, and have probable conflicts with other PC display drivers. See below for more details:

After a "Turn screen off" timeout occurs, this display can prevent Windows 11 from turning on ANY displays currently connected to your PC. This requires you to either unplug and re-plug ALL the displays currently connected or to reset the PC and loose any unsaved work.

It also has issues going into and coming out of "Windows Sleep Mode". It will sometimes not turn off the "pixel refresh" it does while Windows is in sleep mode and the screen is on standby. This means after you turn your PC back on, your screen will be cycling through brightly colored screens every second or so "Red, Green, Blue and White" and you will need to manually turn the monitor off and on again to fix this.

And speaking of the "Pixel Refresh", this screen requires it with every 4 hours of use (this is standard and is also on my other QD-OLED display) but it WONT TELL YOU WHEN IT'S REQUIRED. No pop-up, nothing! My MSI screen FORCES the pixel refresh after 4 hours of continual use, but Dell assumes every user is going to have the screen in standby mode within every 4 hours of use or so and assumes no-one will use the display to stream more than 4 hours of video at a time. you need to manually check and run the the pixel refresh from the OSD menu (this usually takes about 3-5 minutes), and instead of turning back on when it finishes, it simply powers off and requires you to baby sit the screen and manually turn it back on when it's done.

I recommend waiting until Dell releases firmware to address these issues, or play it real safe and wait until another revision of this Display is made next year.

Dell really dropped the ball on this one.

text:
Bought two of these and had to return both. The first one arrived and had a defective wireless card and would not connect to a network, which is required to set up Win11 (no ethernet port on this laptop). So I returned it and purchased another one same day as I shipped the return because I could not wait 3 weeks for an exchange. The second one arrived 3 days later and I did manage to get it set up and it worked fine for a couple of days. Then it would no longer power on. Completely dead. Tried leaving it connected to charger overnight. Still dead next morning. So I returned that one as well. And bought an Acer instead (which works great!).

Be careful to review the return policy. Amazon does clearly states the return policy, but buyer beware. Both of my purchases were from Amazon Marketplace sellers, marked with Amazon Prime and "Shipped from Amazon". Amazon will not refund computer purchases until after they receive the item back and have time to inspect the product. Then it takes 7 days to go back to your credit card. It is not like most Prime purchases where you get the refund almost immediately after UPS scans the return package.

On my first return, it took 3 weeks. That was from Seller "Snow Bell" and I eventually got a full refund. Then the second return took another 3 weeks, so I was carrying $1200 on my credit card while having to purchase a third replacement elsewhere (another $700 on my credit card). And now I am fighting with Seller named "AmazingDeal Arrived" on the second return as they are trying to charge me a $231 "restocking fee" despite the fact the laptop was damaged/defective and the restocking fee is inapplicable. Very frustrating and basically had to put $2k on my credit card and carry $1200 for 3-6 weeks waiting for refunds.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This review is for the S2725HS 27in model.

This is a very nice, high value, well featured monitor. Very well thought out and designed, and certainly a complete package sort of item in its budget friendly segment.

Aside from its clear and vibrant picture with good color accuracy and contrast ratio, its the extras here not found on many other monitors in this segment that set it apart. It features a fully adjustable stand that can be easily set for height, tilt, angle (swivel), and also rotate 180 degrees. It's base is anti-slip, which adds even more stability to an already sturdy set up. Two HDMI ports mean you can seamlessly connect two devices to the monitor, which is very nice for the casual gamer such as myself. And its built in speakers are very good for what they are. The unit lacks USB ports, a headphone jack, and has no audio in/out features otherwise. But given the quality of the audio, the less demanding user won't miss separate speaker options. The audio output quality is on par with popular, basic 2.0 computer speakers on the market today, if not quite as crisp. They're simply a convenient alternative to have, whether you want a less cluttered set up, an alternative to your current external speakers, or need an additional audio source for a connected device. As for myself, it was the former and latter. I have a very small space to work with and added a game console to it. I wanted to upgrade my aging and average monitor to go with, and this monitor made it all plug and play, no additional hardware or wiring needed. Two HDMI ports for laptop and game console, acceptable built in speakers for said game console, and it was a wrap. Simple, space efficient, and easy. I like that.

Nothing feels cheap or flimsy about this monitor, and its attractive and a bit stylish. It has nice cable management touches, and a fair enough range of adjustability concerning its set up and physical footprint. Considering its a standard FHD monitor with a 27in display, it also doesn't lack clarity or sharpness concerning its 81ppi count. It is a good, colorful, and even vibrant panel in its segment with nice clarity and good viewing angles. If you are obsessed about perfectly sharp text and inspect it with the macro lens on your cellphone to verify it meets personal standards, don't get this. Otherwise its more than fine for us regular folks. And the "Eye Comfort" rating is no joke or gimmick. It may sound silly but this monitor is almost relaxing to look at. It never bothers, strains the eyes, or fatigues. Easy to sit before and task with for hours at a time.

Good value, quality build, stylish looks, acceptable built in audio, quality panel, and easy to live with. I could have done so much worse and am glad I didn't. Very solid, budget friendly choice.

I picked this up for my home office setup and it's been a reliable workhorse. The 100Hz refresh rate makes a noticeable difference for everyday tasks — scrolling through documents, jumping between browser tabs, and video calls all feel noticeably smoother than my old 60Hz monitor. Not something I expected to care about for office work but now I can't imagine going back.

The stand is excellent — height, tilt, swivel, and pivot all feel sturdy and well-built with no wobble. I've dialed in the exact position I need for long work sessions and it stays put. The built-in 2x5W speakers also exceeded my expectations. They won't replace a dedicated speaker setup but for video calls, background music, and the occasional YouTube video they're more than adequate and save desk space.

Holding off on the fifth star because out of the box the color accuracy felt a little flat — whites are slightly cool and colors needed some manual calibration to look their best. Not a dealbreaker for a work monitor but worth noting if color precision matters to you. Once dialed in though, it's a great display at a fair price. Would recommend for anyone building a clean, capable home office setup.

text:
I didn't rate this for gaming because I don't have a video card to drive a 4K monitor at a good speed yet, but for everything else, it looks brilliant for the money.

I'm a working stiff these days, so I don't have the free time I'd like to have to play around and get everything set up just so, and I found that there are little hurdles and speed bumps along the way with these newer displays if you want to actually USE all of the fancy marketing buzzwords like HDR or Freesync or G-Sync or high frame rates or FALD (full array local dimming). I haven't gotten those all figured out just yet and the documentation and user interface aren't quite intuitive if you've never had to set those up and get them actually enabled and working correctly in real life before. They're not just "plug it in and bask in the full glory" easy yet-- you have to make sure you have the right combinations of hardware, cables, drivers, and settings between all the devices and peripherals to take full advantage of those newer features. But 4K crystal clear beautiful brilliance does pretty much work right out of the box, and at this price, even just that is worth having. It takes very little adjusting to get very realistic colors compared to my old calibrated Dell setup. I didn't even have to delve into the color calibration tool in Windows to get it fairly close to what I prefer in my lighting environment and get my pictures to look almost exactly like they looked in real life when I originally took the pictures. I don't even feel bad quite yet about not pulling out a hardware calibration tool.

So while I haven't put together all of those pieces in a way that lets me enjoy all the features and functionality of this monitor yet, I am already satisfied with my purchase even if I never take the time to make it all work at peak performance. This is a pretty darn good buy.

I've even considered picking up another one or two to replace my old 1080P monitor and at least one of my work monitors at the office because of the price to performance ratio. The only reason I haven't is because I may get my work to buy one or two for me for that, and at home I'm planning to buy one of the top of the line 4K G-Sync quantum dot monitors as my main/gaming monitor once I've upgraded my rig to push 4K really well, and it seems silly to me to buy a perfectly good monitor to only use for a few months. These are too good to waste and I don't have room on my desk for a triple monitor setup, unfortunately, or it'd be a no-brainer.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’m particular about design. It took me 5 tries to find a monitor that met my needs. Thought I’d write up a review in case it’s helpful to someone else.

No one has paid me for this review. Keep in mind I am using a monitor to extend the display of my MacBook Pro.

My needs: I am a writer and wanted to be able to have multiple pages documents open at the same time. I also do some graphic design and wanted to have true colors represented on the screen. I live in a small cabin so this monitor would also need to serve as my TV—high streaming quality and beautiful resolution is a must. They pretty much only make 4K monitors in the 27” size and those are too large for me to use as a work screen and also too large for my space. That left me trying to figure out what smaller monitor would have a high resolution--it took multiple tries. I also am sensitive to light and wanted something that wouldn’t hurt my eyes after being in front of it for long hours.

Dell 24 Plus Monitor - S2425HSM

CONS
There is no option to hook up a USB-C or thunderbolt cable on this monitor. Thus you can not charge your laptop by plugging it into the monitor.
This monitor is designed so that you plug an HDMI cable into your laptop and then into the monitor. HDMI cables are bulky and don’t bend as easily as a USB-C or Thunderbolt cable. HDMI cables do not charge your laptop. USB-C or Thunderbolt cables are more bendy and charge your laptop directly from your monitor.
You cannot have your MacBook in clamshell mode (laptop closed) without having your laptop charging cable plugged in. Thus instead of one USB-C or Thunderbolt cable you have the bulky HDMI and your laptops power cord. When I had all the cables hooked up it felt messy and it was all sort of awkwardly mashed into the desk riser I built.
The text resolution of this monitor was pretty pixilated. Downloading Better Display and creating a virtual screen helped a bit.

PROS
144Hz refresh rate
The streaming quality wasn’t as good as some of the monitors I’d try later on but it was pretty darn good! Speakers are great.
Pretty much no eye strain!
It’s so odd but I completely fell in love with this monitor despite the fact that it really didn’t meet any of my core needs. I loved the color, the sleek design and the ease of the mini joystick on the monitor itself. The menu on this monitor via the joystick was really enjoyable and adjusting the settings produced effective results (more so than the U2424HE which I’ll review next). I actually liked the menu options on this (adjusting the color, brightness, gamma, screen mode etc) better than any other monitor.
I loved the 16:9 ratio which I would return to when all was said and done.
I barely was able to return this monitor because I was weirdly attached to it. I’d say this is perfect for a high school or college student. As far as budget monitors go, this is a really great option. If it had a USB C option I doubt I would have returned it or bought a thousand other monitors trying to find the right one.

Dell UltraSharp 24" Hub Monitor - (U2424HE)
CONS
This monitor supposedly has better resolution than the Dell S2425HSM. I put them side by side and played the same show. No matter how I adjusted the settings, the U2424HE looked overly red. And the resolution wasn’t that much better, if at all. Text did appear to be slightly sharper but it wasn’t a significant difference.
Contains a USB C Port but would not allow me to put laptop into clamshell mode without having laptop power cord plugged in.
Only 60Hz refresh rate

PROS
None. I can’t recommend this for anyone.

ASUS ProArt 24” (24.1” viewable) 16:10 HDR Professional Monitor (PA248CRV)

CONS
Text still wasn’t as sharp as I’d like.
I didn’t like the screen ratio. But I didn’t know how much I would miss the 16:9 of that first Dell until I tried this one. This is more of a personal preference than a mark against the brand. It does have more vertical space if that is important to you.

PROS
It features a USB-C port (one step down from a Thunderbolt cable) that handles video, data, and charging simultaneously.
Streaming quality was decent. Better than both Dells, not as good as BenQ or Asus PA24ACRV.
Daisy chaining and comprehensive USB hub with 4 ports.
No noticeable eye strain after adjusting settings a bit.
I got very close to keeping this one but I couldn’t get over the ratio. It is a decent monitor though so I ended up giving it to a friend.

BenQ MA270U 27” 4K 3840x2160
CONS
At this point I was about at my wits end and thought that I’d have to get a 27” to get the resolution that I was after. I tried to use this as my work monitor and it was overwhelming. I know a lot of people use a 27” monitor but that was too much for me.
4K panels often require much stronger backlights to push light through those tiny pixels, which can be brutal for light-sensitive eyes in a small space. No matter what I did with the settings it was too bright. This monitor supposedly has blue light blocking technology built in. Look—if eye stain is an issue for you, what I realized is that less is more. Some of these high resolution monitors achieve true colors by using a lot of light, and no amount of filters, screen shade, night shift, blue light glasses etc, is going to help with that much light coming at you. Even when I took the opacity waaaaay down and had all the filters on I still felt like I was being radiated.
This monitor is very large and heavy. Not great for a small desk set up in a small cabin. It about crushed my desk riser.

PROS
Really beautiful colors and crisp text.
Super cool software download (from BenQ website) that allows you to adjust settings. No need for clunky buttons.
Compatibility with Apple.
I ended up giving this monitor to my partner to use as his new TV in the living room. Sitting back from it a few more feet, it’s easier to appreciate.

ASUS ProArt Display 24” (23.8 inch viewable) 1440P Professional Monitor (PA24ACRV)
This is the one I ultimately kept for myself.

CONS
My main complaint is that the physical design of the monitor feels a bit outdated. Sort of 90’s. Dell did a really great job condensing their buttons on their monitor to the one mini joystick. On the Asus monitors it’s a bunch of buttons across the bottom right side of the monitor. Feels clunky. These should be accessed through the joystick or hidden.
Speakers are pretty awful.

PROS
16:9 ratio
It has very sharp text.
The silver color of the monitor base is the same as my MacBook Pro.
USB-C Power Delivery (A step down from Thunderbolt—working great for me). I only have ONE cable plugged in to the monitor and no need for the powercord for my laptop.
Daisy Chain capability with multiple USB ports for mouse, external hard drive etc. and other types as well.
Pixel Density (123 PPI). Standard 24" monitors are usually 1080p (~93 PPI), which macOS struggles to scale, leading to "gray/blurry" text.
Much higher resolution than the Asus PA248CRV that I had tried. Text is crisp. Even crisper after implementing Better Display. Seriously try Better Display. Ask Ai how to set it up. Spending $21 for the pro version of this software can make a monitor like this feel like a much more expensive monitor because macOS assumes most of these monitors are a low-resolution screen. It doesn't use its high-quality "Retina" scaling. Using this software helps these monitors reach their potential.
This monitor has a deeper black than the Dell monitors I tried where the text appeared to be a gray. Colors are vibrant and photos are incredibly vivid.
Resolution quality is great in Adobe/Design work and during streaming. I noticed that when I’m streaming from Safari as opposed to Chrome, the quality is significantly better.

🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 Absolutely Impressive Performance for the Price!

I’ve been using the Acer Aspire 5 Slim (15.6” FHD IPS Touch, Intel Core i7-1355U, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) for a few weeks now, and I can honestly say it exceeded all my expectations. From the moment I turned it on, I was impressed by how fast, sleek, and reliable this laptop is.

First of all, the Intel Core i7-1355U combined with 16 GB of LPDDR5 RAM makes this laptop incredibly responsive. Whether I’m multitasking, running heavy applications, or browsing with multiple tabs open, everything runs smoothly and efficiently. No lag, no delays—just solid performance.

The 15.6” Full HD IPS touchscreen is another huge plus. The display is crisp, vibrant, and perfect for both work and entertainment. The touch feature adds a nice layer of convenience, especially for quick navigation or casual browsing.

Storage is lightning-fast thanks to the 512GB Gen 4 SSD, and the boot-up time is just a matter of seconds. I really appreciate how quick everything loads, which saves me a lot of time during my daily workflow.

The Intel Iris Xe graphics do a great job handling streaming, light gaming, and video editing. While it's not a gaming laptop per se, it definitely holds its own for casual use or creative projects.

I also love the backlit keyboard—perfect for working in dim environments—and the Wi-Fi 6E keeps my internet connection ultra-stable and fast.

🔋 Battery life is solid, and the overall build is slim, modern, and lightweight enough to carry around easily. It feels like a premium device without the premium price tag.

If you’re looking for a powerful, stylish, and versatile laptop at a great value, I highly recommend this Acer Aspire 5. It’s packed with features that you typically find in much more expensive machines.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have been very happy with the machine. I am using it to run some small server apps on windows and on a Linux Virtual Machine with no challenges.

I found Windows 10 Pro pre installed on the machine via a digital license that I was able to link to a Microsoft Account. I observed the network flows from the device and didn't notice anything out of ordinary.

I tested the machine with some workloads and found the cores temps would hover around 70c. I found the fan noise to be minimal during those periods. It would continue to perform the task while maintaining that temperature.

One very minor hiccup I had, my PC after the second day started telling me on the boot that the power supply was lower than rated and it would slowdown performance. I found that the machine went at a crawl.... 800 MHz on all cores. The power supply received is a 90 W supply, likely the cause was a contact got hung up from the power supply to tell the PC that it was high wattage. To work around this I used ThrottleStop app from TechPowerUp to disable the throttling caused by the PC thinking it has an indequate supply. That put all cores back to the normal speed of 2.4 GHz.
