text:
The goodish: At first I really liked this computer, I got it for some at home work and gaming (Minecraft & Valorant). It was great for work. Minecraft lagged badly in Java but once I switched to the windows/bedrock version it played smoother. Valorant seemed to play good but I don’t have great internet so it’s hard to tell & the PC would occasionally crash mid game leading to afk offenses. One thing to note is that the monitor it came with was a wall monitor, I knew there was variations to what monitor you could get but there was no info about it possibly being a wall monitor. It was actually kind of nice for me but if you live in a place that can’t have a wall monitor keep in mind it’s possible for it to come with one that only works on the wall.
The very bad:
As mentioned before it would occasionally crash completely powering down but it would always boot back up and work fine after. About 6 months after I got it the pc crashed mid use, I went to turn it back on and it popped up with a screen saying the PC needed to be recovered with a special disk. I looked up the error code and saw that sometimes that is caused by a usb or power cord not being properly connected and to unplug all cords and check their connection. I did this and In doing this found that the power cord (sent with the computer originally) had melted. For background I only use the computer 4-6 hours at max in a day and had only had the computer on for about an hour when this happened so if I was using this full time for work instead of just occasional projects I don’t know how this pc would have held up. I reached out to the pc seller and after about a week of trying to get in contact (calling and them never picking up or calling me back, them insisting on calling me and then not) they told me to simply pick up a new standard 3 prong power cord. I was obviously worried that there was a bigger issue that would lead to the pc melting a cord but did what they said. They didn’t tell me any other details like what voltage requirements it needed so I looked around and got one that matched the voltage that most on the market are, that didn’t work. I looked at the original cord and it had a different requirement and after scouring the web found one that matched it and tried it however that didn’t work either with the computer only having a flashing orange power light/nothing on screen/and the fan running loud. I then reached out to the seller again and told them this and they said to take it to a local computer repair person because my warranty had ended. Luckily I had gotten the extra asurion protection plan. I called their tech support and they told me that this usually means that the power supply unit has failed and I would need to file a claim to get a refund. I’m glad I got the protection plan but this means packing up a pc, monitor, keyboard, and mouse and shipping it to asurion in order to get an Amazon gift card refund.
Bottom line I’m in shock that in only 6 months of owning this pc the power supply unit failed and on top of that the customer support was incredibly lacking once I did experience issues.

The unit was listed as being in “Excellent” refurbished condition; however, the item I received was, at best, in “Fair” condition. The system’s original wireless/Bluetooth adapter had been removed and replaced with Wireless-N USB dongle. In the product description, this was only referred to as a generic “wireless adapter,” with no indication that it was an outdated unit/standard.

For reference, the IEEE 802.11n standard was introduced in 2009 and superseded by 802.11ac in 2013. Even under ideal conditions, 802.11n offers a theoretical maximum speed of only 600 Mbps, which is significantly slower than the performance of modern adapters. The included Bluetooth dongle is unbranded and appears to be of similarly low quality.

Additionally, the packaging was inadequate; the unit was able to slide freely inside the box. As a result, the Wireless-N adapter arrived broken, which I discovered upon opening and inspection.

I was a bit dubious about ordering this machine as the price seemed to good to be true and it was not available with Prime. I chose the free shipping option and it arrived much faster than predicted - no HST or duties payable on receipt. It was sent form the USA.

It was packed very well and the machine was very clean, the only defect that I could see was that there was a tiny ding in the case otherwise it was in perfect condition.

I ordered the Win11 version with 32GB of memory and a 512GB NVMe drive. In retrospect, I discovered that if I had chosen the Win10 version then I could have ordered it with 64GB of memory and a 1TB NVMe drive. I would have done that if I had realised that at the time, but I can add more memory later if I wish so matter.

My machine did come with on-board wifi and Bluetooth and it also came with a DVD-RW which I was not expecting. There was also the inevitable wired keyboard and mouse.

I like Dell business computers like this, they are solid and workmanlike, are not stuffed with crap software and, most importantly, Dell publishes very detailed online manuals on how to service and upgrade their hardware.

I will be using this computer mostly for software development and running a Linux VM so having lots of memory will be good.

I have been using the machine for a few weeks now with no problems and it is much faster then the Dell Optiplex 5050 that it replaces.

All in all, I am very happy with my purchase and will check out ReUse computers next time I am looking for an upgrade.

BTW. As stated, this version of the 7090 has a 10th generation Intel processor in it, a slighty later version of the 7090 has an 11th generation processor which would allow you to use somewhat faster NVMe drives (4 lanes versus 3). Otherwise I don't think that it makes a significant difference.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Shipped as a two-day prime item and arrived within that window. Nicely packaged in a non-descript box, so if left at your doorstep, no one knows the contents. Dell's own packaging is excellent. The Pc is well protected. The quick start card is a diagram of the keyboard, with an arrow pointing to the on/off button. Nothing else is supplied. On Dell's site, under the support prompt, you can download an extensive, a very extensive, owner's manual. It would be advisable to do that for future reference. Registering the PC for warranty purposes was a bit complicated. Dell has different pages, depending on which retailer you purchased the unit from. It took me three attempts to find the correct page. Registration is straight forward. In less than 30 seconds it was complete. Dell offers several diagnostic apps, one of which is preinstalled. Download the second. You will thank yourself later.

I purchased the premium model that came with the I-9 CPU and 32 Ram. That was money well spent. This is a fast, smooth PC. Setup requires some time, because of the updates waiting to be installed from both Microsoft and Dell. This is an AL/Copilot PC, so those updates are needed to maintain efficiency.
The unit is lightweight, easy to handle, whether at home, at school, at work, or traveling. Oddly, the screen is closer to being a square than a rectangle. I prefer the latter but will adjust to the difference. What Dell calls ice blue is actually a nice matte silver. Accessory ports are few but adequate. Speakers actually have a nice sound. Thru both Microsoft's and Dell's settings, the sound and the picture can be tuned to your liking. It feels sturdy. The case does not flex and it also metal. Hopefully that will protect the innards from heavy handling. It is set up for Windows Hello, if you are inclined towards that. I would have preferred a fingerprint reader, but Dell rarely offers that option. I rated this PC 4 stars, because I am currently familiarizing myself with what it is capable. To date, I am pleased and enjoying my purchase.

1/12/26-- the battery life is spectacular. Dell's claim of "all day life" are accurate. This PC is power stingy. I stream movies and after hours of play, the battery meter has hardly budged. I cannot answer how the graphics will handle power demanding games as I am not a gamer. For everyday use, including some video work, the graphics is more than adequate. Though I have fine-tuned the sound to suit my needs, it still is not where I would like it to be. Distortion is not a problem, high volume is. Ear buds may resolve that issue. Love the picture. Great choice of resolutions. Distinct coloration.

3/24/26 -- Battery life continues to amaze me. It just keeps on going and going without any noticeable drop in power. Because the speakers are small, I could not get the sound adjusted to where it suited me, so I invested in an inexpensive set of plug-in earphones. That resolved any issues I had. Keep one handy, if you stream lots of movies like I do.
Dell's support to date has been excellent in keeping both their software and drivers as well as Intel's up to date. A prompt will appear. One click is all that is needed.

finally, the backlit keyboard is not to my liking. There is little contrast between the silver keyboard and the white light. My old Dell (circa 2013) with its black keyboard doesn't have that problem.

text:
Als Kaufentscheidung für das GEEKOM GeekBook X14 Pro Laptop
standen für mich primär folgende Kriterien im Vordergrund: Laptopkategorie – OLED 2.8k Display – Performance – ausreichende SSD Speicherkapazität (2TB) bei gleichzeitiger Beachtung des Preisleistungsverhältnisses. Natürlich spielte auch der Gesamteindruck hinsichtlich Optik + Haptik, Solidität und Qualität bei gleichzeitig adäquater Akkuleistung eine mitentscheidende Rolle. Ob die vom Hersteller angegebene Akkuleistung von 16 Stunden erreicht werden, möchte ich ein wenig bezweifeln; denn gerade der relativ leistungsstarke I9 Ultra Prozessor und das 2.8k OLED-Display fordern schon ihren Tribut an Akku-Kapazität. Realistischer sind eher 10 bis 12 Stunden im Normalbetrieb - für mich aber soweit völlig ausreichend und somit okay. Mag sein, dass bei Aktivierung aller stromsparender Maßnahmen die 16 Stunden in etwa erreicht werden, aber wer will zB schon permanent bei minimalster OLED Beleuchtung mit dem Laptop arbeiten?

Ein gutes Preisleistungsverhältnis bei der Auswahl eines für mich geeigneten Laptop war ebenfalls ein wichtiges Kaufargument (gerade auch im Vergleich zu anderen Herstellern in diesem Segment, die oft mehrere hundert ..teilweise sogar bis zu 1000€ teurer sind), da ich nicht geneigt bin, überhöhte Markenpreisaufschläge zu bezahlen. Insbesondere auch die sehr gute Displayqualität mit 2.8k OLED bis zu 120Hz, sowie die darüber hinaus gehend sehr kompakte und sehr leichte Bauweise (999g) haben mich beim GeekBook völlig überzeugt. Das Laptop ist von daher besonders mobil- und reisetauglich. Ebenfalls gefällt mir das schlanke und stylisch schicke Design in Verbindung mit dem Magnesiumgehäuse, welches das Geebook Ultra zu einem ein richtigen Handschmeichler macht. Auch wenn es natürlich leistungsstärkere (aber im Vergleich wesentlich teurere) Geräte in diesem Segment gibt, steht bei mir im Vordergrund idR immer auch die Frage, wofür brauche ich so einen Laptop eigentlich im Alltagsleben? Diese Frage sollte sich natürlich ein jeder selbst ehrlich beantworten, der bereit ist, sich einen Laptop in der 1000€ bis 1500€ Kategorie (in meinem Fall ca.1350€) zu investieren. Grundsätzlich gesehen, habe ich aber in leistungs-technischer Hinsicht schon eine gewisse Tendenz in die Richtung gehend „besser haben und nicht brauchen, als brauchen und nicht haben“. Angemerkt sei noch, dass ich absolut kein Gamer bin und von daher auch keine entsprechende Spitzenleistung seitens der Hardware benötige. Wichtig für mich sind auch schnelle Datenübertragungsraten im WLAN-Bereich, da ein entsprechend hoher Datentraffic zwischen Laptop und einem NAS im WLAN stattfindet. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Two things to note, I don't often review products, and I specifically selected STG as the reseller given their positive reviews over the last 12 months, even though I paid $2.00 more and also had to wait an extra day or two for their shipping, it was well worth it.

Not to sound harsh but we as consumers should take some responsibility of what we are purchasing are also specifically who is the reseller, especially when you are buying a refurbished item. You are generally always presented with the cheapest purchase option, that doesn’t mean it is your best option, especially when it comes to refurbished items like PC’s. Keep in mind, this is not a brand-new sparkly PC with a $2K price tag, in the best-case scenario, you are buying a 5-year-old PC, that hopefully was sitting on some drones desk in nice clean office environment, which has now depreciated and is being re-sold back into the mainstream consumer market. The most important part of this process is the cleaning up, reconfiguring and packaging of the PC from its previous life to now being in your most likely, home environment.

STG did a great job of this, the PC was dust free inside, was in pristine condition and from what I can tell, they even put in a new battery on the motherboard (this is to keep the bios going when unplugged, it’s a small battery most people don’t even know exist). It was well packaged, included a very easy to follow single page guide to get Windows activated with Microsoft and they even included a keyboard and mouse for folks who might need it to get started. I will note that the PC itself only has 3 - Display Ports, I missed that in the description but that is on me, not an issue for most people so I just added an HDMI dongle. On a side note, yes, it does have plenty of USB ports, on the front and back, but also has the old school PS/2 style ports available for a mouse and keyboard for nostalgia's sake...ironically, I still have an old trackball mouse that would work on this thing lol.

After getting Windows activated, I immediately added a 2TB NVME drive for the boot drive and cloned the original 1TB SSD through Acronis, which is free to use if you use a Western Digital drive. I then added a dual port 10GB SFP+ network card, an additional 3.5” SATA drive for more storage which I had sitting around, and then added two 16GB DDR4 RAM sticks to get it up to a total of 64GB of RAM. I could not find the exact ADATA ones that came with it, but I did match up the RAM’s speed, voltage and timings to make sure it would work, and it did. Also, I did update the BIOS and some other items from Dell’s website but most people will never need to do this, and in all honesty shouldn’t. I would recommend the RAM I bought but I honestly don't know if it is the same as what came in yours and it may do more harm than good.

This is the first PC I have purchased in about 30 years, I have been building my own since I was a kid in the 90’s but I really just needed a decent PC I could RDP into, use as a management device for my network rack, and also serve as a VM host device using VirtualBox with an Ubuntu and Linux Mint VM. I know Dell is pretty solid when it comes to desktops like these, which are usually targeted at businesses, so my hope is that it just sits in my basement next to the network rack for another 5 years, if it is still running after that, it will just become a full blown linux box.

This is a great little PC as is, but with a few upgrades can be a utility device like what I did, or a light little gaming rig assuming you upgrade the PSU or get a GPU that doesn't need a lot of space or power. Just understand, this is never going to be something you overclock or turn into a 4K 120fps gaming rig, it just doesn't have the space or backbone for it, nor was it ever intended to. It draws very little power, has a nice quiet case and does have WiFi and BT built in if you need it.

text:
Gosh, where to even begin? I've been using Dell Monitors for over a decade now - regardless of what brand PC system I was using. I've always found Dell monitors to be a cut above, given what you spend.

Over the past week, one of the audio components that I had on a shelf directly above my previous Dell monitor, fell from the shelf, hit the table and bounced back into my Dell screen, smashing it - talk about a negative surprise. So I had to find a PC monitor quickly to replace it. Problem is that I needed a monitor whose height adjustment capabilities were a step above. So I called Dell, talked to a sales agent, who asked me what exactly I was looking for. I told him that my PC monitor needed to have substantial height (lowering and raising the monitor) capabilities.

After researching a variety of PC monitors, he recommended that I try the Dell S2425HS monitor, which had a height adjustment capability of 5"-6", which is phenomenal. You see, my monitor is sitting within a small nook space (height-wise), and I needed to have a monitor that would allow me to lower the screen substantially to fit into this space.

So I thanked him and immediately ordered it on Amazon - and it arrived the very next day. When it arrived, I was gratified to see the same care and packing of the monitor that Dell had always provided. Assembly was quick, and I was then surprised to discover that there were two 5-watt speakers (I don't know the actual size of the speakers) integrated inside the monitor.

After connecting everything and subsequently doing a color calibration of this new S2425HS (I do lots of photography, and I need an accurate monitor to process digital photos), I was gratified to then witness a wonderful-looking screen. As an aside, I also am an audiophile that maintains a desktop, near-field audio system around my PC. The gear used includes names such as KEF, Adcom, NAD, SMSL, and more - all providing me with a glorious audio experience while working.

And believe it or not, the biggest surprise for me - besides the excellent screen qualities of this new S2425HS - was the sound of these two 5 watt built-in speakers. In the settings menu on the monitor, you have the options to tune the sound of the integrated speakers for Movie, Music, Standard, Sports, and a few other modes. So I set mine to music, fully expecting these two little speakers to sound tinny and compressed due to their small size.

But boy was I surprised. The speakers had a fuller-bodied sound with excellent separation and an almost holographic sound quality while listening to a variety of materials. It is a good 5 steps above the typical built-in tiny speakers you get with some other monitors. This came as a welcomed treat because I periodically like to give my audiophile amps and associated electronics a rest. In fact, I was watching a band perform on YouTube just a few minutes ago, and for a second, I thought I was listening through my KEF speakers. Of course, when the bass section was performing, I realized then that I was listening to the PC monitor speakers because let's face it, those tiny speakers were limited with what they could do.

So all in all, I am absolutely delighted with this quality-made Dell S2425HS monitor. It provides superb screen and picture qualities, and also gives you the bonus of including two small, yet highly competent speakers that provide excellent sound qualities, despite their small size.

Highly recommended!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I never review my Amazon purchases, but I'm so impressed with this one I had to say something. I had an old Dell monitor that I loved for its color accuracy, but after 12 years the backlight died on me and I had to find a replacement quick and on a tight budget. I caught this one on a limited-time sale for $100, but IMO it would still be an excellent deal at full price.

1. The included stand is the most adjustable I've ever seen out of the box. Notably, it can rotate into portrait mode in _either direction_ (clockwise or counter-clockwise), which doesn't sound super impressive, but it makes things like cable management and getting a good look at the inputs much easier, even if you don't intend to leave it that way.

2. The picture quality (and adjustability via the menu) is way above and beyond my expectations. Straight out of the box it had excellent brightness and contrast but the image was way too cool (par for the course, since default configurations are usually optimized for in-store displays where they're going to be overwhelmed by bright, cool fluorescent store lights). I was able to eyeball-calibrate it to match my primary display in less than 5 minutes using just the built-in menu options. I still need to dig my Spyder out of storage and give it a proper deep-dive software calibration, but already it's good enough that I'd be comfortable doing most of my design work on this display.

3. The included I/O options are excellent. Most of the displays you'll find in this price range only have 1 HDMI and 1 VGA (?!) input, which doesn't meet the bare minimum requirements for my home-office setup, where I need to plug my personal desktop in via DisplayPort and my work laptop in (through a DisplayLink dock) via HDMI or DisplayPort. This has 2x HDMI and 1x DisplayPort input for video, plus a headphone-out (for sending audio through the HDMI or DP inputs), and it can also act as a USB hub. While I would have loved some Mini-DP inputs and DP daisy-chaining support like my old Dell had, this is plenty sufficient for my setup, and, again, really atypical for the price range.

This is a really nice monitor. It was very easy to set up. It weighs a lot less than the antiquated Samsung 4:3 monitor it replaced. The bezel is very thin, and color rendering seems excellent. There were no dead pixels. I also was pleasantly surprised to see a built in power supply instead of the ubiquitous "line lump."

The user manual is for multiple models and I wasted some time looking for the menu access buttons to change sources, adjust screen settings, etc. It turns out that with this model everything is accessed via a joystick-style arrangement on the power button. No wonder I couldn't find any discrete buttons! Samsung should really put an addendum in their instructions concerning this.

It should be noted that though the height shown is 19.59", this is with the stand fully raised. When it's fully collapsed, the actual height is much closer to 18". This might be important for someone whose available space is height constrained.

The built in headphone output was recognized immediately as another audio device, with no driver installation required. Output level is more than sufficient for earbuds and even works well with full sized headphones. I listened to some uncompressed wave files and quality seems quite good..

There are only a couple of negatives that I've found so far. One is the placement of the USB and headphone ports; it is virtually impossible to connect to these without physically tilting the monitor up, and even then it's a hassle. Second, installation would look a bit cleaner if Samsung had supplied rear exit right angles on the monitor end of both the HDMI and Display Port cables. The power cable has a right angle connector on both ends, which is great for the monitor side but may or may not be an issue when you connect it to your AC outlet (I seem to find that these always want to interfere with other plugs, or point in the opposite direction to what you need).

Overall I'm very satisfied with my purchase, and recommend this monitor.

There's not much bad to be said about this monitor. It's got great colors with three color adjustment AND six color hue and saturation adjustment. That's crazy to me at this price point. I was able to dial in the colors to where I like them without a problem. I can't get them dead on, but it's very close. It's very green-tinted and over-saturated out of the box, so be prepared for some adjusting. Viewing angles are also good, and it works fine at 120 Hz without any issues on Windows 11.

For build quality and other bits, the whole thing feels solid. The stand is made of metal and requires four screws to assemble, but there's almost no wobble. There's also no height adjustment, but it has a 100x100 VESA mount if you want to get a better stand. Audio output for my external speakers is good too, with no audible noise and plenty of volume. The single knob for menu navigation is the one point I'll put against this monitor, as multiple buttons are always better. Knobs are just finicky and annoying to use.

If you want a large 1080p monitor with good colors and a higher-than-60 Hz refresh rate, you can't go wrong here.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I paid $219 for my refurbished desktop. If I paid more, I'd be returning it for a refund, but at this price, I'm willing to deal with the issues.

There is some false advertising in the item description, and some partial truth as well. I wanted something cheap that ran windows 11 and bought this before doing all my homework. There are a couple important things to be aware of with this computer:

(this is probably the most important)
#1) this CPU isn't technically supported by windows 11 as it's a 6th gen intel processor. Windows 11 only truly supports 8th gen+ intel processors, so there's a decent chance this computer will lose support at some point in the future. There are workarounds to install Win 11 on outdated CPU's (which is probably what the refurbishers did), but it's anybody's guess as to how long they'll actually receive updates. If windows stops allowing updates on this rig, you'll need to either switch to a different OS like linux (which is my plan if I get "obsoleted") or upgrade your motherboard, CPU, and probably upgrade to DDR4 or 5 RAM, which will all cost you a couple hundred bucks or more depending on how highly you want to upgrade.

#2) this does not have DDR4 RAM. It has DDR3 RAM. I was wondering if the 6th gen processor and motherboard could handle DDR4, and I suspect the board is probably too old to handle DDR4 technology. What makes this slightly even worse, is that the task manager says all 4 slots are being used, so there are 4 cheap 4 GB DDR3 sticks, which may have an effect on stability of the system.

3) This may only affect me since my tech is generally old, but I had to buy new cords to connect to my monitor. The outputs include 2 mini-DisplayPort and 1 regular DisplayPort. I only have VGA and HDMI, so I had to order more from amazon and wait a few more days before I could get it set up.

4) the wifi and bluetooth seem unstable. They're both plugged into USB ports, rather than built in. I've had the wifi drop a few times in the ~1 hour having it up and running. Not a huge concern for me as I'll be hardwiring it in and I doubt I'll ever utilize bluetooth on it.

Having said the negative, there are a few things I do like about this desktop as well
1) good value - this comes with a decent (but kind of old) processor, a 4 gb graphics card (which is more than enough for me), a 1 TB SSD and it came with a mouse and keyboard, which feel pretty cheap but still work out of the box.
2) my kids like the LED lights. I don't love how sparkly it is, but they do.
3) if I have to switch to linux, this thing should be a plenty powerful, stable machine for a lot of years.
4) it's nice and small

text:
RAM-Wise, this thing is a beast, same for the CPU. Compared to most low-end systems, the CPU and RAM alone can outclass a lot of PCs, and most non-gaming laptops. The wifi card is so absurdly powerful it slows down other devices when downloading files, absorbing all of the bandwidth on mediocre wifi routers. But the graphics card is this sad little chip that can barely function. Most games will be forced to run on graphics settings so poor it looks like play-doh, and will run even that at 20 fps or less. Thankfully, its CPU seems to be able to pull the weight if it really struggles. This thing doesn't even start running the fan when you hit 50% CPU capacity, so heat-wise it has no issues that i've encountered. Due to its high memory and CPU power, i recommend using this system for games like Terraria and older skyrim games, Roblox games, Smaller Unity or Flash games, and many Itch.io titles. However, it will struggle to run games such as Fortnite, Apex, Valorant, Fallout 76, DOOM Eternal, or God Of War. But for the games its graphics card survives, the framerate can be buttery smooth.
4/5 stars, if it had a graphics card powerful enough for VR linking, i would gladly pay another 2-3 hundred dollars. Runs Windows 11, all ports work as intended. No parts missing.

text:
Purchasing a new computer should be a straightforward and satisfying experience, especially when buying a pre-configured system from a well-known brand like Dell. Unfortunately, my recent purchase of the Dell OptiPlex 5050 SFF from Green Tech Computers via Amazon has been anything but. What was supposed to be a reliable mini-server for my home office turned into a costly and frustrating ordeal filled with endless troubleshooting, unhelpful customer service, and a product that remains completely unusable.

Below, I’ve outlined my entire experience in detail to ensure others are aware of the challenges I faced and can make an informed decision before purchasing from this seller.

Initial Impressions and Setup
When I first received the Dell OptiPlex 5050 SFF, I was optimistic. The compact design and reputation of the OptiPlex series made it a great fit for my intended use as a mini-server for home projects. However, my optimism quickly faded once I powered on the machine.

From the start, I encountered a critical issue: the system was completely non-functional for basic tasks. I was unable to open browsers, download files, or install any updates. This wasn’t a minor glitch or software hiccup—these are basic functions that any modern computer, let alone a Dell-branded device, should be able to perform right out of the box.

Troubleshooting and Escalation
Recognizing that this wasn’t a typical setup issue, I began an extensive troubleshooting process to identify and resolve the problem. Below is a detailed timeline of my efforts:

1. Initial Troubleshooting Steps
I started by testing the system with standard diagnostics:

Ran Dell Diagnostics: The diagnostics tool reported no hardware issues, which suggested that all components were functioning as intended. However, this was contradicted by the ongoing problems.
Reinstalled Windows: Thinking the issue might be related to the pre-installed OS, I performed a clean installation of Windows 10. Unfortunately, the problems persisted. I couldn’t open browsers, download files, or install updates even after a fresh OS install.
Tested with Linux: I attempted to install Linux as an alternative operating system to bypass potential Windows-related issues. To my shock, the system wouldn’t even proceed to the installation stage, halting abruptly without any clear explanation. The live environment also failed to load. Ubuntu versions16.04, 22.04, 24 and PopOS were used.
2. Communication with Green Tech Computers
Frustrated, I reached out to the seller, Green Tech Computers, for assistance. This began a long and fruitless exchange, documented as follows:

Initial Contact (Dec 21, 2024): I informed them of the 0x80010105 error I was encountering and detailed the issues I was facing. Their response was to apologize and suggest replacing the hard drive, implying that the device had shipped with defective hardware. This was alarming—why would a new product require immediate hardware replacement?

Follow-Up Responses: Over the next several days, I provided them with screenshots of error messages and explained my troubleshooting efforts, including reinstalling Windows and attempting to update drivers. Their replies were repetitive and unhelpful. They insisted that the issue was a missing driver and suggested steps like installing updates via the store or resetting Windows Update components. None of these worked, as the system wouldn’t allow driver installations or updates to proceed.

Contradictory Advice: After reporting the continued failure of their suggestions, they shifted their diagnosis to a "defective system file" or a "Windows activation error." They advised me to download and reinstall Windows from Microsoft’s website—a step I had already performed multiple times without success.

3. Hardware Replacement Attempts
At their suggestion, I replaced the hard drive and memory with new components. I then performed another clean installation of Windows using verified installation media. Despite this, the exact same issues persisted, proving that the problem was not related to the hard drive, memory, or installation media. This confirmed that the root cause was likely a fundamental flaw in the system’s hardware or firmware.

Escalating Frustration
Poor Customer Service from Green Tech Computers
One of the most frustrating aspects of this experience was the lack of accountability or meaningful support from Green Tech Computers. Their responses were generic, dismissive, and showed little regard for the time and effort I invested in troubleshooting their faulty product. Even after replacing hardware and documenting every step of my process, their only advice was to repeat steps I had already tried or refer me back to Amazon.

Warranty Denial
To make matters worse, they refused to honor the warranty, claiming that the system was outside the 90-day warranty period. This was particularly upsetting as the delay in addressing the issue was due to customs clearance, which was beyond my control. I explained this to them and requested some leniency given the circumstances, but they flatly refused to provide any assistance, leaving me with an unusable system and no recourse.

Key Issues with the Product and Seller
1. Defective Hardware
The core problem with this system appears to be a defect in the hardware or firmware. Despite extensive troubleshooting, including replacing components and reinstalling operating systems, the system remains non-functional. This raises serious concerns about the quality control standards at Green Tech Computers.

2. Misleading Support
Throughout my correspondence with Green Tech Computers, their advice was inconsistent and unhelpful. They repeatedly blamed the issue on missing drivers or corrupted files without offering a concrete resolution. Their unwillingness to escalate the issue or take responsibility was unacceptable.

3. Warranty Limitations
Refusing to honor the warranty due to a minor delay caused by customs is an example of poor customer care. Given that the system was clearly defective from the start, Green Tech Computers should have taken ownership of the issue and offered a replacement or refund.

4. Financial Loss
In addition to the cost of the system itself, I incurred additional expenses for replacement hardware (hard drive and memory) and hours of lost time trying to resolve the issue. The total financial and emotional toll of this experience far exceeds the value of the product.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Background: We are blessed in our family to have someone who knows a lot about PCs, so we’re not overly intimidated by needing to replace things inside a PC or trouble shooting. Some of the other purchaser’s negative reviews on this machine were daunting to me though, but the price was so good for the specs, we decided to try it in spite of some of the bad reviews. We concurrently use PCs and Macs of varying ages and operating systems. This is the 2d refurbished machine we’ve ever purchased (the other refurbished PC was a $100 refurbished HP years ago from Overstock.com that’s still working great), but from the varying experiences reflected in the reviews, it may be a bit of a roll of the dice. I like that Amazon is behind this product.

Experience so far: It’s been almost two months of DAILY HEAVY USE on this PC, even creating 3D graphics using Blender, and so far this PC is working great. Very fast efficient start up. Tackles memory hog tasks such as 3D rendering with Blender software well (especially for the price of the PC). However it’s relatively early days, so I still have some doubts of longevity (mostly because of the other Amazon reviews).
So for what it’s worth, here’s my experience so far (from the reviews it appears there’s quite a bit of difference from person to person so read others reviews too). I’m writing the good and bad.
1) The PC arrived NOT well packaged for shipping, so I was dubious it wasn’t damaged. I felt the packing was so bad it disrespected the customer’s time because it seemed so likely the PC would be damaged simply because of poor packaging. For example, the exterior shipping box was damaged and the there was way too much room inside the shipping box for the PC tower to slip around. Luckily, somehow our PC survived the shipping, but the seller should fix this easy fix. Dear Seller: Please pack the PCs as if you had to use the PC yourself. Why go through all that work in refurbishing only to risk screwing it up in the shipping? -so even though the PC actually did work (hurray!), it worked in spite of the sloppy packaging, so I’d rate the packaging as needlessly carelessly bad. It also made me hope the restoration was done with more care and pride in workmanship than the packing was. Not a confidence/goodwill builder, sadly.
2). The PC arrived with a very basic keyboard that is 100% perfect for my needs (I use four computers side-by-side, so keyboard space is at a premium, so I actually love the keyboard, nice large clear letters on each key, easy to read and yet still efficiently space saving).
3) The PC arrived with a basic mouse, a bit smaller-sized but works 100% fine.
4) The PC itself looks as it should, except the seller put a BIG ugly white service sticker on top of the PC in a prominent place, not at all attractive, so I hope the seller reads this and uses more discreet sticker placement for other buyers. The ugly large white service sticker essentially kills any aesthetic/freshness the PC Tower could have.
5) The PC came with a small white wireless dongle that if you want wireless will take up one of the USB ports.
6) With great intrepidation, fearing the worst due to the poor shipping packaging, I hooked up the PC to its mouse and keyboard (and one of my monitors) and turned on the PC. EVERYTHING worked fine. The wireless dongle worked. It booted up. It was super SUPER fast. Eventually we used Ethernet cable instead of wireless Wi-Fi, and the Ethernet connection works fine too. I’ve used the PC to read CDs/DVDs and burned a test DVD just to make sure it works. It does. At least so far :)
7) Because this PC is NOT upgradable to Win 11, etc., be realistic. AFTER I felt the PC was working by running it through its paces, that’s when I bought software for it. In other words, given the negative reviews, make sure you like what you get before investing in software, BUT BEFORE YOU BUY RESEARCH THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SOFTWARE YOU USE FOR WINDOWS 10 Pro. Once you’ve run the PC through its paces, that’s when I recommend you actually buy the most recent version of the software you use that is compatible with Windows 10pro, because eventually the software companies won’t be supporting Windows 10 anymore. (By way of example, the last version of Adobe Photoshop that you could buy to own (as opposed to rent monthly) is not compatible with operating systems past Windows 7, so for the rest of my life I’ll need a Windows 7 machine to use that older Adobe software; similarly if you don’t want to pay a monthly subscription fee for Word/Excel/etc., you’ll need to buy a version of Office that is still compatible with Windows 10 pro (I bought Office 2019 Pro).
8) So this PC has worked well for me with Blender, Outlook, Excel, Word, and the operating system/computer surprisingly came pre-loaded with various software things - even an interesting 3D program (that was a happy surprise, must be part of Windows 10 pro!?!), and I’ve used the PC for the internet, and the PC networked easily to the printer, etc.
9) Eventually all PCs die/fritz. I backup at least daily to an external hard drive, because you just never know (and this is a refurbished PC, especially given the reviews, be realistic and backup backup backup.
Bottom line: This is a speedy effective PC that so far is doing what I need it to do at a great price. There are some super easy fixes the seller can do (BETTER PACKAGING FOR SHIPPING & PLACE THE SERVICE STICKER IN A LESS VISIBLE PLACE). I didn’t need to contact the seller for anything because this PC booted up easily. If everyone had my experience I’d say buy without hesitation; I wonder how many of the bad experiences could have been avoided by better packaging? In any event, so far my experience is FANTASTIC FOR THE PRICE :)
6-17-22 update: it’s still working GREAT, super fast, this morning I thought to myself what an excellent purchase this has been so far. Still FANTASTIC FOR THE PRICE. Of course, haven’t reached the year mark yet & a computer needs to function much longer than this to earn full high grades so early days still, but very happy so far.
9-7-22 update: Still turns on super fast, gets to the log in screen super fast, and then once the password is entered, the PC still gets to the main screen super fast. text:
Wow!!! A Pc for 200$!? too good to be true? (Warning long review)

So I needed a PC to hold me over while I built my main rig (so I bought this XD)
The particular model I got had an i7-4770 - 32 GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD and Windows 10 PRO
I paid 202$ but I've seen it for around 185-212$ USD
This is a Review of the Dell Optiplex 9020 MT

How It Shipped- Not good... had thin-ish bubble wrap and a box to protect it from
the FedEx driver who might dropkick it... (mine was kind- yay)

All the specs were true to the listing and it boots in around 12-16 seconds
4 Kingston DIMMs of 8GB ddr3 1333mhz (32GB) and I have had no failures yet
It also came with a Hajaan 1 TB SSD which can be had for around 60$ USD as of writing
(opinions are mixed about the quality of the SSD but I have yet to find any issue in daily use)

COOLING - a simple downdraft CPU cooler and a single fan in the back???
Okay not "great" but temps under OCCT (CPU stress test) never hit more than 90c
(during an hour-long test)
And during gaming, it never hit higher than 82c with an average of 60-75c!!!
(NOTE) the rear fan was originally set up as an exhaust (in mine)
I flipped it to become an intake and the system runs around 3c less than stock!!!
Speaking of cooling I thought as a refurbished office PC it would have a little dust from its prior life...
NOPE- it was SPOTLESS, I'm VERY appreciative of the refurbisher selling clean systems
(plus the SSD had a PROPER mount so kudos to that)

ACCESSORIES - (I'll keep it brief it's a $200 computer I know accessories won't be "amazing")
Keyboard and Mouse - light and clicky but better than nothing

Wi-Fi adapter... DO NOT USE
It gets concerningly hot under load and the MAX speed recorded by internet speed test
was 60mbs down and 30mbs up but when overheating- speeds drop to unusable levels
(and this was nearly constant) I replaced it with a TP-Link USB AC1300Mbps and have had no issues since

I know everyone will use this PC differently but here are my uses and how well it works for me

Uses and Performance!! (Before mods)

1# 1080p Video Editing
It "works" if you make small videos then it is “good” 32GB of RAM and editing off of an SSD is NUTS
However, due to weak integrated graphics export times are slow. Scrubbing can be choppy too...
(I use Wondershare Filmora, different software May utilize Hardware differently)

2# Web Browsing
It will destroy web browsing for the majority of people out there

3# Gaming...
if this is your primary concern then you might want to look elsewhere if you're not into upgrading...
HOWEVER
for light games (all 1080p low settings)
Unturned. 6 FPS Average
Roblox. 25 FPS Average
Minecraft (java) 10 FPS Average

If all you want to do is "play the games" then buy it and enjoy
However, attempting to screen record or stream from this setup would not work (assuming you have sanity)

Let's Upgrade it-
(I spent 450$ if GPU is factored in)
I added an AMD Radeon RX 5500 4GB
because of this card’s 130-watt TDP, I upgraded the PSU to a Corsair RM750e (2023)
DO NOT USE STATA TO 6/8 PIN
(the risk to your components and your home is worth more than $120 for a new PSU and Adapter)

Adapter??? Oh yeah, I should mention that a standard ATX power supply uses a 24-pin motherboard power connector and THIS Dell Optiplex uses an 8pin for motherboard power
(I paid 10$ for a 24 to 8-pin adapter)

note I got this GPU for free (yay me)
I would suggest an RX 580 8GB instead which sells for around 100$ and is about the best GPU can put in the system alternatively, you can put a GTX 1660 in here if you prefer Team Green
(all three cards are within about 6% of each other in terms of performance)
so go for whatever works for you!!!

Uses and Performance!! (After mods)

1# 1080p Video Editing
It LOVES IT
Again SSD and RAM are awesome but since I work with higher-ish production edits (think 40 - 200GB of data for a video) GPU helps and it runs well,
16 hours of gaming footage (1080p @ 60FPS) Rendered in like 3 hours
(I use Wondershare Filmora, so again different software May utilize Hardware differently)

#2 Web Browsing

#3 Gaming...
Not 300FPS AAA gamer ready but DANG
for light games (all 1080p high settings)

Unturned. 50-100 FPS
Roblox. 60 FPS, it just seems to have an FPS cap... and its PINNED
Minecraft (java) 40-70 FPS

(I want 60 as my min but I will live as this is the .1% low with the main average being shown)
I can probably stream and I use this system to record very comfortably!!!!

Now the CONS!!!! (these are all the issues I found)

1# If you didn't upgrade,
there is no built-in HDMI port for the system

FIXABLE

2# 4th gen Intel = No Windows 11
This could be a reasonable deal-breaker for some people if you like Windows,
then Windows 10 will lose its security updates in the coming year!!!

3# Very little user control even in bios!!!
this one may more apply to the Geeks but a lot of things, like XMP don't exist, and fan speed control? Dell thinks you don't need that!!!

REALLY DELL (sorry for yelling)

All of these things don't really bother me except the last one

You can get a DisplayPort to HDMI adapter for around 10$
No Windows 11 but I'm going to deploy this as a storage server later in its life running Unraid!!
There will be no Windows on the machine XD
(will update when it is a server)

TLDR: Good PC, great for very light games and web browsing
no windows 11

I was able to setup the 3rd unit in place of the 2nd one okay, but later I noticed it wasn't as quick as it should be for a computer with a 6 core i5, 16GB of ram and SSD. Task manager showed it running at .79GHz. So I changed the performance profile to High Performance and rebooted. That changed nothing. I created my own custom high performance profile, selected that and rebooted. Again only .79GHz. I checked the advanced power settings and min and max CPU were set to 100%. I then reset the bios to factory defaults and low and behold on boot I got a message that the type of power supply could not be determined. When this happens to a DELL, it throttles the CPU at the slowest possible speed. The seller is providing a PSU that on paper would have more than enough power for this micro pc, but the barrel jack is too long so the center pin doesn't make contact. That is required for the system to determine the wattage of the PSU.

THE SELLER INTENTIONALLY TURNED OFF THE POST ADAPTER WARNING about the PSU not being identified. I verified this to be the case on ALL 3 UNITS! Unfortunately, I don't have time to wait for returns and refunds, so I ordered myself 2 new PSU's that are advertised as being for this specific model. I will be returning the 2nd unit because despite the PSU .79GHz issue, there has got to be something else going on with the hardware as the other two units were still somewhat usable at .79GHz. The 2560x1440 size is basically a 2K monitor which is, unfortunately, becoming harder to find.

I do a lot of design work on a Mac, but would be happy to use these monitors for that as well if I did not need a PC for charts.

A couple of things to know:
-- these use either HDMI (2x) or DP-IN cables, so make sure you have inputs for those types in your computer.
-- the stands are not all the same height, so if you are using several monitors, they may not line up. It's close, but I personally would like it better if they were the same height since I extend my screen to span all three monitors as a virtual single screen.

text:
If you are on a budget but still want a decent quality 1440p monitor, this won't do you wrong. However, don't expect to be blown away by it. Previously I was daily driving a 1080p Asus. I bought two of these LGs for a dual screen setup. After switching to these, I was a little disappointed with colors. The Asus had better contrast, brightness, saturation, & black levels. I also noticed the lack of local dimming zones. However, it's still acceptable for everyday casual use. I primarily work from my computer but occasionally game too. It's perfectly fine for me, but if you do professional color grading work or want a gaming experience with really vibrant colors or a good HDR experience, look elsewhere. If you're looking for a good 1440p experience at a currently (2021) quite enticing price, this monitor is tough to beat. Despite it's shortcomings, I'm very happy with my decision to buy 2 of these.

Things I love:
- Not necessarily specific to this monitor, but 27" is a great size for 1440p. (108 ppi)
- Menus & navigation. It was really easy to customize all settings to my liking
- Ultra slim bezels!
- No dead pixels. I have 2 of these monitors.
- Black level adjust. No more eye strain in games with dark scenes
- Matte black screen handles reflections well.
- PRICE! At least at the time of purchase, nothing else competes, or even exists at this price point.

Cons
- Viewing angles. Has a perfect viewing spot. Outside of that, blacks are inconsistent across the screen.
- Backlight bleed. Problematic with screen brightness above 65-70%.
- Black levels. Does not have deep blacks. Black is still black, but other monitors have much deeper blacks.
- HDR experience. Wouldn't recommend bothering with it.
- Power cable. Short cable, w/ barrel plug into monitor and an adapter to take up lots of space on your power strip.
- Color/Contrast/Saturation. It's no OLED. It's even easily beaten by other IPS monitors. Still acceptable, but don't expect any similarities here with the LG TVs you may see in the store.

Conclusion: None of the cons were a deal breaker for me and I'm happy. 1440p monitors are expensive, but a dual monitor setup was reasonable with these. If you have the money to spend on a higher quality 1440p monitor, do it. But if you are like me and want decent quality 1440p on as small of a budget as possible, this monitor is absolutely the way to go.

Been using the standard (no USB-C ports) monitor for a couple days now, and I'm super impressed.

Let's get the negatives out the way up front: The standard, cheaper version has no USB connectivity. I wish the silver stand and white cables were black instead. I wish it had even a basic set of built-in stereo speakers. Response times and refresh rates are decidedly unimpressive, but if you're not a gamer, you really won't notice or care.

For me, these aren't deal breakers for a display that otherwise gives you so much at such a good price point.

OK, let's move on to the long list of positives: Super easy to assemble, comes with HDMI and display port cables, very easy to connect on the back vs. bottom. The raise/lower and tilt stand is fantastic for dialing in a great viewing angle. The matte screen handles overhead light and ambient light superbly - annoying glare and reflections are exceptionally well managed. Straight out the box, brightness and contrast are fairly high and good if you like things punchy; color temp is a tad warm to be easier on the eyes. It's super easily adjusted if you prefer a bit cooler and even more accurate and there are many other profiles you can try to match what works best for you - the nice joystick based control on the bottom front lip of the monitor is great and IMO preferable to the buttons you have to reach around back or bottom edges for on other displays. I've done a fair bit of photo editing (not as a pro colorist, just an experienced hobbyist) and the reach the monitor has into shadows and highlights is very good. Gamut coverage is superb at this price point. No dead pixels. What more could you ask for, really?

Conclusion: If you're not a gamer, don't require built-in speakers or USB-C, and want to get a great display at a great price, put it in your cart and buy it now. You won't regret it.

I just purchased the LG 27 inch 650 model. 4K (3840x2160). It was delivered on time. The Amazon/driver drove to my house and placed the obvious labled monitor box inside my gate. I appreciate that. Porch pirates beware I am watching you.

I bought this computer monitor for my new M4 Mac Mini. I tried using the old iMac that I had, but It would not work as display on my old iMac 2015 version. Something about not having a target display mode. That is Apple for you. Most models before that would have worked. So go ahead spend some more money for a 4K display.

I opened the box. It was well packed. There are few parts inside the box. It's fairly easy to put together. Some Youtube videos show needing a screw driver to lock in the monitor and pole/stand attachment, but my version is "slip and lock" only. no screws. It is very light weight, and can be carried around if needed. The leg stand juts out to balance the 27 inch display.

I had the Mac mini attached in no time. I did have to configure some view settings. Like brightness, HDR, etc. Its a bit bright overall. Text and fonts are clear and sharp. Images show good resolution. To do that look for a control button in the bottom middle of the screen. Not so easy to navigate the changes needed. Its more hit and miss. There is no remote control provided. That are some extra cables if needed.

I am using a lower resolution, not the 4K, the numbers ( (1920-1080). You don't really need that higher resolution. It makes the screen fonts very small and hard to read. It is exceptional at 1920x1080. My tired eyes can't really handle that anymore.

Value for the money...good, size good, sound quality needs improvement, durability to be seen.

I gave it 4 stars because the stand/pole attachment is white color. White on devices tend to yellow and show their age. The instructions are not useful. Sound or audio is pedestrian. The settings button is tricky. I did attach a "Bose" speaker sound to it.

Thank you for time. AF~

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
As an I.T. professional for decades... I've opened a LOT of monitors. Yes, this does what you'd expect from a product perspective. I've ordered and installed a couple dozen of these so far. Great screens, no dead pixels, 27" with 2K resolution, comes with HDMI cable, built in power supply so no dumb wall wart or AC adapter. All good things... But let me tell you what the biggest perk is of this thing if you are buying a lot of monitors... THE PACKAGING.

Yes folks, you heard it here first. I appreciate SO MUCH the choices here. Dell nailed it:
- No styrofoam blocks that inevitably break in transit and then leave dozens of single pellets of static electricity annoyance that cling to everything like a toddler to a mom's leg when all she wants is to use the bathroom in peace
- No sliding a block of goods out of a too-tight box that won't move because the "handle" punch-ins were used and now they block any possible extraction of the contents of said box
- No stickers on the bezel that advertise stats about the monitor that you already purchased and don't need to have as selling points, but inevitably leave some sticky residue when removed
- No fingerprint magnet piano black covered in cellophane peels that you will either miss removing or you will remove and then will stick to you despite you flicking your wrist towards the trash can 8 times only to find it on your shoe later in the day
- No plastic sheet covering the screen taped on with industrial strength shipping adhesive tape with fiber reinforcements that surely will not pull off cleanly and will instead peel like a banana when you try to remove it
- No tape sealing every possible ingress point of the box that requires you to cut every seam wondering where the heck the open end is

They NAILED it. The box is opened by laying it on its side, cutting a single piece of tape, opening the lid, pulling out the power and HDMI cables, stand parts (assembled tool-less), and then lifting off a single cardboard insert to reveal a foam bag which is pre-torn at the middle-bottom and you can tear further to expose the VESA mount and snap the stand into the monitor, lift it up and out... plug in cables, snap on a cover, and done.

You are left with only cardboard save for a few sheets of paper, a foam bag, and a plastic bag from the power cable (not sure why a bag is needed) and a plastic wrap (that easily slides off) from the HDMI cable.

If you need quick turnaround and/or appreciate relatively friendly environmentally conscious packaging, this is the winner. Best I've ever seen in terms of packaging.

Plus it looks nice as a white monitor. Well worth the price if you can find it sub $200. Even at full price it's worth it if you are buying in bulk as it will save you time and hassle in deployment. Well done Dell! I bought one... then dozens more. It's now my "go-to" monitor for office use.

I do not game, I do not care about refresh rate, I care about reasonably accurate colors, view angle, and 2D performance for office productivity. For that purpose - it's great.

It comes very well packed, the assembly is super easy as it can only go together one way, and the screws are captive with folding handles, so it's dead simple to setup and get going. The base is solid, it doesn't rock around at max height.

Color is good. View angle is good. Not a ton of gradient or hot spots with backlighting.

QHD is the way to go - 4K irritates most people on shared screen meetings, and most of the time people set them to 150% or 200% zoom. 2K is a sweet spot between legibility and size. Connected directly to a laptop at native resolution, it's sharp, and perfect. I did not see any obvious dead pixels.

8. Tool-less hardware mounting provides easy access to memory slots, swapping out storage devices, etc.

CONS:
1. Would have preferred a single 8GB RAM module vs the 2x4GB config it came with that uses up both slots. If you want to expand the memory you'll have to discard one or more of the existing modules.
2. Question the SATA SSD. I realize the object is to cut costs to the max, but for under 24 bucks you could install a same-sized, more reputable-brand M.2 NVMe drive for better performance, and free up the lone drive bay to boot. Makes one wonder just how cheap (reliable?) the included KingFast SSD is.

OTHER:
1. Cannot be upgraded to Windows 11. This may be a pro or con pending your viewpoint.
2. No wi-fi dongle or card included. Only network/internet connection is via ethernet cable. Not a deal breaker - dongles are cheap if you need wi-fi.
3. Installing an external graphic card could be problematic, unless it's low-power, half-height, and VERY thin. There's less than an inch of space between the slot and the side of the power supply (see pic). Plus, the PC's power supply is only 180 watts.
4. There are rubber feet on both the bottom and along the left side, so you can stand it vertical like a tower if desired.
5. RAM and M.2 slots are under the drive bay.
6. SHOULD you want to install a 3.5 HDD, the only full-size drive bay is filled with a caddy holding the SATA SSD. The caddy snaps out, but you'll have purchase a separate 3.5 caddy for your HDD as there is no inherent way to mount anything directly into the bay. Everything requires some manner of snap-in caddy.

The cons you kind of expect with this kind of product, so overall I give it 5 stars. I would not use it for high-end gaming. Don't know of a powerful enough half-height graphic card that would fit in the slot, but for non graphic-intensive tasks and some older games, this should work very well. So far, very happy with the purchase.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
After having the worst computer in the house for years, oh the joys of being the mom, I finally decided on this one for my upgrade. I had heard about the left speaker issue but I have had this computer for about a month now and haven't noticed this issue myself.
First impressions on the laptop were that it was really heavy. My older laptop of approximately the same size was both thicker and lighter than this one. I think this is due to the full metal case and glass screen that basically has no border. From a viewing perspective the larger screen view makes the images super easy to view and gives them a very clean look. However you will need to keep that in mind as you lift the screen when it closes as it can caused finger prints to get all over the screen if you run your fingers under the edge at all. The surface of the keyboard area is very soft to the touch but shows every little drop of dirt or water that touches it. For that reason if you tend to eat or drink around the computer it won't look clean. If that bothers you might want look for a different computer but it didn't bother me.
The keys on this laptop are really low to the surface which is nice and the keys don't really make any noise when you use them. The keys are all really responsive and I haven't had any issues with missing keystrokes or dropped letters when typing. The mouse pad is large so if you tend to be a person with larger hands or someone who drops their arms when typing you might find yourself dragging your palms or wrists against it. Again this is not an issue for me personally but some might find it very annoying since the mouse pad is just over 1/3 the width of the laptop.
As far as functionality I haven't had anything to complain about. I personally use my laptop for 3 functions. I use it to surf the internet and do basic functions online. I also spend a lot of time in my vinyl cutting machines software and I do play one vintage video game online called Everquest. The computer barely acts like its on when I am using the internet. The software also seems to run well and I have had any issues having multiple project tabs open and watching videos on at the same time, something my old computer could have never hoped to do. The game is the big issue. My old laptop couldn't take the game. It needed a full desk top with dedicated video card. I was pleased to see that the game would run on this laptop with no lag at all and all graphics on which I have rarely done. The fan does start to run at really high speed and fairly loud when I do that but it runs and the heat never gets out of control.
Overall this laptop runs really well with no issues for my purposes. I would recommend it for anyone who will be using it for similar purposes.

Stay away from Tek Refurbs. Full stop.
I ordered 10 refurbished Dell systems for the church where I work, expecting uniform, business-class machines suitable for deployment. What I received was a bait-and-switch disaster.
Every single unit had a replacement motherboard that did not match the model sold. These were not minor revisions — they were entirely different platforms stuffed into the wrong chassis. As a result:
BIOS updates for the advertised model cannot be applied
Chipset and firmware updates must be guessed and manually matched to the actual motherboard
Dell will not provide correct drivers because the service tag no longer matches the hardware
Systems appear functional at first glance but break in subtle, time-consuming ways (USB devices, cameras, firmware management, etc.)
Out of the box, these machines were not fit for business use. They were either unusable or required hours upon hours of deep technical troubleshooting per machine just to reach basic stability. This is completely unacceptable for equipment marketed as refurbished business desktops.
This isn’t normal refurbishment. This is Frankenstein hardware — mismatched boards, wrong firmware paths, and no supportability. If you’re not an experienced systems engineer with time to burn, these machines will waste your time, your money, and your sanity.
Tek Refurbs refused to take responsibility once outside their short return window, despite the issue being hardware misrepresentation, not wear and tear. They are great with copy/pasting the notice that I was outside the return window. No integrity whatsoever though.
If you value:
your time
consistent hardware
the ability to update BIOS and drivers
or any form of vendor accountability
Do not buy from Tek Refurbs.

I purchased a used DELL OptiPlex 3020 SFF Desktop PC as a retired office computer for a family member to handle basic tasks like checking emails, browsing social media, and watching online videos. Overall, it’s been a reliable choice for the price, but it’s not without a few quirks.
The OptiPlex 3020 is a compact, no-frills machine that fits perfectly in a small home setup. Its performance is more than adequate for lightweight tasks—emails load quickly, social media scrolling is smooth, and streaming videos on platforms like YouTube or Netflix works well without buffering (assuming a decent internet connection). The small form factor is a big plus, as it doesn’t take up much space on the desk, and it runs quietly, which is great for a shared living space.
Since it was a used office PC, it came with a clean Windows install, and setup was straightforward. The system handles basic multitasking fine, like having a browser with a few tabs open while streaming music or videos. The included ports (USB, HDMI, VGA) made it easy to connect to a monitor and peripherals, which was a relief for a non-tech-savvy family member.
However, there are a couple of reasons it’s not a 5-star purchase. Being a used unit, the exterior had some minor scuffs and wear, which isn’t a dealbreaker but worth noting. More importantly, it can feel sluggish if too many browser tabs or apps are open at once, especially with heavier websites. The lack of modern upgrades like an SSD (mine came with an HDD) means boot times and app loading can be a bit slow, though this is expected for an older, budget-friendly machine.
For a refurbished office PC, the DELL OptiPlex 3020 SFF does exactly what we need for basic family use. It’s a cost-effective option for email, social media, and video streaming, but don’t expect it to handle anything beyond light tasks. If you’re looking for an affordable, dependable desktop for simple needs, this is a great pick—just consider upgrading to an SSD for a smoother experience!

The 15.6” FHD screen looks sharp and bright, perfect for watching videos and working on documents. The keyboard is comfortable to type on, and the trackpad works great. I like that it’s quiet and lightweight, so I can easily take it from room to room or pack it for travel.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have never heard of the Lenovo brand before purchasing this laptop. I work remotely, but still go into the office at least once a week, so I needed something I could carry around. My last HP laptop started slowing down after 2 years. My husband bought me this as a replacement and we were both pleasantly surprised at how good it was! It’s super fast and still going strong after 3 years (bought in 2022, now 2025…time flies). I have been using laptops for over 20 years and let me tell you, this ain’t your dad’s bulky laptop from the Y2K era. Even though the screen is quite big (how I like it), the body is thin when closed and it doesn’t feel bulky at all. It fits perfectly in my backpack without taking up a lot of space. The keyboard feels good when I’m typing and makes that nice clickety clack sound. The touchscreen has been very useful during my business meetings and I love the gold color, which makes it look expensive, even though it was on the “cheaper” side. The battery life is pretty good. I get maybe 4-5 hours unplugged after fully charging. That’s more than enough for me because I always have my charger with me anyway. This is just a very rough estimate.

You’d think the “brand names” will give you a good quality laptop, but I have been very disappointed in some of them because they just don’t last very long. I will only buy Lenovo from now on. In fact, we bought 2 more Lenovos for our business because we know how good it is. I know this will start slowing down eventually as all computers do, but I will be purchasing another one when that happens. I’m hoping to get at least another year or 2 out of this one. I’ll update my review when it’s time for a replacement.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros: My girlfriend seems to really love it! it runs all of her tabs smoothly, and its overall power is great for the price point, shes been able to play games like Minecraft semi-smooth on low settings, and with performance enhancement mod 60fps is very achievable. a lot of the more casual Steam games run with relatively high success too. if youre looking for a more in-depth review id recommend searching up the model and watching some Youtube videos. finishing up, the overall experience has been above expectations, havent heard any major complaints, and the shipping at least in our case was shockingly quick. (this being to the Philippines.)

Cons: When first opening up the laptop it was in S mode, so turning that off was just a mild inconvenience. on top of being Windows 11, but thats more so nitpicking. On to the major complaint, for some reason due to the Microsoft store, it wouldnt allow us to open the game even after paying it in full. we then had to buy both the launcher and the game once more, in the Microsoft app store. to call it a pain is an understatement, but steam works just fine again once you take it out of S mode.

Final Thoughts: Do your research beforehand, and make sure this is for you. For us, it runs just about everything we need and want. But id say if you can, its more than worth it, this gives you a whole lot more value than what you pay for.

text:
I’ve been using the Legion Pro i7 (RTX + Intel i7 configuration) for a few weeks, playing a variety of modern AAA and multiplayer games — and overall, I’m impressed. Here’s the full breakdown from a gamer’s point of view:
What I really like

Performance: This thing is a powerhouse. It handles demanding titles (think open-world, high-settings) without breaking a sweat. When you crank up settings or use high refresh rates, the i7 + RTX combo keeps fps stable and smooth — no noticeable lag even in hectic firefights or big open-world scenes.

Display: The screen is . Crisp visuals, vibrant colors, and smooth frame delivery make everything look clean — from fast-paced shooters to cinematic story-games. As a gamer who cares about immersion, that matters a lot.

Versatility: It doesn’t feel like a gaming-only machine. I’ve done some lighter tasks, streaming, and even editing-type work (video/audio) and the system handles it like a champ. Perfect if you want one machine for both gaming and “real life.”

Build & convenience: Keyboard and overall build feel sturdy and premium. Ports, connectivity and cooling seem well-balanced — you can plug in accessories, external drives or headsets without fuss; fans don’t get unbearably loud unless under heavy load.

What you should know / What could be better

Battery life: Don’t expect long unplugged sessions. Like most powerful gaming laptops, the battery drains fast if you actually game on battery power. For anything heavy (games, rendering), you’ll want to be plugged in.

Portability vs performance tradeoff: It’s not a super-light laptop. If you move the machine around a lot (school, cafés, trips) you’ll feel the weight. It’s better suited as a “desktop replacement” rather than a daily-carry laptop.

Power draw and heat (if pushed hard): With high settings and long sessions, expect the fans to come alive and the machine to get warm. It’s manageable, but noticeable — plan accordingly if you game on your lap or in hot environments

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Only been using for one week, but the experience so far has been great. Here's a few things I care about:

Laptop Build (5/5). Keyboard is snappy and feels good to type or game on. Track pad is very precise and allows me to read, zoom-in, and traverse webpages very easily. Laptop has some good weight to it and won't move around on a slick surface. Screen has a robust pivot and will move exactly where you want it to and stay there. USBs are as advertised, but there is a physical switch to turn camera off which is really nice. All ports are on the left and right, and the power plug is not a circular power cord, rather a rectangular one which this laptop deserves. It's a good, solid connection, not going to slip out.

Heat Tolerance (5/5). So far, I have had no problem running games on ultra settings. Neither the power brick nor the laptop itself has gotten too hot, just warm. The heat is dissipated behind the screen, pointed away, which is a great location for it. Noise level for maintaining good temperature is great, better than my prior laptop.

Screen/Color Quality (5/5). The screen is beautiful and definitely bright enough. There is built-in color correction that is a game changer, and compared to previous laptops it is not even close. It's great to read or play games on, and there's lots of options.

Gaming Quality (4.5/5). When just playing a game alone, it does great. I have played games on Ultra quality and the FPS doesn't drop below 240 Hz, which is the max refresh rate of the screen. There are certainly more powerful systems out there, but this one is excellent for a laptop. I sometimes will have many Youtube videos open, a discord call, etc., and it still keeps this performance. However, the graphics cards struggles slightly when in the GPU optimized for gaming. Animated GIFs in discord will sometimes glitch out when using this GPU. Additionally, when closing out a game, there is a lag spike that can takes a few seconds, which is the system switching out GPUs. These are minor things, but expect some annoyances. Outside of these instances, it has been perfect.

Operating System and Software (3/5). The systems comes packaged with a bunch of bloatware, and Windows 11 shoves ads down your throat at every opportunity. However, I was able to uninstall all bloatware, and through a few hours of searching the internet, I was able to suppress all of Windows 11's ads. I was also able to remove Copilot, which is a must. I immediately went to install a new browser (Edge is still terrible), but the system seemed to keep on setting my default BACK to edge. It took 4 or 5 tries for it to stick. Clearly, MS doesn't want you making this change. The same is for the default search engine, which kept on going back to the default, when I wanted DuckDuckGO. I was also able to uninstall McAfee (also terrible) and put on Malwarebytes. It comes with a subscription, but you couldn't pay me to that software. Overall this is pretty standard procedure for any new Windows machine, but it stank a little more this time.

Battery Performance (2/5). When the system is on battery, don't expect to play games. For reference, Bloons TD6 is too much, and it switches between normal speed and chugging along like a device from 5 generations ago. It clearly is not able to take it, nor optimized for it. You can do other things like watch videos or whatever for maybe a few hours. I highly recommend keeping this thing plugged in 100% of the time.

Given that all the bloatware and Windows 11 annoyances were able to be fixed, and that battery performance isn't much of a factor for me, I still give this laptop a 5/5. It's a fantastic choice overall. It really feels like a medium performance desktop crammed into a laptop.

text:
This Chromebook is outstanding - perfect reminder of what a Chromebook should be (cheap, long battery, zippy web browsing, worry free usage, optimized port selection). The size is right, the keys feel great, the track pad is fine. The screen resolution is perfect for a Chromebook. I like how well this thing keeps a charge, and charges quickly. USB-C can't be beat, and it still has a headphone jack, HDMI, regular USB and a slot for SD cards. If you're in the market for a Chromebook, you can't do much better especially for the price. The previous Lenovo Chromebook I had is still kicking - I can't believe how much value I get out of a sub-$180 laptop. Just wanted something a little bigger than the 11" Chromebook I already had. Perfect for traveling.

Keep in mind:
- Not a PC or a Mac (if that is really truly what you think you want or need, look elsewhere and expect to spend 3x)
- Do you research about what a Chromebook actually is. All you 1, 2, and 3 star reviewers complaining that its not a PC or Macbook look like goobers in your reviews. It's essentially a web-browser, which for most people is all you need (Facebook, Netflix, look at memes, email, pay bills online, etc.). You can even use the browser version of the Microsoft suite if you're feeling in the mood to do some work.
- Even if the price was 2x, you can't complain about the screen resolution, or the hard drive size, or the lack of back-lit keyboard.
- Plenty of RAM for what you intend to do on a Chromebook
- Not a touch-screen. Don't be surprised.

Things I'd like to see improved:
- Give me an 8GB RAM option just for kicks. 4 is fine, but RAM is cheap these days.
- Flush-mount SD Card slot
