title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Bought this to temporarily replace the windows laptop I normally use when away from my desk until I could replace screen after a child sat on it. Turns out it has more permanently replaced that laptop.

The windows laptop I was using was overkill for what I needed to do when away from my main PC. Plus I have tablets and other laptops for various situations. I normally used that laptop for online shopping, light games, browsing, streaming to tv, etc.

It turns out this Chromebook was the perfect replacement. It is much more portable than my 17" pc laptop and does exactly what I need it to do. Its been about 6 months since purchase and I haven't felt I needed to rush to replace the screen in the old one.

This Chromebook is very light and portable and feels well made. If you do heavy duty gaming, have to work with graphics editors, or need to store lots of data, this isn't for you. But if you do online shopping, internet research, email, or light games this might be a good alternative.

Chromebooks use android apps via the Google Play Store to extend their capabilities. We are searching for houses right now, so Zillow works well and I can cast the computer screen to our TV to review houses we have identified. Plus, when visiting areas of interest we can take this little computer with us, attach to our vehicle hotspot and view listings online. Various browsers are compatible with the Lenovo. Obviously, Gmail also works well.

Wifi 6 makes it faster if your router is wifi 6 enabled. Battery life is good and it charges remarkably fast.

If you have AR/XR glasses the USB-C port apparently doesn't have video out, there is only one such port on the machine and it is used to recharge the machine. It comes with a charging brick. Bluetooth earbuds, mice, etc work fine. The touch screen is a really nice addition. The screen is bright and sound quality is good.

When the machine starts feeling "slow" a restart seems to cure it. You do have to manage storage, don't overload the machine with pics, data or apps. I have used the Lenovo daily now for about 6 months and am happy with its operation. I am a computer speed freak and am constantly upgrading and tweaking my PCs and routers, but haven't felt like this little machine needs any such attention. Again, it isn't for heavy computing.

i would recommend this for people with light computing needs who understand android devices, play store apps, can manage storage and don't mind the Google environment. It is a good value. I would purchase again. Manage your expectations, understand your needs and it will be a good experience.

text: It is a nice laptop. It has decent build quality. I wouldn't say it's the best but for the price, it's pretty decent. It's a little on the heavy side. A lot of people have already said that, but it definitely will weigh a little bit more than your standard laptop for it not being a metal shell. That being said, I have been doing some testing and some games and specifically at least in call of duty and also a little bit in Apex. I haven't tested fortnite or anything like that, but call of duty and Apex. They seem to have some micro stutter that's happening. Basically when you're moving it'll like cut frames for like half a second and then put you right back in. So it seems to be that maybe the drivers are not supported or are not optimized. I've tried reinstalling the drivers from Nvidia and it's hit or miss. I'll load into the game and sometimes I have nothing no center and then I'll load into the other game another day and it's stutter all day so keep that in mind. I don't know if it's the 50/50 series or what, but I saw that somebody was having issues with the 5090 similar to what I was having. So it might just be the 50 series graphics cards in general. Maybe going with a 4060 might be a little bit better but I have also played battlefield and battlefield runs perfectly fine. Battlefield 6 to be exact. So that's a new game. Maybe it's better optimized for these newer graphics cards. Don't know. I did try running a couple other games and those ones played fine. I tried running forza 5 and killing floor 3 They played fine. I tried running gta and that played fine. So overall, if those are the games that you're trying to run then some of those games will run fine and they'll run at respectable FPS. I've been getting on average through most games about 80 FPS to 100 I do try to go for more quality than FPS but that's me so you can maybe get more FPS if you lower the quality a little bit but just know that it's not perfect and it does also overheat a little bit in my opinion. It never shut off on me but when you touch the middle of the keyboard at least on mine it does get hot. Not just warm but hot. I don't know how good that is for the device in the long run, so I bought a aftermarket cooler by llano just to kind of mitigate some of that heat. I'm sure a lot of people already have touched on this, but battery life is not that great. Maybe 2 hours at most of gameplay so you're plugging this in all the time. It's more like a desktop PC than it is. A portable PC that you can just play unplugged but if you have an outlet and you're able to be next to know it. It's a nice PC. It's fast at that at some games and the build quality is decent. Oh last thing speakers are trash get headphones or some external Bluetooth speaker or something because the speakers are garbage at full volume. It sounds like barely half volume on my phone. Overall, I am decently happy with the product. I would probably give it like a 3.7 but they don't have an option for that so I'll give it four stars just because it does play most of the games I want to find. I just wish it had a little bit more tuning to it to make it run cooler and also make the drivers for the Nvidia 50 series a little bit better or at least give it an update or something

text:
La Lenovo LOQ Essential cumple con lo que promete: es una laptop básica para gaming, pensada para quien busca lo mínimo funcional. Con ella es posible jugar títulos AAA, pero únicamente con gráficos reducidos y bajo ciertas condiciones.
El punto más importante es la memoria RAM. De fábrica no es suficiente para este tipo de juegos, por lo que es obligatorio actualizarla a 16 GB para obtener un rendimiento aceptable. Aquí hay una advertencia clave: la laptop solo cuenta con un slot de RAM, lo que limita futuras mejoras.
En cuanto a la refrigeración, el equipo solo tiene un ventilador compartido para CPU y GPU, lo que provoca que, bajo carga, el ruido sea considerablemente alto, especialmente al jugar. Esto puede resultar molesto para sesiones prolongadas.
Considerando que una memoria RAM de 16 GB ronda actualmente los $2,500 MXN, mi recomendación es evaluar seriamente si vale la pena invertir ese dinero en esta laptop. En muchos casos, es mejor destinar ese presupuesto adicional a una laptop de gama superior, con mejor sistema de enfriamiento y mayor margen de actualización.

text:
La Lenovo LOQ Essential cumple con lo que promete: es una laptop básica para gaming, pensada para quien busca lo mínimo funcional. Con ella es posible jugar títulos AAA, pero únicamente con gráficos reducidos y bajo ciertas condiciones.
El punto más importante es la memoria RAM. De fábrica no es suficiente para este tipo de juegos, por lo que es obligatorio actualizarla a 16 GB para obtener un rendimiento aceptable. Aquí hay una advertencia clave: la laptop solo cuenta con un slot de RAM, lo que limita futuras mejoras.
En cuanto a la refrigeración, el equipo solo tiene un ventilador compartido para CPU y GPU, lo que provoca que, bajo carga, el ruido sea considerablemente alto, especialmente al jugar. Esto puede resultar molesto para sesiones prolongadas.
Considerando que una memoria RAM de 16 GB ronda actualmente los $2,500 MXN, mi recomendación es evaluar seriamente si vale la pena invertir ese dinero en esta laptop. En muchos casos, es mejor destinar ese presupuesto adicional a una laptop de gama superior, con mejor sistema de enfriamiento y mayor margen de actualización.

text:
This Chromebook is outstanding - perfect reminder of what a Chromebook should be (cheap, long battery, zippy web browsing, worry free usage, optimized port selection). The size is right, the keys feel great, the track pad is fine. The screen resolution is perfect for a Chromebook. I like how well this thing keeps a charge, and charges quickly. USB-C can't be beat, and it still has a headphone jack, HDMI, regular USB and a slot for SD cards. If you're in the market for a Chromebook, you can't do much better especially for the price. The previous Lenovo Chromebook I had is still kicking - I can't believe how much value I get out of a sub-$180 laptop. Just wanted something a little bigger than the 11" Chromebook I already had. Perfect for traveling.

Keep in mind:
- Not a PC or a Mac (if that is really truly what you think you want or need, look elsewhere and expect to spend 3x)
- Do you research about what a Chromebook actually is. All you 1, 2, and 3 star reviewers complaining that its not a PC or Macbook look like goobers in your reviews. It's essentially a web-browser, which for most people is all you need (Facebook, Netflix, look at memes, email, pay bills online, etc.). You can even use the browser version of the Microsoft suite if you're feeling in the mood to do some work.
- Even if the price was 2x, you can't complain about the screen resolution, or the hard drive size, or the lack of back-lit keyboard.
- Plenty of RAM for what you intend to do on a Chromebook
- Not a touch-screen. Don't be surprised.

Things I'd like to see improved:
- Give me an 8GB RAM option just for kicks. 4 is fine, but RAM is cheap these days.
- Flush-mount SD Card slot

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Bought this to temporarily replace the windows laptop I normally use when away from my desk until I could replace screen after a child sat on it. Turns out it has more permanently replaced that laptop.

The windows laptop I was using was overkill for what I needed to do when away from my main PC. Plus I have tablets and other laptops for various situations. I normally used that laptop for online shopping, light games, browsing, streaming to tv, etc.

It turns out this Chromebook was the perfect replacement. It is much more portable than my 17" pc laptop and does exactly what I need it to do. Its been about 6 months since purchase and I haven't felt I needed to rush to replace the screen in the old one.

This Chromebook is very light and portable and feels well made. If you do heavy duty gaming, have to work with graphics editors, or need to store lots of data, this isn't for you. But if you do online shopping, internet research, email, or light games this might be a good alternative.

Chromebooks use android apps via the Google Play Store to extend their capabilities. We are searching for houses right now, so Zillow works well and I can cast the computer screen to our TV to review houses we have identified. Plus, when visiting areas of interest we can take this little computer with us, attach to our vehicle hotspot and view listings online. Various browsers are compatible with the Lenovo. Obviously, Gmail also works well.

Wifi 6 makes it faster if your router is wifi 6 enabled. Battery life is good and it charges remarkably fast.

If you have AR/XR glasses the USB-C port apparently doesn't have video out, there is only one such port on the machine and it is used to recharge the machine. It comes with a charging brick. Bluetooth earbuds, mice, etc work fine. The touch screen is a really nice addition. The screen is bright and sound quality is good.

When the machine starts feeling "slow" a restart seems to cure it. You do have to manage storage, don't overload the machine with pics, data or apps. I have used the Lenovo daily now for about 6 months and am happy with its operation. I am a computer speed freak and am constantly upgrading and tweaking my PCs and routers, but haven't felt like this little machine needs any such attention. Again, it isn't for heavy computing.

i would recommend this for people with light computing needs who understand android devices, play store apps, can manage storage and don't mind the Google environment. It is a good value. I would purchase again. Manage your expectations, understand your needs and it will be a good experience.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
TL;DR: If you're an average user who just browses the internet, uses social media, checks and sends email, uses a few apps, does school or work projects from home, or watches YouTube/streams shows, this Chromebook is for you!

PROS:

Fast boot up and shut down times
Easy automatic updates
Can't get viruses
It comes preloaded with all the basic apps for free
Smooth and fast web browsing
Very little to no lag while using one app and one or a few tabs at a time
Good build quality
Long battery life
Good size and very portable
Clear and bright basic screen
Good sound quality from the speakers
Expandable storage via SD card slot
Big multi-touch touchpad
Well spaced chicklet keyboard

CONS:

Very limited ports including only one USB port
Screen is only HD (720p)
Very limited built-in storage
Basic processor and limited RAM
No touch screen
No backlit keyboard

Bottom line: If you don't play video games, edit photos/video/audio/etc, if you aren't a power user who uses multiple apps and multiple tabs at one time, then this device is for you. If you're an average everyday user, for the price, this device is really good.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Bought this to temporarily replace the windows laptop I normally use when away from my desk until I could replace screen after a child sat on it. Turns out it has more permanently replaced that laptop.

The windows laptop I was using was overkill for what I needed to do when away from my main PC. Plus I have tablets and other laptops for various situations. I normally used that laptop for online shopping, light games, browsing, streaming to tv, etc.

It turns out this Chromebook was the perfect replacement. It is much more portable than my 17" pc laptop and does exactly what I need it to do. Its been about 6 months since purchase and I haven't felt I needed to rush to replace the screen in the old one.

This Chromebook is very light and portable and feels well made. If you do heavy duty gaming, have to work with graphics editors, or need to store lots of data, this isn't for you. But if you do online shopping, internet research, email, or light games this might be a good alternative.

Chromebooks use android apps via the Google Play Store to extend their capabilities. We are searching for houses right now, so Zillow works well and I can cast the computer screen to our TV to review houses we have identified. Plus, when visiting areas of interest we can take this little computer with us, attach to our vehicle hotspot and view listings online. Various browsers are compatible with the Lenovo. Obviously, Gmail also works well.

Wifi 6 makes it faster if your router is wifi 6 enabled. Battery life is good and it charges remarkably fast.

If you have AR/XR glasses the USB-C port apparently doesn't have video out, there is only one such port on the machine and it is used to recharge the machine. It comes with a charging brick. Bluetooth earbuds, mice, etc work fine. The touch screen is a really nice addition. The screen is bright and sound quality is good.

When the machine starts feeling "slow" a restart seems to cure it. You do have to manage storage, don't overload the machine with pics, data or apps. I have used the Lenovo daily now for about 6 months and am happy with its operation. I am a computer speed freak and am constantly upgrading and tweaking my PCs and routers, but haven't felt like this little machine needs any such attention. Again, it isn't for heavy computing.

i would recommend this for people with light computing needs who understand android devices, play store apps, can manage storage and don't mind the Google environment. It is a good value. I would purchase again. Manage your expectations, understand your needs and it will be a good experience.

text:
TL;DR: If you're an average user who just browses the internet, uses social media, checks and sends email, uses a few apps, does school or work projects from home, or watches YouTube/streams shows, this Chromebook is for you!

PROS:

Fast boot up and shut down times
Easy automatic updates
Can't get viruses
It comes preloaded with all the basic apps for free
Smooth and fast web browsing
Very little to no lag while using one app and one or a few tabs at a time
Good build quality
Long battery life
Good size and very portable
Clear and bright basic screen
Good sound quality from the speakers
Expandable storage via SD card slot
Big multi-touch touchpad
Well spaced chicklet keyboard

CONS:

Very limited ports including only one USB port
Screen is only HD (720p)
Very limited built-in storage
Basic processor and limited RAM
No touch screen
No backlit keyboard

Bottom line: If you don't play video games, edit photos/video/audio/etc, if you aren't a power user who uses multiple apps and multiple tabs at one time, then this device is for you. If you're an average everyday user, for the price, this device is really good.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’ve been using the Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 5 for a few weeks now, and it’s clear this machine was built for professionals who need performance, durability, and reliability.

Pros:
• Excellent Build Quality – Classic ThinkPad design with a sturdy chassis, spill-resistant keyboard, and that iconic red TrackPoint. Feels like it can survive the daily grind of travel and meetings.
• Great Keyboard – Typing is a dream. The keys have great travel and feedback. Ideal for long typing sessions.
• Powerful Performance – With the latest Intel (or AMD) processor, it handles multitasking, data-heavy spreadsheets, and remote work apps without breaking a sweat.
• Plenty of Ports – No need to live the dongle life. USB-A, USB-C, HDMI, Ethernet – they’re all here.
• Strong Security Features – Fingerprint reader, optional IR camera for facial recognition, and a physical webcam shutter give peace of mind.
• Battery Life – Easily gets me through a full workday with moderate to heavy use.

Cons:
• Display Is Good, Not Great – It’s sharp and bright enough, but if you’re doing color-sensitive work like photo editing, you might want an external monitor.
• Not the Lightest – At around 3.2 lbs, it’s not heavy, but there are lighter ultrabooks if portability is your top priority.

Final Verdict:
If you’re looking for a dependable workhorse that balances power, durability, and business-ready features, the T14 Gen 5 should be at the top of your list. It’s not flashy, but it gets the job done – and does it well.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I picked up this Lenovo 300e Chromebook as a secondary device, something I could toss in my bag for on-the-go tasks without worrying about my more expensive laptop. And honestly? It's been surprisingly useful.

Use Cases:

The "Coffee Shop Companion":
I often find myself wanting to escape the home office and get some work done at a local cafe. This Chromebook is perfect for that. It's lightweight, the battery lasts long enough for a few hours of work, and it's great for writing emails, browsing the web, and even some light document editing.
The 2-in-1 design comes in handy when I just want to read an article or watch a quick video while sipping my latte.
Travel Buddy:
I recently took a short trip, and this Chromebook was ideal. It's small enough to fit easily in my carry-on, and it's great for staying connected, checking flight details, and even watching a movie on the plane.
I also let my child use it for some light games, and the touch screen was perfect for that.
Kitchen Recipe Reader:
I've found myself using this chromebook in the kitchen. The 2 in 1 feature allows it to sit on the counter like a tablet, and display recipes while I cook. I don't have to worry about getting my main laptop dirty.
Simple Task Machine:
Let's be real, sometimes you just need a device for simple tasks. Checking email, browsing social media, watching YouTube – this Chromebook handles all of that with ease.
It's also great for letting the kids use for schoolwork or simple games without worrying about them messing up my main computer.

My Personal Take:

Yes, it's a renewed device, so there are a few minor scratches. But honestly, for the price, I'm not complaining.
It's not a powerhouse, so don't expect to run demanding applications or play high-end games. But for everyday tasks, it's more than adequate.
The Chrome OS is simple and intuitive, which is a plus for me. I don't need a lot of bells and whistles. I just want something that works.
I have had no charging issues, and the battery life has been acceptable for my needs.

Overall:

If you're looking for a budget-friendly, portable device for everyday tasks, the Lenovo 300e Chromebook (Renewed) is worth considering. It's not perfect, but it's a solid little machine that gets the job done.

I don't know what the issue is, this thing just... doesn't work well.

I don't know if it's because it's refurbished, if Google OS is weird, if the keyboard isn't responsive, if the tablet is slow, or any of a thousand other things that just feel OFF.

Even though you have as track pad and a keyboard, it only allows you to interface with it as though you were on a phone, seriously limiting my capabilities in Google sheets. You can't rearrange tabs, freezing top row is unintuitive, etc.

While using Google sheets, the keyboard misses inputs. At first I thought it was dropping the first letter I typed because it had to, like, select into the cell. I tried to muscle through and noticed that it would skip random letters in words too though.

I hooked up a Bluetooth mouse and trying to scroll with the mouse is a nightmare, the screen will lock up, the scrolling is inconsistent (on YouTube, for instance, sometimes a scroll will bring you down one row of videos, other times it moves you down a whole page and it locks the app up), and it's very hard to be precise. I'm not talking for graphic design type precision, I'm saying it's hard to click the three dots next to a video the mouse is so janky.

If you have a system update, you can't download or install new apps.

By default, the system uses internal storage and not Google drive, making it a pain to start a document on this device and work on it at your computer.

It will just crash sometimes. Just, while thing, shuts down. No clue.

App functionally is different between this device, mobile, and my computer so switching around is very confusing as each one has little differences.

It's very slow. Just having Google sheets and YouTube open makes it sputter and run incredibly slow.

The touchscreen is very responsive on an up note, it's decently bright and crisp too.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Coming from multiple MacBook Pros, I was looking for a laptop with similar build quality and this delivers. The chassis is solid with no flex when you pick it up. The screen is excellent (actually better than my MacBook), battery life has been great, and the keyboard feels good with nice backlit keys. The trackpad is highly customizable. Even the power brick is compact, which makes a real difference for portability. Sound is decent but not MacBook-level, if that matters to you. The built-in Bluetooth works great with my earbuds and allows them to switch back and forth to my iPhone as needed.

I installed Linux Mint immediately (never even booted Windows 11), and it pairs really well with the hardware. The one thing that doesn't work yet is the NPU (the Ryzen AI chip for local AI processing); Linux support for that is still developing. If you require NPU functionality now, you'll need Windows. If you can wait, this is a great Linux machine.
Highly recommended for anyone wanting a well-built, portable laptop that runs Linux well.

One word of caution: some sellers on Amazon are buying stock laptops, replacing the hard drives, RAM, and other components with larger but much cheaper parts, then trying to sell them at an elevated cost implying they are from the factory that way. Read the listing details carefully and make sure it says new, unopened box, from the factory, etc. Otherwise you might get a base model with cheap upgrades that don't last.

text:
⚠️ WARNING: Laptop came with pre-installed malware and spyware. Read before buying.
My son (who works in IT) analyzed this laptop after we noticed suspicious behavior. Here is what he found:
Malicious Browser Extensions Pre-Installed
Both Chrome and Edge had suspicious extensions force-installed via Windows registry policies, meaning they could not simply be deleted:
• “Search Accelerator” – hijacks searches across Google, Bing, Yahoo, and multiple Yandex domains, redirecting them without your knowledge
• “Ad Reducer” – purpose unclear, but installed covertly via registry
These were configured under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome and the Edge equivalent, making them invisible to normal extension management.
Chrome Configured to Suppress Security Warnings
A Chrome policy (LookalikeWarningAllowlistDomains) was set to whitelist the domain tapnav-com.s1search.co — a known malicious domain. This means Chrome was configured to NOT warn you if you were redirected there. When my son attempted to remove the extensions, the browser displayed graphics served from this suspicious domain before he could close it.
Windows Update Disabled Until 2041
Windows Update had been suspended until November 2, 2041. This appears intentional — to prevent security patches from exposing or removing the malicious settings. This alone should be disqualifying.
Tencent Software Debris
Large amounts of Tencent PC Manager remnants were found in C:\Program Files, Program Files (x86), and throughout the registry. While the executable had been removed before shipping, the leftovers interfered with installing third-party antivirus software (ESET flagged it on installation).
The Same Review Exists on Multiple Listings
We found an identical Japanese-language review describing the exact same malware configuration on at least two different Amazon laptop listings. This is not a one-off — it appears to be a systemic issue across a batch or multiple products from this seller.
What to do if you already bought this:
1. Do NOT connect to WiFi before cleaning the machine
2. Delete the registry keys under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome and \Microsoft\Edge
3. Remove the Search Accelerator and Ad Reducer extensions from both Chrome and Edge
4. Check Windows Update settings and re-enable updates immediately
5. Run a full scan with Windows Defender and Malwarebytes
6. Consider a clean Windows reinstall from official Microsoft media (NOT the built-in recovery, which may also be compromised)
The hardware itself performs as advertised for the price, and the screen size is good. But no hardware value justifies receiving a device pre-configured to spy on your browsing and suppress its own security updates. Buyer beware.

text:
I bought this Lenovo ThinkCentre M920s, i7, 512 GB storage SFF computer as a replacement for an earlier Lenovo model, the ThinkCentre M93p, which I bought refurbished and then used for a remarkable 10 years, with no complaints except that it could not be upgraded to Windows 11. I did at one point install a low-powered video card in the old one because I needed an HDMI port. The reliability of the older machine was a big factor in choosing Lenovo for the new one. The small form factor works well for me, too.

Another reason that I chose this computer is that it has a DVD drive. Many of these refurbished SFF computers don't have those. I didn't want to pay extra for one or fuss with installing one myself.

The vendor that mine came from is different from the vendor that is now shown on the listing.

The unit arrived well-packed and as described. It shipped with a power cord and a USB wifi 5 dongle which says, "BT + AC600, Driver free." I used the dongle while I set up the computer and transferred over my stuff. I am using an ethernet connection now, though.

The first surprise is that there was a fair amount of noise during the initial Windows update. It sounded like a vacuum cleaner. I don't recall my old computer making any noise at all, except a slight fan noise after I installed the aforementioned video card. After the Windows update, I don't detect any noise from this one.

The first thing I did after the initial setup was to disconnect the unit from OneDrive. I want my files to all be stored locally.

The second surprise: this new-to-me computer has a faster processor and more memory than my old one, and I had assumed that it would be faster in every way that I could perceive. However, I have found that start-up on this machine is slower than on the old one. I see a black screen with white characters for several seconds. So that is a disappointment. The difference is so noticeable that I checked to make sure that I actually have an SSD drive, and I do.

Overall, I'm glad that I bought this, but I do have some reservations due to the two things mentioned.

Edit to add that I downloaded the Lenovo Vantage software and it scanned my computer for updates, which led to an update of the BIOS. Start-up is faster now. Thank you to the reviewer who recommended downloading the Vantage software.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Purchased primarily as a work laptop with the option for streaming games during downtime between classes. (I teach and drive around between locations)

Pros:
Sturdy, stylish, and the garaged stylus is convenient. The 144hz display is perhaps overkill and likely accounts for a fair bit of the price tag that I'd personally prefer to have seen invested in all-aluminum construction or a better webcam.

Chrome OS is a solid platform for general purpose productivity. The hardware is more than sufficient to keep the experience smooth and snappy. The garaged stylus is automatically charged, which is a major improvement over my previous experience of having to recharge my old bamboo stylus every time I wanted to use it because I couldn't be bothered to remember charging it.

The core gimmick of the thing is cloud gaming, and I was pleasantly surprised to find it's a perfectly pleasant experience. The libraries on these services (Amazon Luna, GForce Now) are limited, but growing. I find the niche they occupy to be providing a solid casual gaming experience on the road, rather than being a serious competitor for a desktop gaming PC. I could see that assessment changing very rapidly if their libraries grow to rival steam.

Build quality is solid. The plastic components are finished in a grippy texture and are sturdy enough to feel like it earns the premium price point. Would prefer an all-aluminum construction.

Indifferent:
Audio is great (for a laptop), but that's kind of a moot point for me. I'd consider it poor form to use anything but headphones in a public space, and I've got a desktop for home use.

Cons:
There's a weird bump on the "d" key that annoys me constantly despite being of precisely zero consequence. Probably a minor manufacturing defect.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Within our household, three children are gamers alongside two adult gamers. It's getting a little expensive now tbh lol. Over Thanksgiving break we all landed on Stardew Valley as a video game we enjoy playing together as a family, but our youngest sons' 12 yr old entry-level gaming laptop is dying, even with upgrading ram and a reset on that machine it can't handle most games anymore. So he wasn't able to play with us on his own rig. We took turns, but it just wasn't as fun.

Enter the Lenovo Flex 5i. I took the time to enable the Linux Beta, went through the process of getting steam set to 32-bit, and downloaded Stardew Valley. It runs smoothly, with no glitching/lag. I did make the Linux portion of the HD take more of a share than was suggested, 30 Gb vs 10 Gb to accommodate adding more demanding games. It runs Terraria and other similar titles beautifully. But this Chromebook doesn't stop there for us, we've been using it for web surfing, streaming movies, and as an extra device for homework when the school Chromebooks are slow/acting up. It's filling a niche that we truly didn't realize we needed in our home.

Overall: If you are looking to play some low-demand (side scrollers, dungeon crawling 32-bit games) steam games via Linux, then this is a great option. If you just need something to watch movies/youtube/surf the web it's more than powerful enough to handle that with ease. This Chromebook is sleek, peppy, and feels expensive even though we got it for under $300. My only minor complaint so far is the matte finish is prone to showing every fingerprint on the outside of the case, but at the same time, it lets us see how often it is being used and reminds us to clean it often.

But as a final note, for us, this Chromebook is a stop-gap/multi-purpose item to fill in when we need it. In late winter/early spring, our son will probably get a mini gaming PC since he isn't as big of a gamer as the rest of his siblings but may want to play more robust games. This Chromebook gives us some breathing room over the winter to research & shop for his future rig while allowing us all to play games together as a family.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this as a replacement for an earlier model, the Lenovo 330c (which I still use after 4 years). The 330c had two issues: 1) The case was plastic, and the lid developed several large cracks from hinge stress, and 2) It struggled to play videos, especially from facebook and news sites.

This newer model has a metal lid which should solve the cracking problem. It is also notably faster and has no problem so far playing any videos. One the downside, the battery life seems to be much less, and it is slow to wake up from sleep mode, including that it seems slower to reconnect to the wifi than the older model. UPDATE: Today, less than 30 days in, the unit would not start up. The white light on the power button just kept blinking after I closed the lid to move from the kitchen to the living room. I couldn't find any official Lenovo support online, but I did find a YouTube which sent me to try recovery mode (esc+circle-arrow fcn key+ power button) and I was able to power off. Powered up again OK. Worrisome. This unit does not sleep well.

The lighted keyboard is a nice new feature. I also like that the power cord can be attached from either side, since the nearest outlet always seemed to be on the 'wrong' side (and the left-side plug on the old model was always a bit in the way for left-handed folk like me). There's no HDMI port, but I only used that occasionally and it's addressable with a dongle.

Most things synch up pretty well making for an easy setup. I'm a bit old school and keep a lot on the machine memory rather than the cloud. This has plenty of storage for that, but of course that stuff doesn't synch and needs to be transferred. This won't open my Open Office files unless I upload them to the cloud, convert them, and download them back down. A bit of a hassle but not a deal killer.

A good purchase overall, and good enough to become my only computer. I'm going to shed my old desktop tower.

text:
I got this as a replacement for an earlier model, the Lenovo 330c (which I still use after 4 years). The 330c had two issues: 1) The case was plastic, and the lid developed several large cracks from hinge stress, and 2) It struggled to play videos, especially from facebook and news sites.

This newer model has a metal lid which should solve the cracking problem. It is also notably faster and has no problem so far playing any videos. I couldn't find any official Lenovo support online, but I did find a YouTube which sent me to try recovery mode (esc+circle-arrow fcn key+ power button) and I was able to power off. Powered up again OK. Worrisome. This unit does not sleep well.

The lighted keyboard is a nice new feature. I also like that the power cord can be attached from either side, since the nearest outlet always seemed to be on the 'wrong' side (and the left-side plug on the old model was always a bit in the way for left-handed folk like me). There's no HDMI port, but I only used that occasionally and it's addressable with a dongle.

Most things synch up pretty well making for an easy setup. I'm a bit old school and keep a lot on the machine memory rather than the cloud. This has plenty of storage for that, but of course that stuff doesn't synch and needs to be transferred. This won't open my Open Office files unless I upload them to the cloud, convert them, and download them back down. A bit of a hassle but not a deal killer.

A good purchase overall, and good enough to become my only computer. I'm going to shed my old desktop tower.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this on Prime Day as a backup/secondary laptop. When I received it, I wanted to give it a good, solid test run, so I used only this laptop for everything I did for about three weeks. I found it to be surprisingly fast and I had no problems at all running my usual stuff--many tabs open in Chrome, Word, streaming video, email, music, etc. The screen is average/above-average. The keyboard is quite nice to type on! The trackpad is okay, but I did have some irritating moments where it wasn't always as responsive as I needed it to be. The battery life, sadly, was sub par for me. Even keeping the screen brightness turned down to no more than middle of the road, I couldn't really get much more than 3 or maaaaaybe 4 hours. I tinkered with settings to try to help the issue, but in this day and age, I feel like I shouldn't have to reduce everything to the bare, bare minimum to squeeze out 4 hours of battery life. Not when I can get a full day of use on my other laptops without charging.

I did have some Windows 11 glitches with it (several times it wouldn't let me log-in with fingerprint but it also wouldn't let me log in with my pin either and I'd have to reboot), but that's par for the course and hopefully as updates come out, those will be corrected. And that's operating system stuff, not a hardware issue. I'm only pointing it out for people who might be buying this laptop for someone who would find issues like that particularly frustrating.

If you need a solid laptop for light use, you're not going to be too mobile with it, and it'll be mainly plugged in, this is a decent everyday budget laptop. If you need something with more robust battery life, however, this may not be the best choice for you.

I recently purchased the Lenovo ThinkPad E16 Gen 2 for work, and it has exceeded my expectations in several areas. The 16-inch WUXGA IPS display is bright (300 nits), crisp, and provides excellent color accuracy — perfect for spreadsheets, presentations, and even occasional media use.

Battery life is decent for a full-day work setup, and the laptop stays cool even under moderate workloads. I also appreciate the business-focused features, like the fingerprint reader and solid security options.

Minor drawbacks: The laptop is slightly heavier than ultraportables, so it’s not ideal for carrying all day. The 300-nit display is bright but could be stronger in direct sunlight.

Overall, this is a great business laptop for anyone needing a reliable, high-performance machine with a large display. I would definitely recommend it to professionals who value build quality and productivity features.

For the past 4+ years, I have been using the first generation Zenbook Duo laptop that had the second screen that was much smaller and built into the top of the keyboard when the keyboard and both screens formed a one-piece laptop. This model took some getting used to due to its flat keyboard style and position of the trackpad compared to the old model, but having the large second screen made up for that. The laptop is simply gorgeous. The 3K OLED screens image quality are perfect and the flexibility in positioning the screens to how you want to use them can't be beat by any other laptop out there right now.

The laptop is fast, and MUCH lighter than the old Zenbook Duo I had. I was surprised at how light the whole thing was with two screens and a keyboard nicely stacked and docked together. The 120Hz monitors have nice, smooth motion during video and even window animations compared to a 60Hz. The 32GB of RAM and 1TB hard drive are more than adequate for a powerful laptop like this. I do wish it came with Windows 11 Pro instead of Home though.

The 2025 version of this laptop comes with the Ultra 9 285H CPU, which was worth the wait. There are a ton of YouTube video reviews, so I will not go into all of the details - you should definitely watch them first, but here are my pros and cons:

Cons:
Heavier than your usual 14" laptop, but you have 2 screens :-)
Two Thunderbolt 4 ports - why not TB 5?
The keyboard battery life when removed from the body seems a bit short when the backlight is on
The CPU can take more power, but it is limited in this machine to prevent it from throttling too much
Battery life is limited due to the two screens, but that is to be expected
Why not Win 11 Professional instead of Home for a premium device?
There is only 1 M.2 slot for storage, which is a bummer

Overall, this is one of the best machines I have ever used. Applications are quick, and I am never waiting for something to respond. This is NOT a gaming machine, regardless of what you might hear. The iGPU is not the best that Intel has to offer, and the NPU for AI is weaker than most - but for what it is meant to do, it excels. Highly recommended!

I'm an amateur musician and I noticed that a number of my colleagues were using large format iPads for their sheet music, so I looked into it and found that the large iPads were quite expensive, so I decided to see if I could find a cheaper alternative. I found a refurbished unit of this IdeaPad for $219 (thru Amazon), so I purchased it and a Lenovo touchpad stylus (an additional $30). For my purposes, I was looking for a unit with an HD screen, a touchpad, and the ability to convert to a tablet (so it can sit on a music stand). This IdeaPad only has 4GB of RAM, but that is plenty for my purposes. It only has a 128GB M.2 drive (which, again, is plenty for my purposes), but it can be upgraded by the user to a generic 1TB M.2 drive for $50. For my project, I wiped the Windows 11 installation in favor of xubuntu 22. It installs easily once the secure boot feature is disabled in the BIOS.

As for fitness of purpose, I just got this IdeaPad, so I don't know how well it will work as a sheet music alternative. I still need to modify some GPL'd PDF display software ("xournal" seems to be the best candidate I've seen so far) for ease of use during a 2.5 hour rehearsal. Also, preliminary tests seem to indicate that the battery probably won't last for a full rehearsal with the display being driven full-time.

I knocked a star off the touchscreen for its non-intuitive behavior -- the screen starts to respond when one moves the stylus within about 3mm. This has led to some stray marks in my early tests. I knocked off 2 stars from the battery life because of its performance under load. This may be because I purchased a refurbished unit, so take it with a grain of salt.

My middle-schoolers do a lot of work at school on Chromebooks through Google Classroom. I wanted to give them a similar experience at home while keeping the cost reasonable and support overhead very low. The Lenovo Chromebook S330 was just the trick. This thing is fast, the screen is clear and bright and the battery life is awesome with an estimated life of 13 hours. Is it really 13 hours? For perspective, "best" in terms of computer hardware and operating system really comes down to your intended use. You'll get the best value and have the best experience when you buy for that intended use. For what I've described above, this Chromebook is perfect. I could have spent a lot more on a high-performance gaming rig or something with a touchscreen and all the extras, but that's not what was needed.

We haven't had it very long, so I'll post back if any of my initial impressions and observations change.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I don't understand all the negative reviews about the screen. It's not the BEST laptop screen I've ever used, but FAR from the worst. And for less than $250? Are you guys kidding me? Are you expecting an ipad pro level screen?

The laptop is solid even though it's plastic, I'm not worried about putting this thing in my backpack. While the keyboard is a little stiff for my taste, it works well. I'm just used to my mechanical keyboard on my desktop. I can write and do some coding perfectly fine and that's how I would describe this chromebook:

Perfectly fine.
Solid.
Reliable.
Lenovo-quality.
I might as well be in one of their commercials, but Lenovo has never failed me.

The negatives?

The screen can be a BIT wobbly when I adjust it, but that's minor. It doesn't wobble when I type, which would make me want to return it. A couple more ports would be nice as well as an SD card slot that allows the SD card to completely insert. This one, the card sticks out halfway.

Battery life is great, can go for hours at the library without needing to be plugged in and I'm using a higher brightness. I'm not doing anything intensive, just chrome tabs, spotify, watching Youtube.

If you need a laptop to take care of your internet needs and basic computer needs, this is a solid one for the price. If you need stronger hardware, then spend at least 400-500. However, if you're already spending that much money, it might be better to get a Windows machine, unless you LOVE Chromebooks.

I love Chrome OS for what it is. Fast, lightweight, and cost-effective. That's the name of the game. If you buy this laptop, or any laptop a this price, then don't expect a thousand-dollar plus experience and then leave horrible reviews. This is a solid chromebook, especially for the price. I'll be keeping this one for a long while and give it to a family member when it's time for me to upgrade.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text: This computer overall is an excellent product. I know because I have had one for around three years and have been using it for college without any issues until now. The problem is that when I purchased a replacement, it came in and was not functional during the start-up process. It turned on when I plugged it in, however, it had not been updated for two years, and I had to sit and wait for it to do so. Which is okay, no big deal. Until it finished the update, and had to start over and do it again. Even still I waited and allowed it to update a second time. The issue occurred when I attempted to log in with my Google account. The laptop screen went black and all I could see was the mouse. That was for about three minutes. Then the mouse disappeared, the computer turned off, and would not turn back on again. I called Lenovo customer support, and found out that there was no response to the power cycling efforts we made during troubleshooting. Lenovo had sold this product a few years ago and did not have any information on my laptop when I gave them the product number. I was able to get a refund from Amazon, but I am ultimately very disappointed with this product because I really enjoyed my model and everything that came with it. If you are considering this purchase, I wouldn't risk buying this product through Amazon because you cannot rely on it to run as advertised and it is not connected with Lenovo any longer due to it being manufactured a few years ago.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My middle-schoolers do a lot of work at school on Chromebooks through Google Classroom. I wanted to give them a similar experience at home while keeping the cost reasonable and support overhead very low. The Lenovo Chromebook S330 was just the trick. This thing is fast, the screen is clear and bright and the battery life is awesome with an estimated life of 13 hours. Is it really 13 hours? Who knows, but it last through 6 hours of constant and showed a little over half battery remaining, so it seems reasonable.

For perspective, "best" in terms of computer hardware and operating system really comes down to your intended use. You'll get the best value and have the best experience when you buy for that intended use. For what I've described above, this Chromebook is perfect. I could have spent a lot more on a high-performance gaming rig or something with a touchscreen and all the extras, but that's not what was needed.

We haven't had it very long, so I'll post back if any of my initial impressions and observations change.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I ordered up 14 of these units (a couple different orders) and started installing them in client locations. Within a week, we started getting calls about the units trying to boot from PXE or saying "Operating System not found." Thought it was a fluke at first but eventually determined that this company has their own white-labeled M.2/PCIe SSDs and this series of Optiplex 7010s do NOT like them. In the end, we ended up having to replace the half dozen or so units we couldn't really swap out with new, brand-name SSDs to resolve the problem.

We did manage to return 7 of them, but I had to go buy big boxes as we'd already tossed the ones they were delivered in. Then we had to hound Amazon for several days to get the seller to actually refund the money (several days in, two of them had been refunded, but Amazon's site just kept saying "Refund in process" and they'd refund the money once they all were received). After a few pokes at Amazon, we did get our money back, but man did this cost me a lot of man hours having to rebuild failed/incompatible SSDs on the fly.

I don't know what's wrong with their white-labeled SSDs, but they must be incredibly cheap (and modern Optiplex units only really like NVMe models that can run in native RAID mode).

For the record, I did go to their web site and it looks like it was done in Microsoft Word. I managed to get a request out explaining my situation but only got a "please create a ticket" response.

I'd used OEMGENUINE in the past with good results, but wow was this a disaster. Do NOT buy these units unless you intend to put a quality SSD in it!!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pretty good laptop. Will make a really good school or low level gaming laptop compared to latest games.
It came with a 128gb 800mbps m.2 drive that was slow for windows 11 so upgraded it to 1tb 3500mbps m.2 drive. There are mixed reviews and info even from the manufacturer on if it has a extra ram slot or not but this one does not have one. All the ram is soldered to the motherboard and needs to be taken to an Acer shop in order to upgrade. Out of the box it used 6/8gb of ram at first then after the updates it dropped down to 4/8gb used. The system is pretty fast for only having 4gb free. The processor is the main feature I ordered it for since it is a 4core-8thread processor with speed ranging from 2.5ghz to 4.3ghz. After trying some more power demanding games the temp could still not pass 50c and stays quiet and cool to touch. It normally stays idle around 41c when not under a heavy load with no sound from the fans. The screen is decent quality but not meant for games since it's LCD and not being led the games get a bit of blur here and there with higher fps. Word of advice is when installing a different operating system the WiFi drivers do not reinstall with the system so any online activation is almost useless unless you have a usb-ethernet adapter. The battery lasts me around 6 hours in performance mode but in power saving mode could possibly last 9+ hours and way longer with some power setting tweaks. The graphics says 600mb dedicated and 3400mb shared but unlike a lot of systems all the shared moves straight to dedicated making it 4gb for the graphics. The value is pretty good and the appearance is slick. My older brother was checking it out and thinking of buying one now because of how well it does. Some upgrades to look into if you know what your doing is a new m.2 drive with a faster transfer rate and also possibly an upgraded 15.6inch screen that's 1080p-4k.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The "Used - Good Condition" purchase option was a real winner for me. It arrived flawless. No scratches. No scuffs. No marks whatsoever. Came in a factory Lenovo box with all the normal packaging and factory power supply.

It's very lightweight. The screen is fantastic. The touchscreen works. It *does* have a backlight keyboard (FN-Spacebar to toggle on/off).

Mine has Windows 11 Home in it in S-Mode. In the box are instructions to get it into normal Windows mode.

After initial setup and the million Windows updates to install, I used the Lenovo assistant app to update the system bios. For whatever reason, bios update aren't available through the normal Windows Update mechanism.

All that works

I debloated all the telemetry and such (search the Internet for Debloat Windows 11 and use the first GitHub link and PowerShell). Then I uninstalled all the preinstalled apps like Instagram and Spotify and The XBox Bar, etc.

Then I shrunk the windows partition to make room to install Linux. I use Fedora, but any modern Linux should work. No surprises. Hardware drivers were all in the default repos. (The machine has an Intel WiFi 6 card and Realtek audio.)

It's a great inexpensive machine with a 1080p touchscreen display and backlight keyboard, especially at the "Used - Good Condition" price.

HOWEVER, it has only 12GB RAM and *cannot be upgraded* (according to Lenovo's website). 4GB is soldered to the board. 8GB is in a traditional laptop DIMM slot (according to disassembly videos on YT). There is only a single slot. I don't know why it can't support a larger DIMM - I haven't tried to put a larger one in there.

There is a setting in the bios to make them function keys work normally (out of the box you need to press FN-F1 to get F1, etc. Otherwise you get the multimedia shortcut (volume mute in this example).

To boot from a USB, hold F12 when booting and select your USB device from the text menu. To enter the bios, press F2 (or possibly DEL) when booting.

I'm replacing a heavy, 9yr-old, flakey 17" HP, 900p. So I'm thrilled with how much lighter, cooler, and quieter this Lenovo is.

Plus, it runs Linux without a hassle. No driver issues. Trackpad, WiFi, BT, and touchscreen all "just work™".

text: The laptop itself, from an electronics standpoint, is fantastic. However, the engineering, particularly the hinge, is terrible. This was mainly used in bed at night or in the morning, what I would consider light use. Well, in less than 3 months, the hinge broke on one side while opening the laptop. No forceful movements, no jarring, just normal opening of the unit. I even took it to an authorized repair center and it was denied a warranty claim. The cost of repair was 90% the cost of the laptop. I have tried a couple times to repair it myself with no success. I'm sure it can be done, I just don't have the tools or knowledge to do it properly. I do know one thing, though, the design of the hinge is awful. I'm not an engineer, but even I can tell it was under-engineered based on the design and how much stress it receives. It was designed to fail and they will not honor a warranty claim on it. I would recommend finding another laptop other than this one and definitely pay attention to the design of the hinge.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Like all the refurbished stuff, what I get from "supplier A" may not be what you get from "supplier B". That's just how this works. If you go over to the little pull down, you can see a number of folks who all are happy to sell you one of these.

What I happened to get this time was: No SSD bracket, and no DVD. I did get a keyboard, mouse, power cord, built in WiFi, the specified RAM and NVME drive. It also has a pair of serial ports and a VGA. Unlike a few others mine came with the CPU that shows up in the listing. The photo's on the listing are stock photos from who knows where. The certainly did not show what mine look like. Other than the missing SSD bracket, the rest of the "what did I get" really does not matter for my use case. There is "another place" you can go and get them pretty darn cheap ....

Everything functions as it should. It booted fine to Windows 10. That went away as soon as I had a chance to fiddle the BIOS and load Linux.

Mine happened to come with two 8 GB RAM sticks to make up the 16 GB needed. Might another one come with four 4GB? I have no idea. The "two stick" option makes adding more RAM a bit easier. Oddly enough the BIOS showed the installed ram running as 2666MHz rather than 2400MHz. I guess I got lucky. The NVME in mine is a stock Lenovo part. Is it new or has it lived there forever? There's no way to tell. BIOS was last updated in 2024.

Mechanically everything looks fine. No major scratches or dents. Nothing busted or caved in. It would look fine if you wanted to put it on a desktop. This is not a super duper modern CPU and 16 GB is not a lot of RAM. That will impact how it will do running Windows vs something a bit newer.

For the price, I'm quite happy with what I got. Right now this one is the "low cost leader" of the M920s refurbs. That's true here on Amazon and on "that other place".

Nothing's ever perfect, and these Lenovo tablets fall right into that middle ground.

I picked up two 11-inch models (4GB RAM) and one 12.1-inch (8GB RAM), and across the board they've been steady. No standout "wow" moments, but also no real issues to complain about. They just work - which, honestly, counts for a lot.

I'm probably not a typical user. I use them in the field for photography work, sometimes as lightweight monitors, and mainly to avoid dragging a laptop everywhere. In that role, they've been practical and reliable. Battery life is decent, performance is fine for what they are, and they handle everyday tasks without fuss.

I've also experimented a bit - running a full Linux setup on one, keeping the others on Windows - and they've handled that flexibility better than expected. Nothing cutting-edge, but no resistance either.

If you're expecting premium performance or something that feels exceptional, this isn't that. But if you want a functional, adaptable tablet that does its job without getting in the way, they're hard to fault.

At the end of the day, it's subjective. For my use, they've been solid tools. Not perfect, not exciting - just dependable.

They also told me that if they serviced it, (which was questionable, since it had been altered after Lenovo sold it) they would only return it to the original RAM and storage specs (8Gb RAM, 256Gb storage) which are far less than what I purchased, which was unacceptable.
Amazon said my only recourse was with the "seller" ironically named "OEM Genuine". OEM Genuine, after my initial inquiry, refused to answer my questions about possible repairs and has since refused to communicate with me at all.
I thought I was buying a genuine Lenovo computer that would have the advertised specs, but got a used and altered computer that the Lenovo warranty has almost run out on and is now non-functional and these 3 companies all point the finger at the others and nobody will take responsibility and refund my money.
This seems to me to be blatant consumer fraud. The product description is false- Lenovo doesn't even make this model computer with the listed specs, and what was sold was used, not new, with a mostly expired warranty. I seldom write reviews, but had to leave one for this item.
I've bought 4 other refurbished Lenovo desktops and laptops over the years from other sources, and have found it to be a reliable brand (as have many surveys).
I was actually a bit reluctant to purchase this PC, because of the low price, but couldn't be happier with the result....
The PC was delivered 2 days after I ordered it, in a very well-packaged shipping box.
I opened the case and inspected the motherboard, etc, and could not find any trace of dust/dirt, even on the cooling fan fins... it looked in pristine condition.
All extra items were included, and the computer performs wonderfully (and includes a 1 yr warranty!). I purchased this for my dad, since his old PC's hardware did not support Windows 11 (Windows 10 will no longer have (free) security updates starting Oct '25).
The only 2 minor inconveniences I experienced was...
1. The included keyboard is very cheap, and the tiny left shift key makes it basically unusable for me, but I didn't expect the keyboard to be included, so this no issue to me, as the old keyboard works just fine.
2. The instructions recommend setting up the included copy of Windows 11 without a Microsoft account (which I definitely concur with), but this could not be accomplished without the OOBE\BYPASSNRO command and a reboot (google it to see the procedure), so those instructions should be updated.

I've been both buying and building PCs since the early '90s, and overall, I couldn't be happier with this purchase, and will definitely consider MaxE Computers for future refurb purchases.

text:
The screen on my Samsung Galaxy Tab s6 lite has been having fits lately, requiring multiple attempts to communicate with the device regardless whether not I'm using the pen or a traditional stylus. Annoying. I'm not the gamer my wife is so I didn't require the same kind juice she requires. The Lenovo M11 is essentially in the same range power-wise as the S6 Lite.
The tablet feels nice in the hand without the slipperiness. The included case is handy and nice not having to buy a separate case. The case holds the pen. There's the standard USB C connector for charging and data transfer.
Setup and transferring stuff from the S6 to this tablet was breeze (for change). Up and running in less than hour. The most difficult part was having to enter my router password (it's ugly and 56 characters, nice when I get it the first time). FRReader and Nova Prime both were configured using the settings from the S6. Other apps as well. I would rather have had at least WiFi 6 but 'n' will be fine. The screen is definitely more responsive with or without the pen. It is brighter than the S6 as well when the brightness level is set the same between the 2 devices.
The tablet received updates to Android 15. There are a few 'extras' that were installed. They were uninstallable, surprisingly. One thing I really like is being able to turn auto-rotate OFF and leave it off. Lenovo (or may Android 15) supplies an icon that pops up in the lower left that can be tapped to rotate the screen for that instance of the app. Split screen mode is implemented nicely on this tablet.
Mostly used for lite web browsing and low impact games such as Wordaily and sudoko. Primary usage is a an e-book reader using FBReader Prime or Moon+ Reader.
For $130 this is an impressive table for my usage. I'd buy it again. I'm really starting to like Lenovo products.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
[This review is for a refurbished M720S 16GB / 512GB SSD]

Measured at about 3.5" x 10.5" x 13.5" the M720S is a nice little compact desktop. It is sturdy built and Includes 8 USB ports, microphone and headset port, and 2 DVI (display ports). Of course the downside of such size is the limited ability of upgrades, however the M720S can easily host an extra drive and 3 extra PCI cards (including a graphic card) as long as they are low profile (2.5" high). The one I got also has a laptop style DVD drive. I would give this computer 4/5 due to limited overall performance.

Now if you decided to buy this machine the 2nd question is, should I buy it here on Amazon? And here it is questionable. The machine is refurbished, you don't get to see the actual machine you will be getting, so they make you feel like you will get a like-new machine, but mine had some scratches on it and the packaging was very minimal and it sat in Styrofoam which broke and pieces of it were embedded in the computer grill and had to be manually cleaned. There was not even a "fragile" or a "this side up" sticker on the box. I can see how this can easily be a DOA due to shipping.

Moreover, the packaging was missing the DVI to HDMI plug which makes it impossible to connect to any modern screen. I had to contact Amazon to get a replacement and they sent me a new cable for free. I decided to buy from Amazon, which is more expensive than other outlets, because I thought it would be hassle-free and the box will be new, however it was not the case.

Remember that this machine can be found in many different configurations, as far as CPU architecture and speed, memory size, and drive size. It looks the same from the outside, but you are paying for what's inside. In any event never get a machine that cannot be upgraded to Win 11, that would substantially limit the lifetime on it.

A word about software- the machine comes with a brand new Win 11 install, it has no issue and does not come with any bloatware or adware that I could see. The WiFi / BT plugin works well. If you intend to use this machine for gaming, be prepared to add a $100 graphics card to make this machine viable for gaming, otherwise it is a nice home-office machine.

Summary:
Pros:
1. Nice form factor
2. Relatively cheap i7 CPU
3. Win 11 software / no bloatware
4. Reliable manufacturer / return policy
5. DVD drive, lots of SSD space
6. Easy to upgrade

Cons:
1. It is not 'like new' shape
2. Bad packaging - missing add-ons
3. On-board GPU is not good enough for gaming and has DVI out only
4. Needs plug for WiFi / BT (supplied as extra in box)

Overall 3.5 / 5, I rounded it up to 4 since at the end I am happy with the purchase, but really the packaging here should be better. Hope this was helpful for you to make a decision.

text: I received this tablet on sep 28th of 2025. I have been using it everyday for about a week now. Honestly it has exceeded my expatiations. I trust Lenovo with their products so i was never worried that i would not receive the product that was advertised as a gaming tablet. I was a bit worried that the screen would not be large enough to please me. but honestly it's a perfect size in my opinion, it's not to large and not to small. it's a good in the middle screen size. The Tablet Does Come With A Case And A Screen Protector. It also comes with the charger brick and cable. it also include instructions if needed. I absolutely LOVE the case. the look of it is really nice with the word legion written on the back side of the case. the case also allows for air to pass through it since the case has what i guess you could call vent like holes in it. The speed of the tablet has been great, it's defiantly faster than an average tablet. It loads up quickly when powered on or woken up from sleep mode. I have played many different games on this tablet ranging from mobile games to more intense game like dredge or league of legends ect. The only game that i have played on the tablet where it did not have the best frame rate would be the game called DYSMANTLE, However i can not be 100% sure if it's due to the game not being fully optimized via the mobile version or if it is the tablet struggling. it's still playable just not as smooth as it would be if i could get 60fps. instead i seem to fluctuate between 30-20fps. and it does have a bit of a lag to it. But that is the only game i have issues with. As for the tablets ability to cool it self it has done pretty well for what i have played on it. the hottest it has gotten for me was like 38c. but it normally stays in the 25c or 28c range. But i have found a solution to cool the tablet down quickly if i am doing longer game sessions, I just turn on a fan and sit near it while i play on the tablet. it helps keep a cool air flow on it so it doesn't heat up as quickly. You can also buy fan cooler accessories for it. usually any mobile cooling magnetic fan will work for both phones and tablets. you literally just attach it to the back of the tablet/phone. Overall this tablet has been amazing. the picture quality is also very clear and crisp. Defiantly worth the price. Oh if you are wondering this tablet does support a stylus. i ended up buying the Lenovo Tab Pen Plus, apparently this is the only stylus that will work with this tablet via what i read online. it also will support a wireless Bluetooth keyboard. You can even use a PS5 controller with the tablet or buy the Legion G9 Gamepad for it. although i have not found a trust worthy place to buy it from. Honestly the only down side to this tablet is that it can be a bit difficult to find some accessories for it through a trusted seller. example the gamepad.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Looks great, sounds pretty good, nice battery life, but it's not quite what I expected.

Setup right out of the box is nothing but update after update. It probably took me about 2 hours before I could fully use it between the tablet updating from Pie to Q, the dock itself updating, and all of Google's apps... Took a while but worked out.

This is a beautiful display. Shame about that Widevine DRM, though. No HD Disney+, Netflix, or Vudu here. No sir/ma'am. BUT... HBOMax, Prime Video, Movies Anywhere, Google TV/Play Movies & TV, and YouTube (if your digital collection is connected to Movies Anywhere) will all play in 1080p without a hitch. In fact, it'll jump to 1080p in seconds, with little to no buffering.

Overall speed of the tablet is silky smooth. I recommend turning on Developer Options and disabling animations. (You honestly don't need them on any Android device, they're just a needless pretty thing that eats up performance.)

The dock is impressive in its feature set, even if the sound is just okay. It's a Bluetooth speaker, it's a speakerphone, it's a charging cradle/Alexa Show display, and it does all of these things well. There are two, not four (some listings will say this incorrectly) 3w speakers in it. The rest of the body is housing for the logic board and the hollowness (doesn't feel that way) gives it a passive radiator-like feel to the sound. (It's room-filling sound, btw.)

This brings us back to the sound (overall) and I have to say it's...okay. Either in the dock (which sounds leaps and bounds better than the tablet speakers, of course.) or the speakers in the tablet, even with Dolby Atmos baked in (controllable via app). I will say the sound separation on the tablet is much better than that of the dock. If nothing else, you'll at least get a basic Atmos experience out of it. (It's better than no Atmos at all!) You can't use all four speakers at once, unfortunately. Believe me, I tried. lol

I'd say the specs are on par with Amazon's own Fire HD tablets, and the only thing they're really missing is the Lenovo dock. (I mean, they have Atmos baked in, a gorgeous screen, dual speakers (for channel separation), and they have proper Widevine DRM which makes a world of difference on a screen this size and quality. Although, this has one thing the Fire doesn't (aside from the dock) ...the full Dolby Atmos version of Amazon Music Unlimited in the app. The Fire has a custom version installed like bloatware that only offers Ultra HD and 3D and not all the time. (And yes, there's an audible difference.)

Do I recommend this? Well, if you're into Alexa, want a lovely dock/Show Mode device, and are okay with jumping through hoops to get your videos in 1080p, with okay Atmos, then yes. If you're willing to skip the dock and you're fine with Ultra HD/3D instead of Atmos, then you should save the money and go wth the Fire HD 10 Plus. (Yes, it's absolutely worth the extra money with 4GB of RAM in it.)

I think this tablet had a lot of promise, I think the Widevine issue was a bad case of dropping the ball just before the goal. So close, yet so far. Still...a very nice Lenovo tablet, pretty all the way around.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Looks great, sounds pretty good, nice battery life, but it's not quite what I expected.

Setup right out of the box is nothing but update after update. It probably took me about 2 hours before I could fully use it between the tablet updating from Pie to Q, the dock itself updating, and all of Google's apps... Took a while but worked out.

This is a beautiful display. Shame about that Widevine DRM, though. No HD Disney+, Netflix, or Vudu here. No sir/ma'am. BUT... HBOMax, Prime Video, Movies Anywhere, Google TV/Play Movies & TV, and YouTube (if your digital collection is connected to Movies Anywhere) will all play in 1080p without a hitch. In fact, it'll jump to 1080p in seconds, with little to no buffering.

Overall speed of the tablet is silky smooth. I recommend turning on Developer Options and disabling animations. (You honestly don't need them on any Android device, they're just a needless pretty thing that eats up performance.)

The dock is impressive in its feature set, even if the sound is just okay. It's a Bluetooth speaker, it's a speakerphone, it's a charging cradle/Alexa Show display, and it does all of these things well. There are two, not four (some listings will say this incorrectly) 3w speakers in it. The rest of the body is housing for the logic board and the hollowness (doesn't feel that way) gives it a passive radiator-like feel to the sound. (It's room-filling sound, btw.)

This brings us back to the sound (overall) and I have to say it's...okay. Either in the dock (which sounds leaps and bounds better than the tablet speakers, of course.) or the speakers in the tablet, even with Dolby Atmos baked in (controllable via app). I will say the sound separation on the tablet is much better than that of the dock. If nothing else, you'll at least get a basic Atmos experience out of it. (It's better than no Atmos at all!) You can't use all four speakers at once, unfortunately. Believe me, I tried. lol

I'd say the specs are on par with Amazon's own Fire HD tablets, and the only thing they're really missing is the Lenovo dock. (I mean, they have Atmos baked in, a gorgeous screen, dual speakers (for channel separation), and they have proper Widevine DRM which makes a world of difference on a screen this size and quality. Although, this has one thing the Fire doesn't (aside from the dock) ...the full Dolby Atmos version of Amazon Music Unlimited in the app. The Fire has a custom version installed like bloatware that only offers Ultra HD and 3D and not all the time. (And yes, there's an audible difference.)

Do I recommend this? Well, if you're into Alexa, want a lovely dock/Show Mode device, and are okay with jumping through hoops to get your videos in 1080p, with okay Atmos, then yes. If you're willing to skip the dock and you're fine with Ultra HD/3D instead of Atmos, then you should save the money and go wth the Fire HD 10 Plus. (Yes, it's absolutely worth the extra money with 4GB of RAM in it.)

I think this tablet had a lot of promise, I think the Widevine issue was a bad case of dropping the ball just before the goal. So close, yet so far. Still...a very nice Lenovo tablet, pretty all the way around.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Years ago I had a very expensive MacBook Pro that eventually baked itself to death due to grossly inadequate CPU cooling (no fans, just vents thru the keyboard). I vowed, “never again! Henceforth my laptop shall always feature powerful fans!”

Careful what you wish for. While the ROG G750JZ I owned immediately after the MacBook was perfect, cooling-wise, with powerful but not deafening fans, my new Strix G16’s fans are way, way too loud.

If you don’t live with other people or otherwise do your gaming (and other fan-triggering computations) in isolation, then put on good noise-isolating headphones and don’t worry about it. But, if you do game in mixed company as I generally do, be advised: this machine will irritate others when those fans kick in.

That’s the bad news, bad enough to dock a star. The good news is, I love almost everything else about this machine. The display is simply gorgeous. Performance is crazy-good. It’s a compact and medium-weight machine (unlike my beloved G750 which was, admittedly, a boat-anchor).

And, the Strix G16’s “tool-free upgrade” feature makes it super easy to swap out RAM and SSDs: just unlatch and slide off the bottom case cover and there they are. One caveat, though: the instruction manual recommends first disconnecting the battery, which requires you to essentially field-strip the machine using a screwdriver (!!) before adding or removing RAM or SSD’s — clearly there were competing visions between engineering teams at play at Asus. But, people, including me, seem to be ignoring this advice without mishap!

The only other negative for me with the G16 besides noise is the touchpad, which supposedly doubles as a numeric keypad. Personally I detest touchpads, because I always, always, always accidentally bump or brush them with my wrists when typing, causing the cursor to jump around. So, on any laptop I use, this is always the first thing I disable. With the G16, that means losing the numeric keypad, because the physical keyboard lacks one. This is a baffling design choice for a gaming laptop — historically, the numeric keypad has been an important game control in some titles.

And yet, this hasn’t been an issue for me so far when playing Disco Elysium, Baldur’s Gate 3, and other recent games — maybe game designers nowadays depend on these less —so for now at least this is just a quibble. If I ever do need a physical numeric keypad, USB & bluetooth keyboards are cheap enough.

In summary, I find my 2025 Strix G16 to be a powerful, compact, and beautiful-graphics-delivering laptop. I just try not to use it around other people when I’m doing anything that turns those loud fans on.
